info.description: Merged from the per-resource OpenAPI documents Procore publishes through its developer portal (https://developers.procore.com/api/v1/resource_groups). Originals are kept verbatim in openapi/_original/resources/.

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.description:
Returns all Accident Logs for the current date.

See [Working with Daily Logs](https://developers.procore.com/documentation/daily-logs) for information on filtering the response using the log\_date, start\_date, and end\_date parameters. Note that if none of the date parameters are provided in the call, only logs from the current date are returned.

parameters.name: log_date
parameters.description: Date of specific logs desired in YYYY-MM-DD format

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Start date of specific logs desired in YYYY-MM-DD format (use together with end_date)

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: End date of specific logs desired in YYYY-MM-DD format (use together with start_date)

parameters.name: filters[created_by_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) created by the specified User ID

parameters.name: filters[location_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified Location IDs.

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

get.description:
Returns all Action Plan Items for a given Project.

**Deprecated.** Use the v2 Action Plan Items list endpoint (`GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/action_plans/plan_items`) instead.

For backwards compatibility, requests from Procore mobile clients (identified by a `Procore-OSName` header of `iOS` or `android`) have any company-custom item status downgraded to the built-in Procore status it maps to (`status` enum: `open`, `in_progress`, `delayed`, `closed`). For those clients the returned `status` object and `status_id` always reference one of the four built-in statuses (ids 1-4), never a company-custom status. All other clients receive the untouched status, including any company-custom status. Clients that need the full company-custom status must use the v2 endpoint.

import http.client

post.description:
Create an Action Plan Test Record

Action Plan Test Records can have one of the following payload formats (checklist_id, form_id, generic_tool_id, meeting_id, submittal_log_id, observation_item_id, attachment)
Attachment payloads must be a binary file or contain an attachment_id, upload_id, drawing_revision_id, file_version_id, form_id, or image_id.

A specific Action Plan Test Record Type can only leverage its corresponding format.

*For instance, Checklist Test Records can only leverage checklist_id while Attachment/Photo Test Records can only leverage attachment.

parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) that have any of the specified Party IDs as an Action Plan Approver.

parameters.name: filters[custom_fields]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) whose custom field values match the supplied JSON object. Each key must be a custom field definition ID. A scalar value matches Action Plan(s) whose value for that field is equal to it; an array value matches Action Plan(s) whose value for that field is any one of the supplied values. Supplying more than one key returns only the Action Plan(s) that match every key. Custom fields are configured per Action Plan Type, so an Action Plan whose type does not configure the supplied field never matches.

schema.description: JSON object where each key is a custom field definition ID

parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) with the specified Action Plan number(s). A range such as `10...20` is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[receiver_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) that have any of the specified Party IDs as an Action Plan Receiver. Matches every Receiver regardless of whether they have signed.

parameters.name: filters[plan_type_id]
parameters.description: Action Plan Type ID. Returns item(s) with the specified Action Plan Type ID(s).

parameters.name: filters[company_template_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) whose resolved company-level Action Plan Template matches the specified ID(s). A project template resolves through its `company_template_id`; a company template matches itself. Pass `null` (or `nil`) to match plans with no resolved company template.

parameters.name: filters[project_template_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) whose template is a project-level Action Plan Template with the specified ID(s). Pass `null` (or `nil`) to match plans with no project template, including plans created from a company template directly. Distinct from `filters[template_id]`, which matches `itp_plans.template_id` regardless of company vs project scope.

parameters.name: filters[template_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) associated with the specified Action Plan Template ID(s).

parameters.name: filters[root_template_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) whose template lineage root matches the specified ID(s). A project-level copy of a company template resolves to that company template; a company template and a project template with no company lineage each resolve to their own ID. Soft-deleted templates still resolve a root. Pass `null` (or `nil`) to match plans with no template. Distinct from `filters[company_template_id]`, which is the group-by facet: that one excludes soft-deleted templates and places plans with no company lineage in the unassigned bucket rather than under their own ID. Cell `template_id` values returned by the Portfolio `with_action_plans` view use this same roll-up and can be passed straight through.

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Direction (asc/desc) can be controlled by the presence or absence of '-' before the sort parameter.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
Controls which fields are included in the response.

- `list` — Slim view for the plans index table. Returns only the fields
  rendered by the list UI: id, number, title, private, closed_item_count,
  total_item_count, status, custom_fields, plan_type, plan_status, location,
  and manager (name only). Omits plan_approvers, plan_receivers, assets, and
  template_id. Significantly reduces DB queries and payload size.


- `normal` (default) — Full view including plan_approvers, plan_receivers,
  assets, template_id, and the complete manager party object.


- `full` — Extends normal with plan_sections.

- `ids` — Returns only plan IDs as a flat array.

x-changelog.summary: Added filters[root_template_id] to the Action Plans list
x-changelog.description:
`GET /projects/{project_id}/action_plans/plans` now accepts
`filters[root_template_id]`, matching plans whose template lineage root
is one of the given ids. A project-level copy of a company template
resolves to that company template; a company template and a project
template with no company lineage each resolve to their own id.
Soft-deleted templates still resolve a root. Pass `null` (or `nil`) to
match plans with no template.

x-changelog.summary: Added project and company template filters on the Action Plans list
x-changelog.description: `filters[project_template_id]` and `filters[company_template_id]` match plans by project-level template or resolved company-level template. Values may be arrays of IDs; `null` / `nil` match plans with no project template or no resolved company template. Distinct from `filters[template_id]`, which matches `itp_plans.template_id` directly.

x-changelog.summary: Added view=list parameter to Action Plans index endpoint
x-changelog.description:
The GET /projects/{project_id}/action_plans/plans endpoint now accepts a
`view=list` query parameter that returns a slim response optimized for
list table rendering. The list view includes only the fields needed by
the plans table (id, number, title, private, item counts, plan type,
status, location, and manager name), omitting plan_approvers,
plan_receivers, assets, and template_id. This reduces database queries
and payload size significantly. The default behavior (no view param or
view=normal) is unchanged.

x-changelog.description: Both columns hold multiple people, so each sorts on the alphabetically first party name shown in the cell. Plans with no approvers, or no receivers, are returned last in both directions.

x-changelog.summary: Added filters for number, private, custom_fields, approver_id, and receiver_id on the Action Plans list endpoint
x-changelog.description: Five new filters on the Action Plans list endpoint. `filters[number]` and `filters[private]` match the corresponding Action Plan attributes. `filters[custom_fields]` takes a JSON object keyed by custom field definition ID and matches Action Plan(s) whose value for every supplied field equals the supplied value, or is any one of them when an array is given. `filters[approver_id]` and `filters[receiver_id]` match Action Plan(s) having any of the supplied Party IDs as an Approver or a Receiver respectively.

parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) that have any of the specified Party IDs as an Action Plan Approver.

parameters.name: filters[custom_fields]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) whose custom field values match the supplied JSON object. Each key must be a custom field definition ID. A scalar value matches Action Plan(s) whose value for that field is equal to it; an array value matches Action Plan(s) whose value for that field is any one of the supplied values. Supplying more than one key returns only the Action Plan(s) that match every key. Custom fields are configured per Action Plan Type, so an Action Plan whose type does not configure the supplied field never matches.

schema.description: JSON object where each key is a custom field definition ID

parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) with the specified Action Plan number(s). A range such as `10...20` is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[receiver_id]

parameters.name: filters[company_template_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) whose resolved company-level Action Plan Template matches the specified ID(s). A project template resolves through its `company_template_id`; a company template matches itself. Pass `null` (or `nil`) to match plans with no resolved company template.

parameters.name: filters[project_template_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) whose template is a project-level Action Plan Template with the specified ID(s). Pass `null` (or `nil`) to match plans with no project template, including plans created from a company template directly. Distinct from `filters[template_id]`, which matches `itp_plans.template_id` regardless of company vs project scope.

parameters.name: filters[template_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) associated with the specified Action Plan Template ID(s).

parameters.name: filters[root_template_id]
parameters.description: Return Action Plan(s) whose template lineage root matches the specified ID(s). A project-level copy of a company template resolves to that company template; a company template and a project template with no company lineage each resolve to their own ID. Soft-deleted templates still resolve a root. Pass `null` (or `nil`) to match plans with no template. Distinct from `filters[company_template_id]`, which is the group-by facet: that one excludes soft-deleted templates and places plans with no company lineage in the unassigned bucket rather than under their own ID. Cell `template_id` values returned by the Portfolio `with_action_plans` view use this same roll-up and can be passed straight through.

post.summary: Bulk Create Action Plans for Locations
post.description:
Creates multiple Action Plans from a single Action Plan Template at a specified location. The endpoint enqueues background jobs to create the specified number of Action Plans asynchronously.

The template must be in "published" status. Templates in "draft" or "in_revision" status cannot be used to create plans.

Each Action Plan will be created with all sections, items, assignees, references, and test record requests copied from the template.

post.summary: Bulk Create Action Plans for Assets
post.description:
Creates one Action Plan per asset from a single Action Plan Template. Each created plan is automatically linked to its corresponding asset via the Related Items framework.

The endpoint is asynchronous: it returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id` and enqueues background jobs that create the plans and links in batches of 200. Clients poll the existing async-operations endpoint at `GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/submittals/async_operations/{operation_id}` for live progress and a per-asset success / failure breakdown.

Pre-flight validation rejects requests synchronously with `422` when any `asset_ids` entry does not belong to the project (deleted, cross-tenant, or typo'd) — those requests never persist an `Operations::Operation` row or fan out background workers.

Requires the Assets project tool to be active on the project. The selected template must be published and its plan type's configurable field set must have the `assets` field visible for this project; otherwise the request is rejected with `422`.

Each Action Plan is created with all sections, items, assignees, references, and test record requests copied from the template — identical to the per-plan create flow.

asset_ids.description: Asset IDs to create plans for. One Action Plan is created per unique asset id; duplicate ids in the array are deduped before fan-out. Up to 1,000 assets per request.

count.description: The number of Action Plans that will be created (equals the count of unique, non-blank `asset_ids` after server-side dedupe).

get.summary: Get Advanced Forecasting Rows of a Project
get.description: Get Advanced forecasting rows. Each page will have a maximum of 100 items.

parameters.name: budget_view_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the Budget View (also known as Budget Template). Required to return spread amount for other curves besides manual. Also required when column-based forecasting is enabled.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
Array structure to filter the result of the advanced forecasting endpoint
Supported filter objects (with and without budget_view_id):
  - WBS segment item filter
    Structure:
      - id: <segment_id>
      - tier: <segment_tier>
      - type: 'segment'
      - values: <array of segment item ids>
  
    Example:
    `{"id": "23", tier: <segment_tier>, "type": "segment", "values": [2]}`

    URL example:
    https://app.procore.com/rest/v2.0/companies/<company_id>/projects/<project_id>/advanced_forecastings/rows?filters[][id]=23&filters[][tier]=1&filters[][type]=segment&filters[][values][]=2&page=1&per_page=100&budget_view_id=2

Supported filters only if budget_view_id is provided:
  - Actuals by date
    Structure:
      - id: 'date_range_for_actuals'
      - code: 'date_range_for_actuals'
      - type: 'date_range_for_actuals'
      - values: [`<start_date>(YYYY-MM-DD)`, `<end_date>(YYYY-MM-DD)`, `<include_actuals_without_dates (boolean)>`].
    
    Example:
    `{"id": "date_range_for_actuals", "code": "date_range_for_actuals", "type": "date_range_for_actuals", "values": ["2021-01-01", "2021-01-31", false]}`

    URL Example:
    https://app.procore.com/rest/v2.0/companies/<company_id>/projects/<project_id>/advanced_forecastings/rows?filters[][code]=date_range_for_actuals&filters[][id]=date_range_for_actuals&filters[][type]=date_range_for_actuals&filters[][values][]=2021-01-01&filters[][values][]=2021-01-31&filters[][values][]=false&page=1&per_page=100&budget_view_id=2

id.description: Identifier of the thing being filtered on. For a segment filter this is the WBS segment id; for a date-range-for-actuals filter it is the literal 'date_range_for_actuals'.

code.description: Filter code. Required for the date-range-for-actuals filter (set to 'date_range_for_actuals'); omit for segment filters.

tier.description: Tier of the Segment if applicable

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

data.description: Array of Advanced forecasting summarized rows

items.description: Advanced forecasting Row Summarized

budget_line_item_id.description: Identifier of the budget line item this forecasting row belongs to. Null for rows that do not yet have a persisted budget line item.

wbs_code_id.description: Identifier of the WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) code that scopes this forecasting row. Uniquely identifies the budget cost code combination being forecast.

start_date.description: First day the forecast applies to, in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Together with end_date it defines the span over which periods are distributed.

get.description: Returns all of the Resource Planning Assignment data for the given company

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description:
Unique identifier for the company. This parameter accepts both formats:
- **Recommended**: Procore company ID (integer) - Use this for new integrations
- Legacy: LaborChart UUID format (uuid string) - Supported for backward compatibility

A proxy layer automatically handles both formats, but using the Procore company ID is preferred for consistency with other Procore APIs.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Filters items created on or after the specified date (inclusive). Accepts an ISO 8601 date string.

parameters.name: created_at
parameters.description: Filters items based on their creation timestamp. Accepts an ISO 8601 date string.

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Filters items created on or before the specified date (inclusive). Accepts an ISO 8601 date string.

parameters.name: dayRange
parameters.description:
A value specifying how many days forward you would like to get assignments for from the specified startDay. Assignments whose start_day falls within the given range will be returned in the response.
The startDay parameter in conjunction with the dayRange parameter will create a range of dates that will filter each assignment based on its start_day field.
For example, passing in a startDay of 2024-01-01 and a dayRange of 1 will return all assignments that begin on either the 1st or 2nd of January.
If we pass in the same startDay, but with a dayRange of 15, the results will include all assignments whose start_day exists between the dates of 2024-01-01 and 2024-01-15.
Max value is 365.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
This is a **0-based index** representing the page slice of the data you want to retrieve. Each page contains up to **400 items**.
### **📌 Pageable Endpoints** People endpoints that return multiple records **support pagination**. It is recommended to use this feature to prevent network timeouts from excessively large data requests.
### **📌 Response Structure** A successful response will include the following properties:
- **`possible_pages`** *(integer)* → Total number of pages available to retrieve all data. - **`current_page`** *(integer)* → The **0-based index** of the page retrieved. - **`data`** *(array)* → List of records returned for the requested page (up to 400 items per page).
If a **page value exceeds** `possible_pages`, the `data` property will return an **empty array**.

parameters.description: Filters items based on their last updated timestamp. Accepts an ISO 8601 date string.

parameters.name: updated_before
parameters.description: Filters items updated on or before the specified date (inclusive). Accepts an ISO 8601 date string.

| `SQ_FT`, `SQ_YD`, `SQUARE`, `CU_FT`, `CU_YD`  | `AREA`, `VERTICAL_AREA`                                  |

post.summary: Create a markup on a proposal
post.description:
Returns 201 with the created markup.
An ITERATIVE markup always compounds all preceding markups; compound_all is set implicitly and
compound_with is not allowed. Only one ITERATIVE markup can exist per proposal, and it must be POST_TAX.
LEGACY_OVERHEAD and LEGACY_DISCOUNT must be PRE_TAX; creating one re-enables and updates the existing
disabled legacy markup when present. Creating a LEGACY_OVERHEAD sets an existing LEGACY_DISCOUNT's
compound_with to the overhead, and vice versa. Only markups from the same stage, except
ITERATIVE, can be referenced in compound_with.

x-changelog.summary: Support for searching by bid form title within the provided bid package
x-changelog.description:
Bid forms can now be searched by title within the context of the bid package referenced by `bid_package_id`.
The `view` parameter must be omitted to narrow the search to the bid package. The search term must be provided
using the `search` parameter. The `excluded_bid_form_id` parameter is optional and if provided will exclude the
bid form with the specified ID from the search results.

x-changelog.summary: Bid Forms index supports recipient counts and documented pagination
x-changelog.description:
The index endpoint now supports an optional `view=with_recipients` query param to include
`count_of_recipients` per bid form. Pagination behavior is documented with `page` and `per_page`
query params and response headers `page`, `per-page`, and `total`. The `search` param filters on
bid form title within the bid package.

x-changelog.summary: Added proposal_id
x-changelog.description:
Added proposal_id to the payload and response of the endpoint to represent the proposal/estimate in the Estimating tool.
This is to support the integration between the Bidding and Estimating tools.

x-changelog.summary: Added layer_id
x-changelog.description:
Added layer_id to the payload and response of bid form items to represent the layer in the Estimating tool.
This is to support the integration between the Bidding and Estimating tools.

x-changelog.summary: Added lock fields for unit and quantity
x-changelog.description:
Added 4 new lock fields to bid forms: lock_unit_fields_base_bid, lock_quantity_fields_base_bid,
lock_unit_fields_alternates, and lock_quantity_fields_alternates. These fields allow solicitors
to lock unit and quantity fields for bidders at the form level. Fields must be sent explicitly
when creating a bid form (no automatic inheritance from bid package). Defaults to false if not provided.

x-changelog.summary: Added locked_quantity and locked_unit_of_measure fields for bid form items
x-changelog.description:
Added locked_quantity and locked_unit_of_measure fields to the payload and response of bid form items.
These fields allow locking quantity and unit of measure values that cannot be changed by bidders.

x-changelog.summary: Added optional content_position field to bid form items and sub sections
x-changelog.description:
Bid form create and bulk-create requests now accept an optional `content_position`
integer on each bid form item and sub section, and it is returned in bid form
responses. The field places items and sub sections in a single unified 1-based
ordering within their parent section. When provided for any child of a section it
must be provided for all of them, and the values must form a unique, gapless
sequence (1, 2, 3, ...). Null when the unified ordering has not been assigned.

x-changelog.summary: Added optional content_position field to bid form items and sub sections
x-changelog.description:
Bid form update requests now accept an optional `content_position` integer on each
bid form item and sub section, and it is returned in bid form responses. The field
places items and sub sections in a single unified 1-based ordering within their
parent section. When provided for any child of a section it must be provided for
all of them, and the merged values (submitted children plus any omitted persisted
siblings) must form a unique, gapless sequence (1, 2, 3, ...) per section.

bid_status.description:
This status is combination of the `invitation_last_sent_at`, `is_bidder_committed`, `submitted`, & `awarded` values.
The `not_invited`  status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` being null,     `is_bidder_committed` being null,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `undecided`    status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being null,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `will_not_bid` status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being false, `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `will_bid`     status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `submitted`    status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being true,  & `awarded` not being true.
The `awarded`      status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being true,  & `awarded` being true.

x-changelog.summary: Added Values Converted Notification Attributes for Planroom
x-changelog.description:
Added two new attributes to the Bid response for planroom_redesign view:
- values_converted_by_name: name of the solicitor who updated the bid values
- values_converted_at: timestamp when the bid values were last updated by a solicitor
These attributes inform bidders when their bid values have been automatically converted
due to a solicitor locking quantity or unit fields on the bid form.

x-changelog.summary: Added Values Modified Attributes for Planroom
x-changelog.description:
Added two new attributes to the Bid response for planroom_redesign view:
- values_modified_by_name: name of the solicitor who last modified the bid values
- values_modified_at: timestamp when the bid values were last modified by a solicitor
These attributes supersede the now-deprecated `values_converted_by_name` and
`values_converted_at` fields and more accurately describe the banner's
semantics, which fires on any solicitor modification to a submitted bid
(including structural bid-form changes), not just value conversions.

bid_status.description:
This status is combination of the `invitation_last_sent_at`, `is_bidder_committed`, `submitted`, & `awarded` values.
The `not_invited`  status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` being null,     `is_bidder_committed` being null,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `undecided`    status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being null,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `will_not_bid` status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being false, `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `will_bid`     status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `submitted`    status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being true,  & `awarded` not being true.
The `awarded`      status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being true,  & `awarded` being true.

bid_status.description:
This status is combination of the `invitation_last_sent_at`, `is_bidder_committed`, `submitted`, & `awarded` values.
The `not_invited`  status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` being null,     `is_bidder_committed` being null,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `undecided`    status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being null,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `will_not_bid` status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being false, `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `will_bid`     status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being false, & `awarded` not being true.
The `submitted`    status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being true,  & `awarded` not being true.
The `awarded`      status is the same as `invitation_last_sent_at` not being null, `is_bidder_committed` being true,  `submitted` being true,  & `awarded` being true.

A BIM File Extraction can fail for several reasons. When it does, the errors attribute contains a list of errors encountered while processing the model. The following table lists the possible error codes and types.

#### Error Types

| Code | Type                   |
|------|------------------------|
| 1    | Undefined              |
| 2    | NetworkErr             |
| 3    | ServerErr              |
| 4    | JsonParseErr           |
| 5    | TokenExpiredErr        |
| 6    | FileOpenErr            |
| 7    | FileWriteErr           |
| 8    | FileCompressionErr     |
| 9    | FileUploadError        |
| 10   | ModelReadErr           |
| 11   | ModelFileSizeErr       |
| 12   | ModelExportErr         |
| 13   | ModelEmptyDBErr        |
| 14   | ModelViewpointErr      |
| 15   | ModelErr               |
| 16   | InvalidStatusError     |
| 17   | FileDecompressionErr   |
| 18   | UnsupportedFileFormat  |
| 19   | No3DGeometry           |
| 20   | InvalidInputError      |
| 21   | UnsupportedFileSource  |
| 22   | MeshNodeLimitError     |

post.description:
Create a Revision for a BIM Model. If a set of upload UUIDs or model artifact references are not provided, the revision will be created with 'unpublished' publish status.


For 3d files converted to Procore's format using BIM File Extractions API, the `geometry_file_id` can be retrieved via [BIM File Extraction API](https://developers.procore.com/reference/rest/v1/bim-file-extractions?version=1.0#show-bim-file-extraction) using the following JSONPath:

    $.extraction_items.artifact.properties.id



Note that in the response for this BIM Model Revision endpoint, `geometry_file_id` will be designated as `published_model.id`, and `property_file_id` will be designated as `object_definition.id`.

get.summary: Get Detail Rows for a Project's Budget
get.description:
Get detail rows for a project's budget view.
To restrict or reorder which columns are returned, pass `column_ids` with the desired column `id` values, in the desired order. A column's `id` (used for `column_ids`) is different from its `attribute` (the key used for that column's value in each row below) — see [Get a Budget View](https://developers.procore.com/reference/rest/budget-view?version=latest) for the `columns` array, which has both plus display metadata (`label`, `type`, `format`, `display_rules`).
To read rows from a snapshot instead of the live budget, pass `source_snapshot_id` — this query parameter is shared across this endpoint, Summary Rows, and the Budget View endpoint.
For forecasting views, spread columns will be included for budget line items where appropriate. Spread columns represent monthly forecast amounts and are named using the pattern "spread_{month}_{year}" (e.g., "spread_may_2010", "spread_june_2010").
This endpoint is paginated with `page`/`per_page` (maximum 100); requests with a larger `per_page` return 400. Page through results with `page`, and read `Total`, `Per-Page`, and `Link` from the response headers.

Note:
In addition to all the fields outlined in the response example, there will be an additional key for each visible,

x-changelog.summary: Introducing v1.0 Sync Budget Line Items endpoint
x-changelog.description:
The Sync Budget Line Items endpoint is a new endpoint that allows developers to create and update Budget Line Items in bulk.

x-changelog.summary: Introducing v1.1 Create Budget Line Items endpoint
x-changelog.description:
'wbs_code_id' is replacing the 'cost_code_id' and 'line_item_type_id' parameters for creating Budget Line Items.
Previously, we required 'cost_code_id' and 'line_item_type_id', along with all other attributes in order to create a Budget Line Item.
Now, developers may only send 'wbs_code_id' and succesfully create a Budget Line Item.

As well, 'wbs_code' is now a property of the response of a successful Budget Line Item creation.
The new endpoint will also no longer respond with fields related to Budget columns, e.g. "approved_budget_changes", "projected_costs", "direct_costs", etc...

When migrating from v1.0 to v1.1, cost_code_id and line_item_type_id params must be converted to a Work Breakdown Structure Code, which can be found using the Work Breakdown Structure Codes List endpoint (https://developers.procore.com/reference/rest/v1/codes#list-project-wbs-codes).
Once the Work Breakdown Structure containing the same Cost Code and Line Item Type is found, the ID can be used as the 'wbs_code_id' parameter for the Budget Line Item Create request.

parameters.name: filters[financial_period_id][]
parameters.description: Filter snapshots by financial period ID. Accepts one or more IDs. Pass the token `null` (or `nil`) as a value to match snapshots that have no financial period. Tokens and IDs can be combined — e.g. `["42", "null"]` matches snapshots in period 42 or with no period.

parameters.name: comparison_budget_column_ids
parameters.description: Restrict comparison data to these budget column IDs. When omitted, comparison is returned for all columns.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order for the returned snapshots. Prefix a value with `-` for descending order. `created_at` sorts by when the snapshot was taken; `financial_period` sorts by the associated financial period's date range (snapshots without a financial period sort last when ascending).

mapped_to_status.description: The default status this custom status maps to

available.description: Whether the status is available for selection

initial.description: Whether this is the initial status for new snapshots

standard_type.description: Origin/category of the status: approved and under_review are Procore-provided; custom is company-defined.

parameters.name: budget_view_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the Budget View (also known as Budget Template).

get.summary: Get Summary Rows for a Project's Budget
get.description:
Get summary rows for a project's budget view. Rows are grouped and aggregated according to `group_by`, unlike Detail Rows, which returns one row per budget line item.
To restrict or reorder which columns are returned, pass `column_ids` with the desired column `id` values, in the desired order. A column's `id` (used for `column_ids`) is different from its `attribute` (the key used for that column's value in each row below) — see [Get a Budget View](https://developers.procore.com/reference/rest/budget-view?version=latest) for the `columns` array, which has both plus display metadata (`label`, `type`, `format`, `display_rules`).
To read rows from a snapshot instead of the live budget, pass `source_snapshot_id` — this query parameter is shared across this endpoint, Detail Rows, and the Budget View endpoint.
This endpoint is paginated with `page`/`per_page` (maximum 100); requests with a larger `per_page` return 400. Page through results with `page`, and read `Total`, `Per-Page`, and `Link` from the response headers.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description:
Array of group objects to create hierarchical groupings. Rows will be grouped by the first criterion, 
then by the second within each first-level group, and so on.

Supported group object types:
  - WBS segment group
    Structure:
      - id: <segment_id>
      - tier: <segment_tier>
      - type: 'segment'
      - values: <array of segment item ids>

    Example:
    `{"id": "23", tier: <segment_tier>, "type": "segment", "values": [2, 3]}`
    
  - WBS attribute group
    Structure:
      - id: <attribute_id>
      - type: 'attribute'
      - values: <array of attribute item ids>

    Example:
    `{"id": "23", "type": "attribute", "values": [2, 3]}`

**Hierarchical grouping examples**:

Multiple groups (array format):
```json
[
  {"id": "12", "tier": 1, "type": "segment"},
  {"id": "23", "type": "attribute"}
]
```

Query string example:
`group_by[0][id]=12&group_by[0][tier]=1&group_by[0][type]=segment&group_by[1][id]=23&group_by[1][type]=attribute`

This would group rows first by segment ID 12, then by attribute ID 23 within each segment group.

    Query string example:
    `comparison[snapshot_id]=1&comparison[column_ids][]=23&comparison[column_ids][]=45&comparison[modes][]=variance`

x-changelog.summary: Accept Time-category units of measure when creating a Budgeted Production Quantity
x-changelog.description:
Create now accepts `unit_of_measure` values from the company's master
Units of Measure list that are categorized as Time (for example `days` or
`hours`). Those values previously returned 422. Units that are not on the
company list are still rejected.

x-changelog.summary: Sync creates to Production Tracking when claiming schemes are enabled
x-changelog.description:
On a project that tracks production by rules of credit, create now writes a
matching planned production quantity in Production Tracking before the
budgeted row is saved. When Production Tracking refuses the request, the
response is 422 with `errors` as an object (for example `errors.base`),
the same shape create already uses for validation failures. The budgeted
row is not created.

x-changelog.summary: Accept a rules-of-credit tree on create when claiming schemes are enabled
x-changelog.description:
When claiming schemes are enabled, create accepts optional `components` or
`scheme` (not both). A malformed tree returns 422. These fields are ignored
when claiming schemes are off. The tree is not returned in the response.

x-changelog.summary: Corrected quantity validation when creating a Budgeted Production Quantity
x-changelog.description:
An existing bug allowed BPQs to be created with negative quantities and absurdly large values,
both of which have been corrected.

'quantity' must now be greater than or equal to 0 and must round to an absolute value less
than 1,000,000,000.00. Values outside that range are rejected with a 422 instead of being
stored.

On a project that tracks production by rules of credit, a quantity carrying more than two
decimal places is rounded to two on save rather than stored at full precision, so the value
matches what Production Tracking holds.

x-changelog.summary: Accept Time-category units of measure when updating a Budgeted Production Quantity
x-changelog.description:
Update now accepts `unit_of_measure` values from the company's master
Units of Measure list that are categorized as Time (for example `days` or
`hours`). Those values previously returned 422. Units that are not on the
company list are still rejected. The existing lock when the quantity has
associated actual (installed) production quantities is unchanged.

x-changelog.summary: Accept wbs_code_id when updating a Budgeted Production Quantity
x-changelog.description:
Update accepts optional `wbs_code_id` so a row can be reassigned to a
different production quantity code. The field was not part of the published
update schema and was previously dropped by strong parameters. Omit it to
leave the current code unchanged. A new `wbs_code_id` is rejected with 422
when it is not a production quantity code on this project, or when the
quantity has associated actual (installed) production quantities (matching
the existing unit-of-measure lock).

x-changelog.summary: Sync updates to Production Tracking when claiming schemes are enabled
x-changelog.description:
On a project that tracks production by rules of credit, update now patches
the linked planned production quantity in Production Tracking before the
budgeted row is saved. When Production Tracking refuses the request, the
response is 422 with `errors` as an object, the same shape update already
uses for validation failures.

x-changelog.summary: Accept a rules-of-credit tree on update when claiming schemes are enabled
x-changelog.description:
When claiming schemes are enabled, update accepts the same optional
`components` or `scheme` tree as create. On update, a component or a step
may also carry an `id`, to change one that already exists, or
`_destroy: true`, to remove one. Update does not check the shape of the
tree the way create does. These fields are ignored when claiming schemes
are off.

x-changelog.summary: Corrected quantity validation when updating a Budgeted Production Quantity
x-changelog.description:
An existing bug allowed BPQs to be updated with negative quantities and absurdly large values,
both of which have been corrected.

'quantity' must now be greater than or equal to 0 and must round to an absolute value less
than 1,000,000,000.00. Values outside that range are rejected with a 422 instead of being
stored.

On a project that tracks production by rules of credit, a quantity carrying more than two
decimal places is rounded to two on save rather than stored at full precision, so the value
matches what Production Tracking holds.

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.description: Returns the direct children of `parent_uuid` in the company portfolio-program hierarchy, each with Capital Planning rollups over its full visible subtree. `parent_uuid=root` returns the top tier plus metadata and the grand total; a node uuid returns that node’s children. Read-only.

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: When set, serves the tier from the hierarchy frozen in the given completed snapshot instead of the live tree. Same params and response shape; `parent_uuid` resolves against the snapshot’s nodes. 404 for a missing or foreign snapshot, 409 while it is still building.

parameters.name: filters[in_plan][]
parameters.description: Filter by in-plan state. Accepts `true` or `false`; sending both, or omitting it, returns projects in either state.

parameters.name: filters[portfolio_program][]
parameters.description: Portfolio-hierarchy node filter. Send node uuids, or the sentinel `none` to include projects with no node (or a node not yet synced). Matches the project’s own node only (no descendants).

parameters.name: filters[program][]
parameters.description: Legacy program filter. Send the program's procore_program_id, or the sentinel `none` to include projects with no program.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on project name or number

parameters.name: include_rows
parameters.description: Default true. With `parent_uuid=root&include_rows=false` the response carries `metadata` and `grand_total` only, with `data: []`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sibling order as `field:asc|desc`. Fields: name, planned_amount, original_budget, revised_budget, job_to_date_costs, forecast_to_complete, estimated_cost_at_completion, remaining, descendant_project_count. Default `name:asc`. The Unassigned row stays last regardless of sort.

parameters.name: parent_uuid
parameters.description: `root` for the top-level tier (Unassigned row included, last), or a node uuid for its direct children. `none` is invalid — the Unassigned row has no child programs.

200.description: One hierarchy tier; metadata and grand total on the root tier

Per-Page.description: Page size

Total.description: Visible siblings under parent_uuid

Link.description: Pagination link header

data.description: One sibling tier, ordered per `sort` and paged. The Unassigned row is last on the root tier regardless of sort.

uuid.description: Node uuid. `null` only on a synthetic Unassigned row: the root one (`parent_uuid` `null`) or the one listed last in a program's child tier (`parent_uuid` = that program).

procore_id.description: Upstream Procore program id. Reference only, never a lookup key.

parent_uuid.description: Parent node uuid; `null` at the root tier.

procore_level_id.description: Hierarchy level id; `null` on the Unassigned row.

level_label.description: Level label resolved from `metadata.hierarchy.levels`; `null` on the Unassigned row.

has_children.description: True when at least one visible child program exists. Expand fetches `/portfolio_programs?parent_uuid=<uuid>`.

project_count.description: Visible projects assigned directly to this node. When `has_children` is true, they are listed under a synthetic Unassigned row last in the node's child tier; otherwise expand fetches `/projects?portfolio_program_uuid=<uuid>`.

descendant_project_count.description: Visible projects across the full subtree (equals `project_count` on leaves).

monthly_forecasts.description: Summed monthly forecasts across the subtree, keyed `YYYY-MM`.

metadata.description: Present on `parent_uuid=root` requests only.

currency_display.description: Preferred currency display/symbol from company Currency Settings.

permission_level.description: The requesting user's Capital Planning permission level, used by the UI to gate admin-only affordances (e.g. the settings entry point).

enabled.description: True when at least one hierarchy level is ingested for the company. When false the UI renders the legacy program view.

levels.description: Hierarchy levels ordered by position ascending.

programs.description: Legacy programs with at least one visible project, for the `filters[program][]` picker. The client appends the `none` option.

grand_total.description: Company-wide totals over the filtered project set. Present on `parent_uuid=root` requests only.

409.description: SNAPSHOT_NOT_READY — the snapshot has not finished building

503.description: The permission check could not be completed (`AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE`) — safe to retry

patch.description: Applies one set of forecasting fields (planned start date, planned end date, curve) to many projects at once. Targets either an explicit list of project ids or every project matching a filter query minus exclusions. Partial success: projects failing validation are skipped and reported in the response rather than failing the request.

all.description: When true, target every project matching the query below, minus excluded_ids.

ids.description: Procore project ids to update. Required unless `all` is true; ignored when `all` is true.

excluded_ids.description: Procore project ids to exclude. Only meaningful when `all` is true.

program_ids.description: Restrict the selection to these programs. Use "none" for projects with no program. Omit for company-wide. Only used when `all` is true.

portfolio_program_uuid.description: Restrict the selection to projects directly under this portfolio program node (descendants excluded), as `GET /projects` `portfolio_program_uuid`. Use "none" for projects with no node (or a node not yet synced). Mutually exclusive with `program_ids` and `filters.portfolio_program`. Only used when `all` is true.

search.description: Name/number search applied to the selection. Only used when `all` is true.

filters.description: Narrows the selection. Only used when `all` is true.

program.description: Legacy program filter, as `GET /projects` `filters[program][]`: procore program ids, or `none` for projects with no program.

portfolio_program.description: Portfolio-hierarchy node filter, as `GET /projects` `filters[portfolio_program][]`: node uuids (the project's own node), or `none` for projects with no node (or a node not yet synced).

200.description: Counts of updated projects plus per-project failures

updated_count.description: Projects whose capital plan data was written.

failed_count.description: Projects skipped because they failed validation. See `failures`.

concept_project_count.description: Subset of `updated_count` that are concept-stage projects. Reported so the client can attribute bulk edits without a second read.

failures.description: One entry per skipped project. Empty when every target succeeded.

message.example: End Date cannot be before Start Date

planned_amount.description: Set a Planned Amount. Use "0.00" to clear and freeze at zero. null means never set — the response follows the live budget (COALESCE(revised_budget, estimated_budget)). To store blank with no tracking, send planned_amount: null with budget_cleared: true.

budget_cleared.description: When true with a null planned_amount, the cell stays blank and does not track the budget. An explicit budget_cleared in the same request wins even alongside a non-null planned_amount.

monthly_forecasts.description: Manual forecast values keyed by month (`YYYY-MM`); a null clears that month. At most 240 months in one request. Keys that are exactly one fiscal year (12 consecutive FY-aligned months) or one fiscal quarter (3 consecutive FY-aligned months) record a single `FY{year}` / `FQ{n} {year}` change-history row, not one row per month — that is the current FE year/quarter cell payload.

program_name.description: Display name of the legacy Procore program the project belongs to (the flat-view Program column); null when unassigned.

portfolio_program_uuid.description: The portfolio-hierarchy node the project belongs to; null when unassigned. Always null on snapshot reads (not captured).

planned_amount.description: Effective Planned Amount. When the stored column is null and budget_cleared is false, this is resolved from COALESCE(revised_budget, estimated_budget) and tracks later budget changes. A stored "0.00" is a cleared value and does not re-prefill.

budget_cleared.description: True when the Planned Amount was explicitly emptied (null + no budget tracking). False for untouched (tracks budget), set, or cleared-to-zero ("0.00") cells.

parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified Change Reason ID(s).

parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified Change Type ID(s).

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified IDs.

parameters.name: filters[include_deleted]
parameters.description: Use 'only' for only deleted resources. Use 'with' for deleted and undeleted resources.

parameters.name: filters[origin_type][]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified origin type(s). Valid values are `Observations::Item`, `Rfi::Header`, `Meeting`, `SiteInstruction`, `CommunicationThread`, and `GenericToolItem`.

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: include_rfqs
parameters.description: Determines whether to include RFQs in the response. If it's true, or left off, RFQs will be shown in the response. If it is false, RFQs will not be shown.

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

id.description: Unique identifier of the Change Event. Use as the {id} path parameter for GET/PATCH /rest/v1.0/change_events/{id}.

number.description: Number with alpha characters stripped out

origin_data.description: Origin data

origin_id.description: Origin ID

title.description: Human-readable title summarizing the Change Event.

description.description: Detailed description of the work or reason for the Change Event.
description.example: Replace the bathtub in the bathroom

status.description: Name of the Change Event's current status, lowercased (e.g. 'pending - revised').

project_id.description: Unique identifier for the project.

created_at.description: Created at

deleted_at.description: Deleted at

updated_at.description: Updated at

event_type.description: Display name of the Change Event's Change Type (e.g. 'TBD', 'Owner Change').

event_scope.description: Scope classification indicating whether the Change Event is in scope, out of scope, or still to be determined.

change_event_origin_id.description: ID of the source record this Change Event originated from. Paired with change_event_origin_type.

change_event_origin_type.description: Type of the source record this Change Event originated from (e.g. Rfi::Header, GenericToolItem).

full_number.description: RFI Number including the prefix stage if exists

full_number_with_revision.description: RFI Number including the prefix stage and revision number if exists

status.description: Status

id.description: Unique ID of this segment item (cost code, sub-job, line item type, or custom segment item). Use as segment_item_id when constructing a new WBS code via POST /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/work_breakdown_structure/wbs_codes.

code.description: Short alphanumeric code for this segment item (e.g., '01-222'). Combined with sibling segment codes to form the flat_code on the parent WBS code.

name.description: Human-readable name of this segment item (e.g., 'Lighting'). Combined with sibling segment names to form the flat_name on the parent WBS code.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this segment item was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this segment item was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

parent_id.description: ID of the parent segment item in a tiered segment hierarchy. Null for root-level items or items in a flat-structure segment.

path_ids.description: Ordered list of IDs from the root ancestor down to (and including) this segment item. Use to reconstruct the full hierarchy path.

path_code.description: Full path code for this segment item representing the leaf code in its hierarchy (e.g., '01-222').

is_parent.description: Whether this segment item has child items in a tiered segment structure. Always false for flat-structure segments.

path_codes.description: Ordered list of code strings from the root ancestor down to (and including) this segment item, formatted as 'code - name'.

path_names.description: Ordered list of name strings from the root ancestor down to (and including) this segment item, formatted as 'code - name'.

in_use.description: Whether this segment item is currently referenced by at least one entity (e.g., a budget line item or WBS code).

segment.description: The WBS segment definition that this segment item belongs to.

id.description: Unique ID of the WBS segment definition.

name.description: Display name of the segment (e.g., 'Cost Code', 'Sub Job').

type.description: Category of this segment. One of: 'cost_code', 'line_item_type', 'sub_job', 'custom', 'attribute'. Determines which domain entity backs the segment items.

position.description: Display order of this segment within the WBS pattern. Lower numbers appear first when reading the flat_code left to right.

delimiter.description: Character used to separate this segment's value from adjacent segments in the flat_code (e.g., '.').

required.description: Whether this segment must have a value for a WBS code to be valid.

segment_items_count.description: Total number of segment items defined for this segment.

Python3
x-code-samples.content:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

headers = { 'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN" }

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v1.0/change_events?project_id=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&per_page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&filters%5Bchange_event_status_id%5D%5B%5D=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE&filters%5Bchange_order_change_reason_id%5D%5B%5D=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE&filters%5Bchange_type_id%5D%5B%5D=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE&filters%5Bcreated_at%5D=SOME_STRING_VALUE&filters%5Bid%5D=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE&filters%5Binclude_deleted%5D=SOME_STRING_VALUE&filters%5Borigin_type%5D%5B%5D=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE&filters%5Bupdated_at%5D=SOME_STRING_VALUE&include_rfqs=false", headers=headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

x-changelog.summary: Added include_rfqs as an optional parameter
x-changelog.description:
Added a parameter that allows Change Event INDEX response to remove RFQs from the response.

RFQs will be included by default in the Change Events INDEX response. The new parameter takes the following values:

* `true` (the default value if not provided)
* `false`

To exclude RFQs from each Change Event, add `?include_rfqs=false` to the query string.

x-code-samples.content:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

payload = "{\"project_id\":345756,\"change_event\":{\"title\":\"Toilet replacement\",\"number\":\"A14\",\"status\":\"open\",\"change_event_status_id\":345998,\"change_order_change_reason_id\":3452,\"event_scope\":\"in_scope\",\"event_type\":\"tbd\",\"origin_data\":\"OD-123654789\",\"origin_id\":\"654987123\",\"rfi_id\":496787,\"change_event_line_items_attributes\":[{\"id\":592648,\"wbs_code_id\":{\"id\":40389},\"description\":\"Add caulk to bathtub base\",\"uom\":\"hours\",\"estimated_cost_amount\":\"17705.0\",\"estimated_cost_quantity\":125.5,\"estimated_cost_unit_cost\":75.5,\"estimated_cost_calculation_strategy\":\"manual\",\"line_item_type_id\":657393,\"cost_code_id\":32940,\"proposed_vendor_id\":58320,\"proposed_contract_id\":234859,\"commitment_contract_line_item_id\":342949}],\"attachments_by_drawing_revision\":[{\"id\":3456}],\"attachments_by_file_version\":[{\"id\":3456}],\"attachments_by_form\":[{\"id\":3456}],\"attachments_by_image\":[{\"id\":3456}],\"attachments_by_uuid\":[{\"upload_uuid\":\"01FG753MPADZBDWA63MH20XQVQ\"}]},\"change_event_origin_id\":5944991,\"change_event_origin_type\":\"GenericToolItem\",\"origin_global_id\":\"gid://procore/GenericToolItem/5944991\",\"attachments\":[\"string\"]}"

headers = {
    'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN",
    'content-type': "application/json"
    }

conn.request("PATCH", "/rest/v1.0/change_events/%7Bid%7D?project_id=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

Python3

import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

headers = { 'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN" }

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v1.1/change_events/%7Bid%7D?project_id=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&include_deleted_change_event_line_items=true", headers=headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

x-changelog.description: - Change Event new attribute source_of_revenue_rom

x-changelog.summary: Remove unit_of_measure from ChangeEvent ChangeItems
x-changelog.description:
Updated the LIST request so it will not include next attributes anymore:
  - change_event[change_items][revenue_impact][estimate][unit_of_measure]
  - change_event[change_items][budget_impact][estimate][unit_of_measure]

x-changelog.summary: Add commitments and change orders converted amounts and their currency data to Change Events responses
x-changelog.description:
Updated the response in our Change Event endpoints to include commitments and change orders converted amounts and unit costs:
  - amount_project_currency: returns the converted amount of the commitment or change order in the project's currency
  - unit_cost_project_currency: returns the converted unit cost of the commitment or change order in the project's currency
  - currency_configuration: provides the currency configuration for the commitment or change order, including the currency code and exchange rate

x-changelog.summary: Add timestamps and ability to include deleted Change Event Line Items to Change Events responses
x-changelog.description:
Updated the response in the Change Event endpoints to include deleted Change Event Line Items:
  - change_items: can now return deleted Change Event Line Items if `include_deleted_change_event_line_items` is passed in the query params
  - change_items.created_at: returns the created_at timestamp of the Change Event Line Item
  - change_items.updated_at: returns the updated_at timestamp of the Change Event Line Item
  - change_items.deleted_at: returns the deleted_at timestamp of the Change Event Line Item

- Updated the LIST response to contain associated Budget Change data in Production Quantities
- Updated the LIST response to contain associated Prime CO data in Production Quantities

x-changelog.description: - Updated the LIST response to contain new attribute source_of_revenue_rom

x-changelog.summary: Remove additional data to ChangeEvent Production Quantities response
x-changelog.description:
Updated the response so it will remove prime_contract_change_order:
  - production_quantities[prime_contract_change_order] will be removed

x-changelog.summary: Add commitments and change orders converted amounts to Change Events responses
x-changelog.description:
Updated the response in our Change Event endpoints to include commitments and change orders converted amounts and unit costs:
  - amount_project_currency: returns the converted amount of the commitment or change order in the project's currency
  - unit_cost_project_currency: returns the converted unit cost of the commitment or change order in the project's currency
  - currency_configuration: provides the currency configuration for the commitment or change order, including the currency code and exchange rate

x-changelog.summary: Add timestamps to Change Events responses
x-changelog.description:
Updated the response in the Change Event endpoints to include timestamps:
  - change_items.created_at: returns the created_at timestamp of the Change Event Line Item
  - change_items.updated_at: returns the updated_at timestamp of the Change Event Line Item
  - change_items.deleted_at: returns the deleted_at timestamp of the Change Event Line Item

x-changelog.summary: Add budget_modification_id to Change Event responses
x-changelog.description:
Updated the response in the Change Event endpoints to include the budget_modification_id:
  - budget_modification_id: returns the budget modification ID of the Change Event

x-changelog.summary: Add search filtering to the Change Events list
x-changelog.description: Added `filters[search]` to filter Change Events by searchable fields. Blank searches return the default list.

x-code-samples.content:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

payload = "{\"change_event\":{\"number\":\"A056\",\"title\":\"New Bathtub Installation\",\"description\":\"Install a new bathtub in the bathroom\",\"scope\":\"in_scope\",\"prime_contract_for_estimates\":{\"id\":3465},\"event_origin\":{\"origin_id\":3465,\"origin_type\":\"rfi\"},\"change_reason\":{\"id\":3465},\"status\":{\"id\":123},\"source\":\"budget_change\",\"source_of_revenue_rom\":\"latest_cost\",\"change_type\":{\"id\":123},\"external_data\":{\"origin_data\":\"OD-123654789\",\"origin_id\":\"string\"},\"custom_field_%{custom_field_definition_id}\":\"custom field value\",\"change_items\":[{\"budget_code\":{\"id\":40389},\"budget_impact\":{\"estimate\":{\"amount\":123.34,\"auto_balance\":true,\"calculation_strategy\":\"manual\",\"quantity\":123.45,\"transfer\":{\"amount\":123.45,\"from_wbs_code_id\":1},\"unit_cost\":321.54,\"unit_of_measure\":\"ft\"},\"source_of_budget_rom\":\"automatic\"},\"cost_impact\":{\"estimate\":{\"amount\":76.25,\"calculation_strategy\":\"manual\",\"quantity\":2.5,\"unit_cost\":30.5,\"unit_of_measure\":\"hours\"},\"vendor\":{\"proposed\":{\"id\":43088}},\"contract\":{\"proposed\":{\"id\":43088}}},\"description\":\"Add caulk to bathtub base\",\"revenue_impact\":{\"estimate\":{\"amount\":116.55,\"calculation_strategy\":\"manual\",\"quantity\":10.5,\"unit_cost\":11.1,\"unit_of_measure\":\"hours\"},\"source_of_revenue_rom\":\"latest_cost\"}}]}}"

headers = {
    'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN",
    'content-type': "application/json"
    }

conn.request("POST", "/rest/v1.1/change_events?project_id=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

x-changelog.description:
Updated the response in our Change Event endpoints to include commitments and change orders converted amounts and unit costs:
  - amount_project_currency: returns the converted amount of the commitment or change order in the project's currency
  - unit_cost_project_currency: returns the converted unit cost of the commitment or change order in the project's currency
  - currency_configuration: provides the currency configuration for the commitment or change order, including the currency code and exchange rate

import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

headers = { 'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN" }

x-changelog.description:
Updated the response in our Change Event endpoints to include commitments and change orders converted amounts and unit costs:
  - amount_project_currency: returns the converted amount of the commitment or change order in the project's currency
  - unit_cost_project_currency: returns the converted unit cost of the commitment or change order in the project's currency
  - currency_configuration: provides the currency configuration for the commitment or change order, including the currency code and exchange rate

x-changelog.summary: Filter List Checklists (Inspections) by failed async operation items
x-changelog.description: The List Checklists (Inspections) and List Grouped Checklists (Inspections) endpoints, and their recycle bin counterparts, accept `filters[failed_items_by_operation_id]` and optional `filters[error_category]`. When `failed_items_by_operation_id` is present, the list is restricted to the Inspections that failed in that bulk operation. Omitted `error_category` returns every failure in the operation, including those classified as `unknown`. The operation must be one you started on the project, otherwise the request returns `404`, and a list of operation ids is rejected with `400`.

parameters.description: Searches the WBS code and description values and returns results sorted in descending order of relevance to the search query.

parameters.description: Along with 'group_id', groups WBS codes by the specified group type and group ID. Only supported option is 'contract'.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: Along with 'group_type', groups WBS codes by the specified group type and group ID. Only supported option is a contract ID.

parameters.description: If true, will hide WBS codes that are not in the specified 'group_type' and 'group_id'. Default is true. If false, WBS codes in the specified group will be returned first followed by WBS codes not in the group.

schema.description: A work breakdown structure code

id.description: Unique identifier of the Work Breakdown Structure code. Use as the {id} path parameter in PATCH /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/work_breakdown_structure/wbs_codes/{id}.

flat_code.description: The Work Breakdown Structure code made up of segment values, concatenated by the set delimiter. Use this value to display or identify a WBS code.

flat_name.description: The names of the Work Breakdown Structure segments concatenated using the company's delimiter and WBS pattern.

description.description: Description of the WBS code. Falls back to flat_name when no custom description  has been set.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the WBS code. One of: 'active' (available for use in budgets and line items), 'inactive' (not available for selection). Filter collections with filters[status][]=active or filters[status][]=inactive.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this WBS code was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this WBS code was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

segment_items.description: The segment items that make up this WBS code, one per segment in the WBS pattern. Each item represents a cost code, line item type, sub-job, or custom segment item.

id.description: Unique ID of this segment item (cost code, sub-job, line item type, or custom segment item). Use as segment_item_id when constructing a new WBS code via POST /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/work_breakdown_structure/wbs_codes.

code.description: Short alphanumeric code for this segment item (e.g., '01-222'). Combined with sibling segment codes to form the flat_code on the parent WBS code.

name.description: Human-readable name of this segment item (e.g., 'Lighting'). Combined with sibling segment names to form the flat_name on the parent WBS code.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this segment item was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this segment item was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

parent_id.description: ID of the parent segment item in a tiered segment hierarchy. Null for root-level items or items in a flat-structure segment.

path_ids.description: Ordered list of IDs from the root ancestor down to (and including) this segment item. Use to reconstruct the full hierarchy path.

path_code.description: Full path code for this segment item representing the leaf code in its hierarchy (e.g., '01-222').

is_parent.description: Whether this segment item has child items in a tiered segment structure. Always false for flat-structure segments.

path_codes.description: Ordered list of code strings from the root ancestor down to (and including) this segment item, formatted as 'code - name'.

path_names.description: Ordered list of name strings from the root ancestor down to (and including) this segment item, formatted as 'code - name'.

in_use.description: Whether this segment item is currently referenced by at least one entity (e.g., a budget line item or WBS code).

segment.description: The WBS segment definition that this segment item belongs to.

id.description: Unique ID of the WBS segment definition.

name.description: Display name of the segment (e.g., 'Cost Code', 'Sub Job').

type.description: Category of this segment. One of: 'cost_code', 'line_item_type', 'sub_job', 'custom', 'attribute'. Determines which domain entity backs the segment items.

position.description: Display order of this segment within the WBS pattern. Lower numbers appear first when reading the flat_code left to right.

delimiter.description: Character used to separate this segment's value from adjacent segments in the flat_code (e.g., '.').

required.description: Whether this segment must have a value for a WBS code to be valid.

segment_items_count.description: Total number of segment items defined for this segment.

project_can_modify_origin_project.description: Whether project-level users can modify segment items that originated from this project.

project_can_delete_origin_company.description: Whether project-level users can delete segment items that originated from the company level.

structure.description: Hierarchy structure of the segment. 'flat' means items have no parent-child relationship; 'tiered' means items can be nested with parent_id references.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this segment definition was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this segment definition was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

wbs_pattern_id.description: ID of the WBS pattern this segment belongs to.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the segment item. One of: 'active' (available for selection when creating WBS codes), 'inactive' (not available for new WBS codes).

wbs_pattern_id.description: ID of the WBS pattern that defines the segment structure for this code. All WBS codes under the same project share the same wbs_pattern_id.

attribute_items.description: Custom attribute items assigned to this WBS code. Only present when the project has WBS attributes configured. Empty array when no attributes are assigned.

attribute_id.description: ID of the WBS attribute definition.

id.description: ID of the WBS attribute item.

name.description: Display name of the assigned attribute item (a value within an attribute, e.g. 'Labor').

is_in_group.description: Whether this WBS code belongs to the group specified by the group_type and group_id query parameters. Only present when the group_type query parameter is provided;  group_id is optional.

amount.description: Amount - this field is nullable on unit quantity SOVs but NOT amount-based SOVs. For line item creates, if this field is omitted on unit quantity SOVs,  the amount will be calculated as quantity * unit_cost. For line item updates, if a null amount is passed in on unit quantity SOVs, it will set the line item extended type to "calculated".

quantity.description: Quantity - only accepted on unit quantity SOVs

unit_cost.description: Unit cost - only accepted on unit quantity SOVs

uom.description: Unit of measure - only accepted on unit quantity SOVs. For line item updates, pass null or an empty string to clear the unit of measure.
enum: Any value present in the Company list of Units of Measure

wbs_code_id.description: WBS code ID

funding_rule_id.description: ID of the funding rule associated with this line item. Funding Sources must be enabled at the project level. The rule must be ACTIVE and its currency must match the contract currency. Pass null to disassociate an existing funding rule.

quantity.description: Number of units for this line item, in the line item's unit of measure. Present only on unit-quantity schedules of values.

unit_cost.description: An "unformatted" decimal number. Specifically a number with a period as the decimal separator, without a thousands separator, and with an optional sign. It should be assumed that this number includes arbitrary precision and scale, however, the API may not store or process the number with infinite precision and scale.

post.summary: Create CSV export for Commitment Change Order Rows
post.description:
Starts an asynchronous CSV export of the Commitment Change Order Rows collection and returns
an export identifier. Generation happens in the background; poll the export status endpoint
(`GET .../commitment_change_order_rows/csv_exports/{change_order_csv_export_id}`) with the returned
`export_id` until it responds with a download URL.

202.description: Accepted. Returns the export identifier and expiration time.

export_id.description: UUID identifying the asynchronous CSV export job. Pass it as the `change_order_csv_export_id` path parameter to the status endpoint to poll for completion and obtain the download URL.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the export job and its eventual download URL expire. The job is retained for roughly six hours after creation; poll before this time.

total_payments_amount.description: Total amount paid on the contract to date across all payments, as a decimal string. May trail total_invoices_amount when invoices are billed but not yet paid.
