parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Specifies which view (which attributes) of the resource is going to be present in the response. The extended view includes vendor name and custom fields data, while the default view does not.

type.description: The type of the Commitment Contract.

number.description: The Commitment Contract number. Defaults to the project numbering sequence for the respective contract type.

status.description: The Commitment Contract status.

executed.description: The Commitment Contract executed status.

vendor_id.description: The ID of the vendor for the contract. The selected invoice contacts must all belong to this vendor. When the vendor is changed, the invoice contacts are reset.

assignee_id.description: Only applicable to Purchase Order Contracts. The ID of the user assigned to the Commitment Contract. The user must belong to the project directory (see the Project Users endpoint).

signature_required.description: If true, a signature is required to execute the contract; otherwise no signature is required.

billing_schedule_of_values_status.description: The subcontractor schedule of values (SSOV) status. Only applicable to contracts which use an SSOV.

inclusions.description: Only applicable to Work Order Contracts. The inclusions of the Commitment Contract.

exclusions.description: Only applicable to Work Order Contracts. The exclusions of the Commitment Contract.

bill_to_address.description: Only applicable to Purchase Order Contracts. The address to which invoices are sent. The default will be the bill to address of the most recently created purchase order.

ship_to_address.description: Only applicable to Purchase Order Contracts. The address to which materials are shipped. The default will be the ship to address of the most recently created purchase order.

ship_via.description: Only applicable to Purchase Order Contracts. The shipping method for the Commitment Contract.

payment_terms.description: Only applicable to Purchase Order Contracts. The payment terms for the Commitment Contract.

payment_terms_id.description: UUID of the payment terms record to associate with this Commitment Contract.

retainage_percent.description: An "unformatted" decimal number. Specifically a number with a period as the decimal separator, without a thousands separator, and with an optional sign. It should be assumed that this number includes arbitrary precision and scale, however, the API may not store or process the number with infinite precision and scale.

accounting_method.description: The accounting method for the contract. Default is driven by a project setting.

allow_comments.description: If true, comments are allowed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise comments are not allowed. Default is driven by a project setting.

allow_markups.description: If true, markups are allowed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise markups are not allowed. Default is driven by a project setting.

change_order_level_of_detail.description: The level of details for showing change orders on invoices attached to this contract.

enable_ssov.description: If true, the subcontractor schedule of values (SSOV) is enabled for the Commitment Contract; otherwise the SSOV is not enabled. Default is driven by a project setting.

allow_change_orders_ssov.description: If true, the subcontractor schedule of values (SSOV) can be enabled on change orders for this Commitment Contract. When enabled, Change Order SSOV toggles become available. Default is false.

allow_payment_applications.description: If true, invoices are allowed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise invoices are not allowed. Default is driven by a project setting.

allow_payments.description: If true, payments are allowed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise payments are not allowed. Default is driven by a project setting.

display_materials_retainage.description: If true, materials retainage is displayed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise materials retainage is not displayed. Default is driven by a project setting.

display_work_retainage.description: If true, work retainage is displayed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise work retainage is not displayed. Default is driven by a project setting.

show_cost_code_on_pdf.description: If true, cost codes are displayed on the Commitment Contract PDF; otherwise cost codes are not displayed. Default is driven by a project setting.

ssr_enabled.description: If true, the sliding scale retention is enabled for the Commitment Contract. Default is driven by a project setting.

bill_recipient_ids.description: IDs of users in the project directory (see the Project Users endpoint). These users must belong to the selected vendor and are the invoice contacts for submitting subcontractor invoices. To grant access to view the contract, these users must also be added as accessors.

private.description: If true, visible to admins and accessors only; otherwise visible to those with access to the commitments tool. Default based on project level setting.

show_line_items_to_non_admins.description: Only applicable to private contracts. If true, line items are visible to non-admins; otherwise visible to admins only.

accessor_ids.description: Only applicable to private contracts. IDs of users in the project directory (see the Project Users endpoint). These users will be able to view the commitment contract.

actual_completion_date.description: Only applicable to Work Order Contracts.

contract_estimated_completion_date.description: Only applicable to Work Order Contracts.

contract_start_date.description: Only applicable to Work Order Contracts.

delivery_date.description: Only applicable to Purchase Order Contracts.

currency_exchange_rate.description: Exchange rate used to convert amounts from the contract currency to the project currency. Accepted only on projects with multi-currency enabled and when you have permission to edit the contract exchange rate; otherwise the value is ignored.

currency_iso_code.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. USD, EUR) for the contract. Accepted only on projects with multi-currency enabled; otherwise the value is ignored.

request_for_quote_attachment_ids.description: List of attachment IDs to attach. These must presently be associated with Request For Quotes (or their Quotes / Responses).

attachment_ids.description: The current attachments to the item. Values should be omitted to remove attachments. New files cannot be attached via this param. If the key is omitted, the existing attachments will remain unchanged.

x-changelog.summary: Support attaching files from change events
x-changelog.description:
A new request parameter `change_event_attachment_ids` supports attaching
files which are presently attached to change events.

x-changelog.summary: Added allow_change_orders_ssov parameter
x-changelog.description: Added "allow_change_orders_ssov" boolean field. When true, Change Order SSOV toggles become available on this commitment's change orders.

x-changelog.summary: Support attaching files from request for quotes
x-changelog.description:
A new request parameter `request_for_quote_attachment_ids` supports attaching

x-changelog.description: Added writable "payment_terms_id" request parameter and returned "payment_terms_id" in the response payload for Commitment Contracts. The value represents the identifier of a payment terms record.

x-changelog.summary: Changed payment_terms_id values from integer identifiers to UUIDs
x-changelog.description: The "payment_terms_id" request parameter now requires the UUID of the payment terms record instead of its integer database ID.

status.description: The Commitment Contract status.

ship_via.description: Only applicable to Purchase Order Contracts. The shipping method for the Commitment Contract.

payment_terms.description: Only applicable to Purchase Order Contracts. The payment terms for the Commitment Contract.

payment_terms_id.description: UUID of the payment terms record to associate with this Commitment Contract.

retainage_percent.description: An "unformatted" decimal number. Specifically a number with a period as the decimal separator, without a thousands separator, and with an optional sign. allow_markups.description: If true, markups are allowed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise markups are not allowed. Default is driven by a project setting.

change_order_level_of_detail.description: The level of details for showing change orders on invoices attached to this contract.

display_materials_retainage.description: If true, materials retainage is displayed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise materials retainage is not displayed. Default is driven by a project setting.

display_work_retainage.description: If true, work retainage is displayed on the Commitment Contract; otherwise work retainage is not displayed. Default is driven by a project setting.

show_cost_code_on_pdf.description: If true, cost codes are displayed on the Commitment Contract PDF; otherwise cost codes are not displayed. Default is driven by a project setting.

ssr_enabled.description: If true, the sliding scale retention is enabled for the Commitment Contract. Default is driven by a project setting.

get.description: Returns the currency configuration for the specified company. When no configuration has been created yet, currency-related fields are returned as null while company eligibility and toggle defaults are still populated, so consumers can detect the unconfigured state without a 404.

schema.title: Company Currency Configuration GET Response
schema.description: Currency configuration for a Procore company. When no configuration has been created yet, currency-related fields are returned as null while company eligibility and toggle defaults are still populated.

company_id.description: Procore company ID this configuration belongs to. Matches the {company_id} path parameter and is the foreign key to use for all company-scoped multicurrency requests.

currency_iso_code.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the company's base currency (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY'). All company-scoped monetary amounts in Procore are denominated in this currency. Null when no currency configuration has been created for the company.

currency_display.description: How currency amounts should be rendered. 'symbol' renders with the locale currency glyph (e.g., $); 'code' renders with the ISO code (e.g., USD). Null when no currency configuration has been created for the company.

multicurrency_enabled.description: Whether multicurrency support is enabled for the company. When true, projects under this company may be configured with their own currency and exchange rates. Returns false (and effective date null) when no configuration exists or multicurrency has not been enabled.

multicurrency_enabled_effective_date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp marking when multicurrency was first enabled for the company. Null if multicurrency has never been enabled or no currency configuration exists. Use to audit when multicurrency went live.

eligible_for_multicurrency.description: Whether the company satisfies the prerequisites to enable multicurrency (e.g., compatible ERP integration). When false, attempts to enable multicurrency will be rejected; use this to decide whether to surface the multicurrency toggle in your UI.

multicurrency_phase_two_flag_enabled.description: Whether the company has access to the extended multicurrency capabilities (separate base/quote currency tracking and per-record exchange rate fields used by multicurrency-aware downstream resources). When false, the company is limited to baseline multicurrency behavior. Use as a hint when deciding which API shape to expect from other multicurrency-aware endpoints.

patch.description: Updates the company's currency configuration. Send only the fields you want to change; omitted fields are left unchanged. Note that `currency_iso_code` cannot be changed via this endpoint — the base currency is fixed once set. Enabling multicurrency for the first time requires a signed beta agreement (returns 400 MISSING_BETA_AGREEMENT otherwise).

currency_display.description: How currency amounts should be rendered. 'symbol' renders with the locale currency glyph (e.g., $); 'code' renders with the ISO code (e.g., USD). Defaults to 'symbol' on first configuration. Omit to leave the existing value unchanged.

multicurrency_enabled.description: Whether to enable multicurrency for the company. When true, projects under this company may be configured with their own currency and exchange rates. The first time you set this to true the company must have a signed multicurrency beta agreement; otherwise the API returns 400 MISSING_BETA_AGREEMENT. Omit to leave the existing value unchanged.

schema.title: Company Currency Configuration
schema.description: Currency configuration for a Procore company. Returned after a successful update or delete; all fields reflect the persisted record.

company_id.description: Procore company ID this configuration belongs to. Matches the {company_id} path parameter and is the foreign key to use for all company-scoped multicurrency requests.

currency_iso_code.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the company's base currency (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY'). All company-scoped monetary amounts in Procore are denominated in this currency.

currency_display.description: How currency amounts should be rendered. 'symbol' renders with the locale currency glyph (e.g., $); 'code' renders with the ISO code (e.g., USD).

multicurrency_enabled.description: Whether multicurrency support is enabled for the company. When true, projects under this company may be configured with their own currency and exchange rates.

multicurrency_enabled_effective_date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp marking when multicurrency was first enabled for the company. Null if multicurrency has never been enabled. Use to audit when multicurrency went live.

eligible_for_multicurrency.description: Whether the company satisfies the prerequisites to enable multicurrency (e.g., compatible ERP integration). When false, attempts to enable multicurrency will be rejected.

multicurrency_phase_two_flag_enabled.description: Whether the company has access to the extended multicurrency capabilities (separate base/quote currency tracking and per-record exchange rate fields used by multicurrency-aware downstream resources). When false, the company is limited to baseline multicurrency behavior. Use as a hint when deciding which API shape to expect from other multicurrency-aware endpoints.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

put.description: Updates an existing naming rule. Use isActive=false to deactivate without deleting.

parameters.name: rule_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the naming rule.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

schema.description: Request to update a field rule (definition + metadata)

rule_type.description: Optional metadata. NOT updatable: if provided, must match the existing rule's type; the server rejects mismatches.

fieldset_id.description: New fieldset id. FIELD_DEFAULTS only; ignored / rejected for NAMING. Provided to recover a rule whose asset type's fieldset has been changed by an admin. Must match the asset type's current fieldset and must contain the rule's trigger_field.

definition.description: Rule definition. Shape must match the rule's stored type — for NAMING, supply expression_fields; for FIELD_DEFAULTS, supply actions. Sent as a raw JSON object; the server converts it to the correct subtype and runs explicit validation. Omit entirely to update only metadata (e.g. is_active toggles).

is_active.description: Whether the rule is active. Set to false to deactivate.

conditions.description: Conditions AST for a conditional-validation rule

root.description: Root node of the recursive conditions tree

id.description: Unique identifier of the field rule

company_id.description: Company this rule belongs to

project_id.description: Project this rule applies to; null for company-level rules

asset_type_id.description: Asset type this rule applies to. Populated for FIELD_DEFAULTS; null for NAMING.

fieldset_id.description: Fieldset scope. '-1' for Procore default fields, external configurable fieldset id for custom fields. Null for NAMING.

rule_type.description: Kind of rule

trigger_field.description: Field that triggers this rule (e.g. asset_code for NAMING, custom_field_1234 for FIELD_DEFAULTS)

definition.description: Structured rule definition. Shape depends on ruleType: FieldRuleDefinitionDTO for NAMING, FieldDefaultsDefinitionDTO for FIELD_DEFAULTS, ConditionalValidationDefinitionDTO for MANDATORY/WARNING.

items.description: Expression segment for naming rule

value.description: For LITERAL: static text value

field.description: For REF: field identifier from Constants.NAMING_FIELDS (e.g. project, asset_type_id)

fallback.description: For REF: fallback when field value is null or empty

skip_if_empty.description: For REF: when true, omit this segment (and collapse delimiters) if the resolved value is empty instead of using fallback. Mutually exclusive with fallback. Default false.

dedupe_parent_segments.description: For REF parent_asset_id only: when true, enable ancestor segment de-duplication by dropping other REF segments whose values are already represented in the parent asset ID. Default false.

digits.description: For SEQ: number of digits for padding (e.g. 3 -> 001)

start_value.description: For SEQ: optional starting sequence number

actions.description: Non-empty list of actions to apply. Must include exactly one SET_DEFAULT; SET_READ_ONLY is optional and appears at most once.

items.description: A single action inside a field rule definition

value.description: Action value. For SET_DEFAULT: matches the Asset custom_fields storage format (String/Number/Boolean for primitives, {id, name} for reference types). For SET_READ_ONLY: Boolean true/false.

data_type.description: FieldType key (required for SET_DEFAULT; null for SET_READ_ONLY)

message.description: Optional message (reserved for future action types like SET_REQUIRED)

oneOf.description: Rule definition for MANDATORY/WARNING rules (optional custom message)

message.description: Optional custom validation message shown when the rule fires

conditions.description: Conditions AST for a conditional-validation rule

root.description: Root node of the recursive conditions tree

rule_group_id.description: Group id linking granular rules authored from one admin UI row. Null when ungrouped.

is_active.description: Whether the rule is active and applied; false to deactivate without deleting

validation_errors.description: Validation issues detected on this rule. Null when the rule is valid; a non-empty list otherwise.

items.description: Validation issue detected on a field rule at read time.

code.description: Code identifying the class of issue.

effect.description: Description of the impact of this issue.

remedy.description: Guidance on how an admin can resolve the issue.

overridden.description: Project-scope overlay indicator. Populated only in the project-scoped list view: true when a project rule overrides the company configuration for this field (value and/or editability differs, or no company rule exists); false when the row is inherited from the company with no project override. Null in company-scoped responses.

created_by.description: Contact Information

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

422.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.

get.description: Returns every Observation Type defined at the Company level, including deactivated ones. Company types are the pool that individual Projects activate from; use `GET /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/observation_types` to see what is actually selectable on a given Project.

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

schema.description: Array of Company Observation Types

id.description: Unique identifier for this Company Observation Type. Pass as `observation_template[observation_type_id]` when creating an Observation Template, or as `observation[type_id]` when creating an Observation Item on a Project where the type is activated.

name.description: Display name of the Observation Type, localized to the requesting user's locale when a translation exists.

localized_name.description: Type name resolved for the locale of the request, falling back to the Company default and then the stored name. Display this to end users rather than reimplementing the fallback chain.

category.description: Localized display name of the type's Observations Category. Procore ships six built-in categories (Quality, Safety, Commissioning, Warranty, Work to Complete, Environmental), but companies can define additional categories, so treat this as free-form text. Use `category_key` for programmatic comparisons.

category_key.description: Stable, unlocalized key of the type's Observations Category. Prefer this over `category` when branching on category in code.

category_id.description: ID of the Observations Category this type belongs to. Corresponds to the `id` returned by `GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/observations/categories`.

company_active.description: Whether the type is active at the Company level. For a company-level type this always matches `active`; the two diverge only when the same type is read in a Project scope where it has been deactivated.

active.description: Whether the type can be selected on new Observations. Inactive types are still returned so existing Observations render correctly.

kind.description: Whether the type is owned by the Company or defined on a single Project. Always `company` for records returned by the Company Observation Types endpoint.

parent_inactive.description: Whether the type's parent company-level type has been deactivated. Always false here, since Company Observation Types have no parent.

in_use.description: Whether at least one Observation Item currently references this type or one of its project-level children. Use to warn before deactivating or deleting a type.

name_translations.description: Company-authored translations of the type name, keyed by locale code (for example `en`, `es`, `fr-CA`). Null when the Company has not configured custom translations for this type.

reason.description: A human-readable code providing additional detail on the cause of the error.

parameters.name: engine_name
parameters.description:
Tool engine name (e.g. `assets`, `rfi`). Matches `Tool.engine_name`
for `provider_type` Project.

get.description:
Returns projects under a company that have a project-scoped Tool record
for the given `engine_name`, along with each project's active state and
whether the tool is active on that project.

Without filters all projects are returned regardless of status. Use
`filters[tool_active]` and `filters[project_active]` to narrow results,
or `filters[name]` to search by project name.

A tool is considered active when both `is_active` and `is_available` are
true, matching the criteria used by `Project#has_active_tool?`.

`name` is the project's display name: it's prefixed with the project
number (e.g. `"1234 - Downtown Renovation"`) when the company has
`prepend_project_number` enabled and the project has a number,
matching the format used by `GET /rest/v1.0/navigation`'s
`available_projects`. `filters[name]` and `sort=name` both take the
project number into account in that case.

Results are ordered by ascending project id by default. Use `sort` to
order by `name`, `project_active`, or `tool_active` instead.

parameters.name: filters[tool_active]
parameters.description:
Filter by tool activation status. `true` — tool active (`is_active`
and `is_available` both true). `false` — tool inactive.
Omit to return all records regardless of tool status.

parameters.name: filters[project_active]
parameters.description:
Filter by project active state. `true` — active projects only.
`false` — inactive projects only.
Omit to return all records regardless of project status.

parameters.name: filters[name]
parameters.description:
Search by project name. Matches projects whose `name` (as returned
in the response) contains the given value, case-insensitively — so
when project numbers are prepended, `4521`, `harbor`, and
`4521 - harbor` all match `"4521 - Harbor Tower"`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of fields to sort by, applied in order.
Prefix a field with `-` to sort it descending. For example,
`sort=-project_active,name` returns active projects first, then
inactive ones, alphabetically by name within each group.
Defaults to ascending project id when omitted. Supported fields:
`name`, `project_active`, `tool_active`.

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

number when the company has `prepend_project_number`
enabled and the project has a number.

x-changelog.summary: Added Company Project Tools endpoint
x-changelog.description: Returns projects within a company that have a project-scoped tool for the given engine_name, including each project's display name, active state, and whether the tool is active (is_active and is_available both true, matching Project#has_active_tool?). The name is prefixed with the project number when the company has prepend_project_number enabled and the project has a number, matching GET /rest/v1.0/navigation's available_projects format. Without filters all records are returned. Optional filters[tool_active] and filters[project_active] boolean params narrow results by tool or project active state respectively, and filters[name] searches by the underlying project name (case-insensitive, partial match). Results are ordered by ascending project id by default; an optional sort param (e.g. sort=-project_active,name, for active projects first then inactive, alphabetically within each group) supports ordering by name, project_active, and/or tool_active, descending when prefixed with '-'; sort=name orders by the underlying project name.

x-changelog.description: When the company has prepend_project_number enabled, filters[name] now matches against the returned "number - name" value, so searching by the project number, the name, or the full "number - name" string all work.

post.summary: Bulk add company users to projects
post.description:
This endpoint allows company users to be bulk added to multiple projects with a permission template in one request.
If the user was already part of that project it will not update the assigned permission template.

users.title: Company Users Bulk Add
users.description: Array of existing company users with a permission template id and project id that they will be assinged to. The maximum amount per request is 1000 user_id, project_id, permission_template_id triplets. If more than 1000 objects are sent then a worker will be triggered to perform the action asynchronously.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to add

project_id.description: The ID of project to add the user to

permission_template_id.description: The ID of the permission template to assign to the user

schema.description: One key for each user ID passed in

userId.description: One key for each project ID for that nested user ID

projectId.description: Success if the user ID / project ID combination succeeded, failure if not

patch.description:
Creates or updates a batch of Company Vendors.
See [Using Sync Actions](/documentation/using-sync-actions) for additional information.

#### Country and State codes
The `country_code` and `state_code` parameter values must conform to the ISO-3166 Alpha-2 specification.
See [Working with Country Codes](/documentation/country-codes) for additional information.

#### Documentation

The purpose of this API is to allow one or more vendors to be created or updated.

The caller provides an array of hashes, each hash containing the attributes for
a single vendor. The attribute names in each hash match those used by the Create
and Update Company Vendors APIs. Attributes for a maximum of 1000 vendors may
be passed with each call.

The API will always return an HTTP status of 200.

The response body will contain two attributes entities and errors. The attributes
for each successfully created or updated vendor will appear in the entities list.
The attributes for each vendor will match those returned by the Show Company Vendor
API. For each vendor which could not be created or updated, the attributes supplied
by the caller will be present in the errors list, along with an additional errors
attribute which will provide reasons for the failure.

For each vendor the caller supplies data for, the Sync API uses two different
types of unique identifier to determine whether a new vendor is to be created,
or an existing vendor is to be updated. The unique identifiers are supplied
as the ID and origin_id attributes.

If neither unique identifier is provided, Procore will attempt to create a new
vendor. For example the request below will create two new Vendors.

````json
{
  "company_id": 352361,
  "updates": [
    { "name": "New Vendor 1" },
    { "name": "New Vendor 2" }
  ]
}
````

The response to this request lists all attributes for the vendors which have been created.

The ID attribute is the Procore unique identifier for a particular vendor.
If the caller already knows the Procore unique identifier for a particular
vendor (either through the List Company Vendors API or through the Create Company Vendor API)
this value can be passed to indicate which vendor is to be updated. Note that
if the caller passes an ID value which Procore does not recognise, Procore will report
an error.

The caller does not need to be aware of the unique identifiers assigned by Procore
for each vendor in order to create or update them. Instead the caller can provide
their own unique identifier for the vendor in the `origin_id` attribute.
If Procore cannot find a vendor with the supplied `origin_id` it will create
a new one. If Procore can find a vendor with the supplied `origin_id` it will update it.

Note that alongside the origin_id attribute, Procore also provides an `origin_data`
attribute. Procore does not interpret the contents of this attribute.
The caller can use this to store and retrieve their own contextual
information about this vendor.

x-changelog.description:
When create fails because a custom field shares a visible label with a
default field, the 422 `error.details[]` entry for
`DUPLICATE_VISIBLE_FIELD` now includes an optional `meta` object with
`default_field_id`, `default_field_name`, `custom_field_id`, and
`custom_field_name`. The detail `message` now names both fields. Other
validation errors are unchanged and omit `meta`.

get.description:
Lists the contract compliance documents

**Procore Pay must be enabled to use this endpoint.**

parameters.name: status[]
parameters.description:
Return only compliance documents in the given statuses. Repeat the parameter to filter on more than one status. Omit it to return documents in every status.

Example usage:

        ?status[]=not_compliant&status[]=in_review&status[]=revision_needed

Documents still stored under a legacy status are matched by the current equivalent — `not_compliant` also returns `not_submitted` documents, `in_review` also returns `review_pending`, `revision_needed` also returns `revise_and_resubmit`, and `compliant` also returns `approved`. The legacy values themselves are not accepted as filter values.

A value outside the enum returns `400 Bad Request`.

parameters.name: allow_vendor_submission

x-changelog.summary: Add list and show endpoints for contract compliance documents
x-changelog.description:
New endpoints to list and retrieve compliance documents associated with a contract.
`GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/compliance/contracts/{contract_id}/documents` returns a paginated list of compliance documents for the specified contract.
`GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/compliance/contracts/{contract_id}/documents/{id}` returns a single compliance document by ID.
Requires `view_compliance_information` permission on the commitments tool.

x-changelog.summary: Add status and allow_vendor_submission filters to the contract compliance documents list endpoint
x-changelog.description:
The list endpoint now accepts optional `status[]` and `allow_vendor_submission` query parameters, which can be used on their own or together.
`status[]` may be repeated to match several statuses, for example `?status[]=not_compliant&status[]=in_review&status[]=revision_needed`.
Documents still stored under a legacy status are matched by the current equivalent, so `compliant` also returns documents stored as `approved`.
A status outside the documented list returns a 400.
Omitting the parameters preserves the existing unfiltered behavior.

x-changelog.summary: Add required_for_vendor_submission field to the contract compliance documents list and show responses
x-changelog.description:
The `required_for_vendor_submission` field is now returned by:
`GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/compliance/contracts/{contract_id}/documents` (list)
`GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/compliance/contracts/{contract_id}/documents/{id}` (show)
When true, the vendor must submit this compliance document before they can submit an invoice. Only applicable when `allow_vendor_submission` is true. Defaults to false.
The field is returned only; it is not yet accepted in create or update requests.

x-changelog.summary: Add compliance_document_requirement_id to contract compliance document responses
x-changelog.description:
List, show, create, and update now return `compliance_document_requirement_id`.
It contains the parent document requirement ID for documents created from a template and is null for manually created documents.

`PATCH /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/compliance/contracts/{contract_id}/documents/{id}` updates a compliance document. Requires admin permission or bill-recipient status on the contract.
`DELETE /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/compliance/contracts/{contract_id}/documents/{id}` deletes a compliance document. Requires admin permission on the commitments tool.

`PATCH /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/compliance/contracts/{contract_id}/documents/{id}` (update)

x-changelog.summary: Added viewer_doc_id field to document snapshots
x-changelog.description:
The `viewer_doc_id` field has been added to coordination issue document snapshot endpoints.
This field identifies the document viewer type associated with a snapshot and is used to
determine which viewer to use when displaying the document.

* `GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/coordination_issues/{coordination_issue_id}/document_snapshots` — returns `viewer_doc_id` in each snapshot item (nullable)
* `POST /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/coordination_issues/{coordination_issue_id}/document_snapshots` — accepts optional `viewer_doc_id` in the request body
* `PATCH /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/coordination_issues/{coordination_issue_id}/document_snapshots/{id}` — accepts optional `viewer_doc_id` to update the existing value

The field is optional and nullable. When not provided during creation, it defaults to null.

post.summary: Create a document snapshot on a coordination issue (REST v2.0)
post.description:
Creates a new document snapshot linked to the coordination issue. The `snapshot_upload_uuid`
must reference a previously uploaded file (via the Procore upload flow).

The `DocumentSnapshotCreator` service creates a `ProstoreFile` from the upload UUID
using `ProstoreFileCreator`. The snapshot record is then created with the resolved
file and the provided document container/revision identifiers.

A uniqueness constraint prevents duplicate snapshots for the same `prostore_file` on the
same coordination issue (scoped to non-deleted records).

`snapshot_upload_uuid` identifies a previously uploaded file (via Procore's upload flow).

and links it to the new snapshot record.

x-changelog.summary: Map frontend 'private' field name to 'is_private' in column exports
x-changelog.description:
The export endpoint now correctly maps the frontend `private` field name (used in
CIColumnKeys) to the backend `is_private` column when building exports from table
column state. Previously, only the `is_private` key was recognised; the `private`
variant sent by the frontend was silently dropped, causing the column to be missing
from exports when the user had selected it in the data table.

This mapping is only active when the private coordination issues feature flag is
enabled for the project.

Additionally, export events are now tracked via analytics with the event key
`project.coordination_issues.coordination_issue_export.list_exported`.

x-changelog.summary: Support for custom column configuration from frontend table state
x-changelog.description:
A new optional `column_state` parameter allows the export endpoint to respect custom column configurations
from the frontend table state. This enables users to export coordination issues with their personalized
column visibility and ordering from the web interface.

The `column_state` parameter accepts an array of objects with field names that correspond to the frontend
table configuration. The export will include only the visible columns in the order specified by the user.

Features:
* Custom column visibility based on frontend table state
* Maintains user-defined column ordering in exports
* Automatic mapping between frontend field names and backend column names
* Falls back to configurable field sets or default columns when `column_state` is not provided
* Always includes non-configurable columns (issue_number, status, created_at) for data integrity

Example usage: `GET /coordination_issues/export` with `column_state: [{"field": "title"}, {"field": "assignee"}]`

x-changelog.summary: Sort by Created By company name and then by status and finally by issue number
x-changelog.description:
A new optional sort allows the index endpoint to sort by company name of the issue creator, then by status, and finally by issue number in descending order.

The status order will always be:

* `unblocked`
* `open`
* `ready_for_review`
* `blocked`
* `moved_to_observation`
* `closed`

To use the new sort, include the following query parameter: `?sort=company_then_status`

x-changelog.summary: Add Watchers column to CSV exports
x-changelog.description:
A new optional column allows the export endpoint to include watchers information in CSV exports.

The watchers column displays a comma-separated list of watcher names for each coordination issue.

To include watchers in the export, add 'watchers' to the column_state parameter.

get.description: Lists potential assignees for Coordination Issues. Use the optional `min_access_level` query parameter to filter which project users (by access level on the Coordination Issues domain) are included; see that parameter for allowed values and default behavior. Results are sorted by first name, then last name. Use `filters[search]` and `filters[id][]` with `page` and `per_page` to page through large projects.

parameters.name: min_access_level
parameters.description: Minimum project access level for users included in the assignee list for the Coordination Issues domain. `admin` limits results to Admin (plus project admins per server rules). `standard` includes Standard and Admin. `read_only` includes Read Only, Standard, and Admin. If omitted or not recognized, the response uses the same set as `standard`.

parameters.name: filters[search]
parameters.description: Case-insensitive partial match on the assignee's full name or company name.

parameters.name: filters[id][]
parameters.description: Return only the assignees with the given user IDs, e.g. `filters[id][]=1&filters[id][]=2`. IDs that are not potential assignees for the project are ignored.

items.description: Login Information

id.description: Login Information ID uniquely identifying this user.

name.description: User's display name, formatted first name then last name.

company_name.description: User Company name. If the user belongs to a vendor, the vendor name will be returned.

locale.description: IETF locale code for the user's language preference (e.g., 'en', 'ko'). Null when the user has not set a locale.

x-changelog.summary: Search and ID filters for potential assignees
x-changelog.description:
The index endpoint accepts two new optional filters:

* `filters[search]` - case-insensitive partial match on the assignee's full name or company name.
* `filters[id][]` - return only the assignees with the given user IDs, e.g. `?filters[id][]=1&filters[id][]=2`.

Filtering and pagination are applied before serialization, so `page` and `per_page` can be used to page through large projects.

CoordinationIssue can be associated with other procore items. This API endpoint creates that association.
The extended view provides what is shown below.
The normal view is the same as the extended view but excludes subject and title in item_data.
The compact view returns coordination_issue_id, item_id, and item_type only.
The default view is normal.

x-changelog.summary: Sort by Created By company name and then by status and finally by issue number
x-changelog.description:
A new optional sort allows the index endpoint to sort by company name of the issue creator, then by status, and finally by issue number in descending order.

The status order will always be:

* `unblocked`
* `open`
* `ready_for_review`
* `blocked`
* `moved_to_observation`
* `closed`

To use the new sort, include the following query parameter: `?sort=company_then_status`

get.summary: List coordination issue viewpoints (legacy + Model Manager, REST v2.0)
get.description:
**GET collection** — returns every viewpoint mapping on the issue. **Legacy** rows (join has
`bim_viewpoint_id`) use **`BimViewpointBlueprint`** view **`:procore_v0_1`** — the **same** shape as
the **`viewpoints`** array on the coordination issue resource (`CoordinationIssueBlueprint` view
`:extended_with_viewpoint_v0_1`): `camera_data`, `sections_data`, `redlines_data`, `snapshot`,
`bim_file_id`, `uuid`, numeric `id`, etc.

**MM-backed** rows (`viewpoint_uuid` only) are loaded in bulk from Model Manager
(`POST .../bim/viewpoints/batch`) and appear as full MM viewpoint objects (same shape as
`GET .../viewpoints/{uuid}` inner `data`).

Order follows the join table: `position`, then `created_at`. Pagination counts **join rows**, not
only legacy viewpoints.

Supports pagination (`page`, `per_page`; default per page **10**, max **100** per
`Rest::V2::ApplicationController` / `RestV2Pagination`).

Response headers may include `Per-Page`, `Total`, and `Link` (RFC 5988) for pagination.

**502** if Model Manager returns 5xx while resolving MM-backed rows on this page.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
When `ids_only`, response body is `{ "data": [...] }`: legacy mappings use integer
`bim_viewpoint_id`; MM-backed mappings use UUID strings. Order matches the full list (`position`,
`created_at`).

parameters.name: primary
parameters.description:
When `true`, only mappings marked primary on the issue are returned. When `false`, only non-primary
mappings. When omitted, all mappings are returned (subject to pagination). Applies to both the full
list and `view=ids_only`.

parameters.name: included
parameters.description:
**Ignored.** The `viewpoint_format` query parameter now controls the response shape.
When `viewpoint_format=v2` (default), all viewpoints are returned in Model Manager shape.
When `viewpoint_format=v1`, all viewpoints are returned in legacy shape.

parameters.name: viewpoint_format
parameters.description:
Specify the response format for viewpoint data.
When `v1`, all viewpoints (including Model Manager-backed) are returned in legacy shape (`camera_data`, `sections_data`, `redlines_data` as JSON strings). Model Manager viewpoints are transformed to match the legacy BimViewpointBlueprint `:procore_v0_1` structure.
When `v2` (default), all viewpoints (including legacy BimViewpoints) are returned in Model Manager shape (structured `payload` object with nested `camera`, `clipping`, `markup`, `visibility`, `render_mode`). Legacy viewpoints are transformed to match the Model Manager viewpoint response structure.
Identity and reference fields (`id`, `uuid`, `scene_id`, `bim_file_id`, `company_id`, `project_id`, etc.) are never transformed — they pass through as-is from the source record. Fields not present on a source record appear as `null` in the response.

200.description: OK — merged viewpoint list or id list when `view=ids_only`

x-changelog.description:
Added a `viewpoint_format` query parameter to the index, show, and batch endpoints.
When `viewpoint_format=v1`, Model Manager viewpoints are returned in legacy shape

When `viewpoint_format=v2` (default), legacy viewpoints are returned in Model Manager

post.summary: Create a Model Manager viewpoint and link it to the issue (REST v2.0)
post.description:
Proxies to Model Manager `POST /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/bim/viewpoints`
(`RequestsCreateViewpointRequest`: `scene_id`, optional `name`, `payload` per MM OpenAPI), plus
**Procore-required** `bim_model_uuid` for application validation. Then inserts
`coordination_issue_bim_viewpoints` with `viewpoint_uuid` (MM viewpoint id).

May trigger notification side effects for observers of the issue.

schema.description:
BIM MM `RequestsCreateViewpointRequest` fields plus **Procore-only** `bim_model_uuid` (required by
monolith validation; not sent as a top-level field to Model Manager).

When **`payload` is omitted**, `ViewpointCreateViaModelManagerService` builds the MM payload from
`camera_data`, `sections_data` (mapped to `clipping.planes`), `redlines_data` (mapped to `markup`),
`visibility`, `render_mode`, and `name` only.

**`primary` and `position`** affect the local `coordination_issue_bim_viewpoints` row, not the MM payload shape.

**`bim_file_id`** and **`bim_view_folder_id`** are permitted by the controller but are **not** applied on the
Model Manager strategy; include any file/folder data inside **`payload`** if Model Manager should receive it.

**`snapshot_upload_uuid`** is consumed on the **legacy strategy only** (when `scene_id` / `bim_model_uuid` are
omitted): it is forwarded to the BIM viewpoint creator, which attaches the uploaded image as a `ProstoreFile`
on the resulting `BimViewpoint`. The Model Manager strategy ignores this field — include snapshot data inside
**`payload`** instead.

bim_model_uuid.description: Required by Procore `ViewpointCreateViaModelManagerService` validation (not sent to MM create as a top-level field).

oneOf.description:
Viewpoint payload sent to / returned from Model Manager. Matches BIM MM `TypesViewpointPayload`
(camera, clipping, visibility, snapshot, markup, measurements, etc.).
JSON string of a `TypesViewpointPayload` object (same shape as the object form).

camera_data.description:
Used when top-level `payload` is absent — becomes `camera` in the MM payload. Send a JSON object or a JSON string
(parsed server-side).

redlines_data.description: Used when top-level `payload` is absent — becomes `markup` in the MM payload (object or JSON string).

sections_data.description:
Used when top-level `payload` is absent — parsed value is set on `clipping.planes` in the MM payload.
Model Manager expects an array of clipping planes (`TypesClippingPlane`); object or JSON string is accepted and passed through after parse.

bim_file_id.description: Accepted in the JSON body for parity with other viewpoint APIs; **not** applied by MM create in this flow.

bim_view_folder_id.description: Accepted in the JSON body for parity with other viewpoint APIs; **not** applied by MM create in this flow.

snapshot_upload_uuid.description:
Upload UUID of a previously uploaded snapshot image (via `POST /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/uploads`).
**Legacy strategy:** the image is attached to the created `BimViewpoint` as a `ProstoreFile`; the snapshot URL
is returned on subsequent reads. **Model Manager strategy:** ignored at the top level — include snapshot data
inside `payload` instead.

primary.description: Sets `is_primary` on the coordination-issue viewpoint mapping.

position.description: Sets ordering `position` on the coordination-issue viewpoint mapping (auto-incremented if omitted).

post.summary: Batch-get Model Manager viewpoints by UUID (REST v2.0, issue-scoped)
post.description:
Request body must include `ids` (non-empty array of UUID strings). The server **filters** `ids`
to those present on this issue as MM-backed mappings, preserves request order for the intersection,
then calls Model Manager `POST .../bim/viewpoints/batch`.

If no ids remain after filtering, returns `{ "data": [] }` **without** calling Model Manager.

Response body is forwarded from Model Manager (typically `{ "data": [ ... ] }`).

When `viewpoint_format=v1`, the Model Manager viewpoint objects are transformed to legacy shape
(camera_data, sections_data, redlines_data as JSON strings).
When `viewpoint_format=v2` (default), viewpoints are returned in Model Manager shape as-is.

parameters.name: viewpoint_format
parameters.description:
Specify the response format for viewpoint data.
When `v1`, all viewpoints (including Model Manager-backed) are returned in legacy shape (`camera_data`, `sections_data`, `redlines_data` as JSON strings). Model Manager viewpoints are transformed to match the legacy BimViewpointBlueprint `:procore_v0_1` structure.
When `v2` (default), all viewpoints (including legacy BimViewpoints) are returned in Model Manager shape (structured `payload` object with nested `camera`, `clipping`, `markup`, `visibility`, `render_mode`). Legacy viewpoints are transformed to match the Model Manager viewpoint response structure.
Identity and reference fields (`id`, `uuid`, `scene_id`, `bim_file_id`, `company_id`, `project_id`, etc.) are never transformed — they pass through as-is from the source record. Fields not present on a source record appear as `null` in the response.

post.summary: Copy Model Manager viewpoint snapshots into Prostore (REST v2.0, issue-scoped)
post.description:
Copies the snapshots of the issue's Model Manager viewpoints into the project as Prostore files, so
they can be attached to other items (for example with `prostore_file_ids`). Model Manager snapshots
are stored in File Access Service behind presigned URLs that browsers cannot read.

Only Model Manager viewpoints mapped on this issue are copied; send `viewpoint_ids` to limit them,
or omit it to copy all of them. Snapshot URLs are resolved from Model Manager, never from the request.

Copies are reused: calling the endpoint again for the same snapshot returns the existing Prostore
file instead of creating a new one.

A snapshot that cannot be copied (missing, not PNG/JPEG, larger than 25 MB, or download failure) is
reported in its `error` field; the request still succeeds.

schema.description:
Optional list of Model Manager viewpoint UUIDs whose snapshots should be copied. The server keeps only
ids that are Model Manager viewpoints on this issue. Omit `viewpoint_ids` to copy every Model Manager
snapshot on the issue.

data.description: One entry per Model Manager viewpoint processed, with either the Prostore copy or the reason it could not be made.

prostore_file.description: Prostore copy of the viewpoint snapshot. Omitted when the copy could not be made.

id.description: Prostore file ID; send it as a `prostore_file_ids` entry to attach the snapshot.

error.description: Why the snapshot could not be copied. Present only when `prostore_file` is omitted.

patch.summary: Update viewpoint mapping and/or Model Manager viewpoint content (REST v2.0)
patch.description:
Updates the MM-backed mapping (`viewpoint_id` = `viewpoint_uuid`): **`primary`** and **`position`** on
`bim_viewpoints_coordination_issues`, and optionally **`name` / payload fields** via Model Manager PATCH.
Discrete fields (`camera_data`, `sections_data`, `redlines_data`, `visibility`, `render_mode`) are merged
into the current MM payload after loading the viewpoint from Model Manager, unless **`payload`** is sent
(full replace of MM payload).

Parity keys such as **`scene_id`** / **`bim_model_uuid`** are accepted but not applied on PATCH; a body
containing **only** those (and similar no-op) fields returns **422**.

When `primary` is `true`, any other primary mapping on this issue is cleared first (at most one primary).

Requires **at least one** attribute in the body. `position` must be an integer when provided
(unless explicitly set to `null` to clear). **502** if Model Manager returns 5xx.

schema.description:
Accepts the same optional fields as **POST create** (`viewpoint_create_request.yml`) for Model Manager content
(`name`, `payload`, discrete `camera_data` / `sections_data` / `redlines_data` / `visibility` / `render_mode`)
plus **`primary`** and **`position`** on the coordination-issue join row.

**At least one** property must be present.

Model Manager **PATCH** is invoked when `name`, `payload`, or any discrete payload field is sent. If discrete fields
are sent **without** top-level `payload`, the server **loads the current viewpoint from Model Manager**, **deep-merges**
your changes into the existing payload, and replaces the MM payload with the merged result.

**`scene_id`**, **`bim_model_uuid`**, **`bim_file_id`**, **`bim_view_folder_id`**, and **`snapshot_upload_uuid`** are
accepted for parity with create but are **not applied** on update (Model Manager PATCH does not relocate the viewpoint).
A body containing **only** those fields returns **422**.

When `primary` is `true`, any other primary mapping on this issue is cleared first (at most one primary).

name.description: Passed to Model Manager viewpoint PATCH (`name`) when provided.

scene_id.description: Accepted but not applied on PATCH (create-only relocation).

bim_model_uuid.description: Accepted but not applied on PATCH.

oneOf.description:
Viewpoint payload sent to / returned from Model Manager. Matches BIM MM `TypesViewpointPayload`
(camera, clipping, visibility, snapshot, markup, measurements, etc.).
JSON string of a `TypesViewpointPayload` object (replaces MM payload when sent).

camera_data.description: When `payload` is absent — merged into MM payload as `camera` (object or JSON string).

redlines_data.description: When `payload` is absent — merged into MM payload as `markup`.

sections_data.description: When `payload` is absent — merged into MM payload as `clipping.planes`.

bim_file_id.description: Accepted but not applied on this PATCH flow.

bim_view_folder_id.description: Accepted but not applied on this PATCH flow.

snapshot_upload_uuid.description: Accepted but not applied on this PATCH flow.

primary.description: Sets `is_primary` on the coordination-issue viewpoint mapping.

position.description: Sort order on the join row; send `null` to clear when supported by validation.

**`primary`** and **`position`** from the join row included.

delete.summary: Remove viewpoint association from issue (REST v2.0; MM soft-delete when applicable)
delete.description:
Path parameter **`viewpoint_id`** must be a **UUID** (route constraint). The server resolves the join
row by **`viewpoint_uuid`** matching that id on this coordination issue (numeric `BimViewpoint` ids are
not valid on this path).

Transaction:
1. If the mapping has `viewpoint_uuid`, calls Model Manager `DELETE .../bim/viewpoints/{uuid}`.
   `404` from MM is ignored; local mapping is still removed.
2. Destroys the `coordination_issue_bim_viewpoints` row.

May trigger notification side effects for observers of the issue.

**Success response**: `head :ok` → **HTTP 200** with **no response body**.

get.summary: Resolve scene_id to bim_model_id for viewpoint deep linking
get.description:
Resolves a platform `scene_id` (from a Model Manager viewpoint) to the corresponding
`bim_model_id`. This endpoint is used by the CI MFE to construct deep-link URLs to
the document viewer with viewpoint restoration.

The resolution happens via the Model Manager service: queries model revisions filtered
by `current_platform_scene_id` and returns the `bim_model_id` from the first matching
revision.

**Not nested under a coordination issue** — authorized at the project level.

x-changelog.description:
A new optional sort allows the index endpoint to sort by company name of the issue creator, then by status, and finally by issue number in descending order.
The status order will always be:
* `unblocked`
* `open`
* `ready_for_review`
* `blocked`
* `moved_to_observation`
* `closed`
To use the new sort, include the following query parameter: `?sort=company_then_status`

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.summary: List coordination issues for a project (REST v2.0)
get.description:
Returns a paginated list of coordination issues visible to the user within the project.

Supports `view=ids_only` for `{ "data": [<id>, ...] }` (JSON numbers from `pluck(:id)`).

 Query `included` controls which attributes are present on each item (see schema description).
 Include `permissions` in the query to get `can_edit` field for each issue.

 When `save_sticky_filters` is truthy, list filters may be persisted for the tool (sticky filters).

 **`filters[is_private]`** narrows to public (`false`) or private (`true`) issues. Private-issue
 filtering may be unavailable in some projects, in which case all issues remain public.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: When `ids_only`, response is id list only (no full blueprint objects).

parameters.name: save_sticky_filters
parameters.description: When true, persist current filters for the coordination issues tool where supported.

parameters.name: included
parameters.description:
Comma-separated blueprint field names (e.g. `assignee,title,uuid,location,is_private`). When omitted or empty,
all conditional fields are included.

parameters.name: filters[assignee_company_id]
parameters.description: Filter item(s) with matching assignee vendor companies.

parameters.name: filters[assignee_id]
parameters.description: Filter item(s) with matching assignee user IDs.

parameters.name: filters[created_by_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) created by the specified User IDs

parameters.name: filters[created_by_company_id]
parameters.description: Filter item(s) with matching created by vendor companies.

parameters.name: filters[ids]
parameters.description: Return only coordination issues with these ids (see `CoordinationIssues::Filter` / `with_ids`).

parameters.name: filters[location_id]
parameters.description: Filters by specific location (Note: Use *either* this or location_id_with_sublocations, but not both)

parameters.name: filters[search]
parameters.description: Returns item(s) matching the specified search query string.

parameters.name: filters[status]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified statuses

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[due_date]
parameters.description: Filter Coordination Issues by due date.

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort results by field. Direction (asc/desc) controlled by presence or absence of '-' prefix.

parameters.name: filters[document_container_id]
parameters.description: Filter Coordination Issues by document container ID(s).

parameters.name: filters[document_revision_id]
parameters.description: Filter Coordination Issues by document revision ID(s).

parameters.name: filters[coordination_issue_file_id]
parameters.description: Filter by BIM / coordination issue file id(s).

parameters.name: filters[is_private]
parameters.description:
Filter by private flag. When the `enable-ci-private` feature is inactive for the project, all issues behave as public
for visibility and this filter has limited effect. Values are booleans (`true` = private, `false` = public).

parameters.name: filters[include_deleted]
parameters.description:
Controls visibility of soft-deleted coordination issues (recycle bin).
- `only`: return only soft-deleted issues
- `with`: return all issues including deleted ones
- omitted (default): return only active issues
Requires `view_deleted_coordination_issue` permission when set.

200.description: OK — paginated issues or ids when `view=ids_only`

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

items.description:
Rendered by `V2::CoordinationIssueBlueprint`. **`id` is always present.** Other keys depend on `included`:
when `included` is omitted or empty, all conditional blueprint fields are serialized; when `included`
lists comma-separated names, only those fields (plus `id`) appear. The BIM file association is keyed
**`bim_file`** (not `coordination_issue_file`). Nested user objects use the identity-with-company shape
(e.g. `email`, `name`).

status.description:
Current status (e.g. `open`, `closed`, `in_progress`). In projects where `in_progress` is unavailable,
issues stored as `in_progress` may serialize as `open`.

is_private.description: Present when `included` contains `is_private` or when `included` is omitted (all fields). Indicates a private coordination issue when `true`.

coordination_issue_type.description:
Configurable issue type record (`CompanyConfigurableBlueprint`: `id`, `name`, `active`, `position`,
`global`, `deletable`, timestamps). Present when `included` contains `coordination_issue_type` or is omitted.

coordination_issue_priority.description:
Configurable priority record (`CompanyConfigurableBlueprint`: `id`, `name`, `active`, `position`,
`global`, `deletable`, timestamps). Present when `included` contains `coordination_issue_priority` or is omitted.

viewpoint_count.description: Number of viewpoints attached to this coordination issue.

coordination_issue_bim_viewpoints.description:
Viewpoint mappings on this issue (`CoordinationIssueBimViewpointBlueprint` view `:normal`). Present when
`included` contains `coordination_issue_bim_viewpoints` or is omitted.

bim_viewpoint_id.description: Linked legacy BIM viewpoint id; null for Model Manager-backed mappings.

is_primary.description: Whether this mapping is the primary viewpoint for the issue.

source_file.description:
Resolved source file for the coordination issue. Returns the document name from
`document_container_metadata` when present, otherwise falls back to the BIM file.

id.description: Document container id or BIM file id.

linked_drawings.description:
Drawing revisions linked via published drawing markup (Coordination Issue pin), same semantics as REST v1
`view=extended`. Omitted unless `included` lists `linked_drawings` or `included` is omitted/empty.

url.description: Deep link to the drawing with focused markup element

drawing_markup_preview_images.description:
Preview images for published drawing markup layers. Omitted unless `included` lists
`drawing_markup_preview_images` or `included` is omitted/empty.

document_snapshots.description:
Document snapshots linked to this coordination issue (`CoordinationIssueDocumentSnapshotBlueprint`
view `:normal`). Present when `included` contains `document_snapshots` or is omitted.

items.description:
Rendered by `CoordinationIssueDocumentSnapshotBlueprint` view `:normal`. Represents a point-in-time
snapshot image of a document revision linked to a coordination issue. The `prostore_file` nested object
provides the file URL, name, content type, and viewable status.

document_container_id.description: The document container (folder) the source document belongs to.

document_name.description:
Human-readable name of the source document. Surfaced as the coordination issue's
source file for outside-workflow (document snapshot) issues. May be null for snapshots
created before this field existed.

document_revision_id.description: The document revision id from which the snapshot was taken.

document_revision_version_id.description: The specific document revision version id for this snapshot.

viewer_doc_id.description:
Identifier for the document viewer type associated with this snapshot. Used to determine
which viewer to use when displaying the document. May be null if not set.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created.

prostore_file.description:
Prostore file object (`ProstoreFileBlueprint` view `:normal_with_viewable`). Contains the snapshot
image file details including a signed URL, content type, and whether the file is viewable.

url.description: Signed download URL for the snapshot file.

content_type.description: MIME content type.

viewable.description: Whether this file has a viewable document representation.

permissions.description:
User permissions on this coordination issue. Returned only when `policy_context` is provided
in render options (typically by including the `X-Policy-Context` header or equivalent).

can_edit.description:
Whether the current user can edit (update) this coordination issue. Requires `update_coordination_issue`
permission from the policy AND the workflow (if present) to not be terminated or completed.

can_update_status.description:
Whether the current user can change the issue's status. Present only when the policy supports status
transitions; true when at least one status action is available and the workflow (if present) is active.

data.description: Coordination issue primary keys from `pluck(:id)` (JSON numbers).

x-changelog.summary: Added soft-delete filtering and restore action to coordination issues
x-changelog.description:
The REST v2.0 coordination issues endpoint now supports soft-delete filtering and restore:

* `GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/coordination_issues?filters[include_deleted]=only` — List only soft-deleted issues (recycle bin view)
* `GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/coordination_issues?filters[include_deleted]=with` — List all issues including deleted
* `GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/coordination_issues/{id}?include_deleted=true` — Show a soft-deleted issue
* `POST /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/coordination_issues/{id}/restore` — Restore a soft-deleted issue

The `filters[include_deleted]` and `include_deleted` parameters require `view_deleted_coordination_issue` permission.
The restore action requires `update_deleted_coordination_issue` permission.

post.description:
Creates an issue via `CoordinationIssues::Public::CreateService`. Request body is **flat** JSON
(not wrapped in `coordination_issue`). See create schema for which fields are persisted vs accepted-only.

**`template_id`:** Optional. When provided, the template's `issue_details` are merged as defaults
underneath the explicitly supplied fields. If configurable field validations fail, a 422 response
includes `prefill_data` with the merged template defaults for the client to present to the user.

**`status: in_progress`:** May be unavailable in some projects; when unavailable it is stored as `open`.

**`is_private`:** Optional boolean; when sent, persisted on create (see create request schema).

**`document_snapshot`:** Optional object to associate a document snapshot with the coordination issue.

Observers may enqueue notifications / activity side effects.

schema.description:
Flat request body (not wrapped in `coordination_issue`). Persisted attributes include `title`,
`description`, `status`, `creation_source`, `bim_file_id` (stored as the coordination issue file),
`bim_model_id`, `trade_id`, `location_id`, `assignee_id`, `due_date`, `issue_type`, `priority`,
`coordination_issue_type_id`, `coordination_issue_priority_id`, `company_id`, and **`is_private`**
when sent. Attachments, an optional inline document snapshot, origin, and watchers are created as
associated records.

project_id.description: Path includes project; may be echoed in body (ignored for scoping).

company_id.description: Company id for the new issue (typically matches path company).

description.description: Free-text description of the coordination issue.

status.description:
Initial status. On create, only `open`, `closed`, or `in_progress` are valid. `in_progress` may be
unavailable in some projects, in which case it is stored as `open`.

location_id.description: Location id scoped to the project.

assignee_id.description: Login information / user id for assignee.

bim_file_id.description: BIM file id for the coordination issue file association.

due_date.description: Due date for the coordination issue.

issue_type.description: Issue type label, such as `clash` or `building_code`.

priority.description: Permitted by controller; not applied by `CreateService` — use PATCH to set.

coordination_issue_type_id.description: ID of the configurable coordination issue type to assign.

coordination_issue_priority_id.description: ID of the configurable coordination issue priority to assign.

template_id.description:
Optional template ID. When provided, the template's `issue_details` are used as default values
that the explicitly supplied fields override. If the resulting issue fails configurable field
validations, a 422 response is returned with `prefill_data` containing the merged template defaults.

is_private.description:
When `true`, creates a **private** coordination issue (restricted visibility). Omitted keys leave the
column at its default (typically public).

attachment_upload_uuids.description: Prostore upload UUIDs for new attachments.

watcher_ids.description: User ids to add as watchers on the new coordination issue.

origin.description: Optional origin metadata stored with the issue when created or updated.

document_snapshot.description:
Optional inline document snapshot to create with the issue. The `snapshot_upload_uuid` references a
previously uploaded file; a `ProstoreFile` is created from it and linked to the new snapshot.

snapshot_upload_uuid.description: UUID of the previously uploaded snapshot file.

document_container_id.description: The document container (folder) the source document belongs to.

document_revision_id.description: The document revision id from which the snapshot was taken.

document_revision_version_id.description: The specific document revision version id for this snapshot.

201.description: Created — `data` is the new issue (`V2::CoordinationIssueBlueprint`, default view)

data.description:
Rendered by `V2::CoordinationIssueBlueprint`. **`id` is always present.** Other keys depend on `included`:
when `included` is omitted or empty, all conditional blueprint fields are serialized; when `included`
lists comma-separated names, only those fields (plus `id`) appear. The BIM file association is keyed
**`bim_file`** (not `coordination_issue_file`). Nested user objects use the identity-with-company shape
(e.g. `email`, `name`).

status.description:
Current status (e.g. `open`, `closed`, `in_progress`). In projects where `in_progress` is unavailable,
issues stored as `in_progress` may serialize as `open`.

is_private.description: Present when `included` contains `is_private` or when `included` is omitted (all fields). Indicates a private coordination issue when `true`.

coordination_issue_type.description:
Configurable issue type record (`CompanyConfigurableBlueprint`: `id`, `name`, `active`, `position`,
`global`, `deletable`, timestamps). Present when `included` contains `coordination_issue_type` or is omitted.

coordination_issue_priority.description:
Configurable priority record (`CompanyConfigurableBlueprint`: `id`, `name`, `active`, `position`,
`global`, `deletable`, timestamps). Present when `included` contains `coordination_issue_priority` or is omitted.

viewpoint_count.description: Number of viewpoints attached to this coordination issue.

coordination_issue_bim_viewpoints.description:
Viewpoint mappings on this issue (`CoordinationIssueBimViewpointBlueprint` view `:normal`). Present when
`included` contains `coordination_issue_bim_viewpoints` or is omitted.

bim_viewpoint_id.description: Linked legacy BIM viewpoint id; null for Model Manager-backed mappings.

is_primary.description: Whether this mapping is the primary viewpoint for the issue.

source_file.description:
Resolved source file for the coordination issue. Returns the document name from
`document_container_metadata` when present, otherwise falls back to the BIM file.

id.description: Document container id or BIM file id.

linked_drawings.description:
Drawing revisions linked via published drawing markup (Coordination Issue pin), same semantics as REST v1
`view=extended`. Omitted unless `included` lists `linked_drawings` or `included` is omitted/empty.

url.description: Deep link to the drawing with focused markup element

drawing_markup_preview_images.description:
Preview images for published drawing markup layers. Omitted unless `included` lists
`drawing_markup_preview_images` or `included` is omitted/empty.

document_snapshots.description:
Document snapshots linked to this coordination issue (`CoordinationIssueDocumentSnapshotBlueprint`
view `:normal`). Present when `included` contains `document_snapshots` or is omitted.

items.description:
Rendered by `CoordinationIssueDocumentSnapshotBlueprint` view `:normal`. Represents a point-in-time
snapshot image of a document revision linked to a coordination issue. The `prostore_file` nested object
provides the file URL, name, content type, and viewable status.

document_container_id.description: The document container (folder) the source document belongs to.

document_name.description:
Human-readable name of the source document. Surfaced as the coordination issue's
source file for outside-workflow (document snapshot) issues. May be null for snapshots
created before this field existed.

document_revision_id.description: The document revision id from which the snapshot was taken.

document_revision_version_id.description: The specific document revision version id for this snapshot.

viewer_doc_id.description:
Identifier for the document viewer type associated with this snapshot. Used to determine
which viewer to use when displaying the document. May be null if not set.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created.

prostore_file.description:
Prostore file object (`ProstoreFileBlueprint` view `:normal_with_viewable`). Contains the snapshot
image file details including a signed URL, content type, and whether the file is viewable.

url.description: Signed download URL for the snapshot file.

content_type.description: MIME content type.

viewable.description: Whether this file has a viewable document representation.

permissions.description:
User permissions on this coordination issue. Returned only when `policy_context` is provided
in render options (typically by including the `X-Policy-Context` header or equivalent).

can_edit.description:
Whether the current user can edit (update) this coordination issue. Requires `update_coordination_issue`
permission from the policy AND the workflow (if present) to not be terminated or completed.

can_update_status.description:
Whether the current user can change the issue's status. Present only when the policy supports status
transitions; true when at least one status action is available and the workflow (if present) is active.

`422 Unprocessable Entity` with reason code `TEMPLATE_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the requested `template_id`

or with a template that is still active for the project, are unaffected.

Updates use `CoordinationIssues::Public::UpdateService`. `bim_file_id` is mapped to the internal file association.

get.description:
Returns a list of Coordination Issues that have associated workflow metadata.
Issues are filtered based on user visibility rules:
- Project Admins can see all workflow issues
- Issue creators can see issues they created
- Issue assignees can see issues assigned to them
- Workflow members can see issues for workflows they are part of
Include `permissions` in the query to get `can_edit` field for each issue.

x-changelog.summary: Added new Workflow Issues endpoint
x-changelog.description:
Added a new endpoint to list Coordination Issues that have associated workflow metadata.
Issues are filtered based on user visibility rules:
* Project Admins can see all workflow issues
* Issue creators can see issues they created
* Issue assignees can see issues assigned to them
* Workflow members can see issues for workflows they are part of

x-changelog.summary: Added permissions field to responses
x-changelog.description:
All Workflow Issues responses now include a `permissions` object with a `can_edit` boolean
indicating whether the current user can edit the issue. The value is `false` when the
associated workflow instance is terminated or completed.
