x-changelog.summary: Introduce GET Download All Response Attachments endpoint
x-changelog.description:
Introduces a dedicated endpoint to download all of a correspondence response's prostore-file attachments as a single zip.
Creates an asynchronous zip manifest and 302 redirects to its streaming URL. Returns 422 when fewer than 2 prostore-file attachments are present.
Replaces the legacy session-uuid based bulk-download mechanism for response attachments specifically; other tools using the shared helper are unaffected.

x-changelog.summary: Download All Response Attachments validates combined attachment count
x-changelog.description: The Download All Response Attachments endpoint now returns 422 when the response has fewer than 2 attachments in total (ProStore + PDM) or has no ProStore files to bundle, rather than counting ProStore-file attachments only. PDM attachments are counted toward the threshold but are still excluded from the resulting ProStore-only zip.

x-changelog.summary: Added a "tool_name" query parameter to the list endpoint.
x-changelog.description:
Added an optional `tool_name` query parameter that specifies which tool's read
permissions are used to authorize the request. Supported values are `admin` and
`timesheets`. When the parameter is omitted, the request is authorized against the
company `admin` tool, so callers without read access to the tool being checked
receive a `403 Forbidden`.

Example: `GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/custom_field_definitions?tool_name=timesheets`

x-changelog.summary: Added "home" as a supported value for the "tool_name" query parameter.
x-changelog.description:
Added `home` to the list of supported values for the `tool_name` query parameter on
`GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/custom_field_definitions`. When `tool_name=home`
is passed, the request is authorized against the caller's read access on the company
`home` tool. Supported values for `tool_name` are now `admin`, `home`, and `timesheets`.

Example: `GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/custom_field_definitions?tool_name=home`

schema.description: Array of Direct Cost Line Items

items.description: A condensed representation of a Direct Cost line item, returned by the list-all endpoint.

id.description: Unique identifier of the line item. Use as the {id} path parameter to retrieve, update, or delete this line item.

amount.description: Bottom-line monetary amount of the line item, as a decimal string. Equals quantity × unit_cost when extended_type is calculated, or the entered value when manual.

cost_code.description: Cost code assigned to the line item.

id.description: Unique identifier of the cost code.

full_code.description: Fully qualified cost code including any parent prefixes.

name.description: Display name of the cost code.

origin_id.description: Identifier of the cost code in the originating external system. Null when not synced.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the line item was created, in ISO 8601 format.

description.description: Free-text description of what the line item covers.

extended_amount.description: Bottom-line monetary amount of the line item, as a decimal string. Equals quantity × unit_cost when extended_type is calculated, or the entered value when manual. Currently identical to `amount` and `total_amount` (Direct Costs does not implement markups).

extended_type.description: How the line item amount is derived. `calculated` means amount = quantity × unit_cost; `manual` means the amount was entered directly.

holder.description: Parent record that owns this line item (the Direct Cost Item).

id.description: Unique identifier of the holder record (the Direct Cost Item ID).

holder_type.description: Class name of the holder record. Always DirectCost::Item for direct cost line items.

line_item_type.description: Cost category (line item type) assigned to this line item.

id.description: Unique identifier of the line item type.

base_type.description: Underlying category the line item type maps to.

code.description: Short code for the line item type.

name.description: Display name of the line item type.

origin_data.description: Opaque third-party payload stored with the line item type for external integrations.

position.description: Sort order of the line item within its parent Direct Cost Item.

project.description: Project the line item belongs to.

quantity.description: Quantity of the described item, as a decimal string. Multiplied by unit_cost when extended_type is calculated.

sub_job_id.description: Identifier of the sub job the line item's cost code belongs to. Present only when the cost code is billed to a sub job; otherwise omitted.

tax_code_id.description: Identifier of the tax code applied to this line item.

total_amount.description: Bottom-line monetary amount of the line item, as a decimal string. Equals quantity × unit_cost when extended_type is calculated, or the entered value when manual. Currently identical to `amount` and `extended_amount` (Direct Costs does not implement markups).

unit_cost.description: Cost per unit of the described item, as a decimal string.

uom.description: Unit of measure for the described item (for example, Lbs, cubic feet). Must be a value from the company's Units of Measure list.

get.description:
Return a list of all Direct Cost Line Items.

See [Filtering on List Actions](https://developers.procore.com/documentation/filtering-on-list-actions) for information on using the filtering capabilities provided by this endpoint.

parameters.name: filters[id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified IDs.

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

post.description:
Create a new Direct Cost Line Item.
This action does not support concurrent requests. If there is an attempt to create a Direct Cost Line Item that belongs to a Direct Cost which is being updated or deleted by another request, a 409 Conflict error will be returned.
Note: A budget line item will automatically be created for Non-budgeted line items for all new projects and for projects enabled with Non-Budgeted line item beta functionality

amount.description: Monetary amount for the line item. When extended_type is `calculated` it is derived from quantity × unit_cost; when `manual` it is the entered value.

wbs_code_id.description: ID of the WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) code to assign. Either wbs_code_id or cost_code_id + line_item_type_id is required when creating a line item; wbs_code_id takes precedence.

cost_code_id.description: ID of the cost code to assign to the line item. Ignored if wbs_code_id is supplied.

description.description: Free-text description of what the line item covers.

direct_cost_id.description: ID of the parent Direct Cost Item this line item belongs to.

extended_type.description: How the line item amount is derived. `calculated` means amount = quantity × unit_cost; `manual` means the amount is entered directly.

quantity.description: Quantity of the described item. Multiplied by unit_cost when extended_type is `calculated`.

line_item_type_id.description: ID of the line item type (cost category) to assign.

origin_data.description: Opaque third-party payload stored with the line item for external-system integrations. Not interpreted by Procore.

origin_id.description: Identifier of this line item in the originating external system; used to correlate synced records.

unit_cost.description: Cost per unit of the described item.

uom.description: Unit of measure for the described item. Must be a value from the company's Units of Measure list.
enum: Any value present in the Company list of Units of Measure

tax_code_id.description: ID of the tax code applied to this line item.

funding_rule_id.description: ID of the funding rule associated with this line item. Funding Sources must be enabled at the project level. The rule must be ACTIVE and its currency must match the direct cost currency. Pass null to disassociate an existing funding rule.

payload = "{\"line_item\":{\"amount\":1000,\"wbs_code_id\":1989,\"cost_code_id\":4682,\"description\":\"100' of Copper Piping\",\"direct_cost_id\":81753,\"extended_type\":\"manual\",\"quantity\":82.0201,\"line_item_type_id\":26943,\"origin_data\":\"OD-2398273424\",\"origin_id\":\"px-1990\",\"unit_cost\":12.03,\"uom\":\"cubic feet\",\"tax_code_id\":1,\"funding_rule_id\":12345}}"

headers = {
    'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN",
    'content-type': "application/json"
    }

conn.request("POST", "/rest/v1.0/projects/%7Bproject_id%7D/direct_costs/%7Bdirect_cost_id%7D/line_items", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

patch.description:
This endpoint creates or updates a batch of Direct Cost Line Items. For this endpoint either wbs_code_id or cost_code_id and line_item_type_id are required when creating a line item. If both wbs_code_id and cost_code_id are provided, the endpoint will use wbs_code_id.
This action does not support concurrent requests. If there is an attempt to update or create a Direct Cost Line Item that belongs to a Direct Cost which is being updated or deleted by another request, a 409 Conflict error will be returned.
See [Using Sync Actions](/documentation/using-sync-actions) for additional information.

schema.title: Direct Cost Line Item Sync Body

id.description: ID of an existing line item to update. Omit to create a new line item.

amount.description: Monetary amount for the line item. When extended_type is `calculated` it is derived from quantity × unit_cost; when `manual` it is the entered value.

wbs_code_id.description: ID of the WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) code to assign. Required when creating a line item if cost_code_id and line_item_type_id is not provided.

cost_code_id.description: ID of the cost code to assign to the line item. Required when creating a line item if wbs_code_id is not provided.

description.description: Free-text description of what the line item covers.

direct_cost_id.description: ID of the parent Direct Cost Item this line item belongs to. Required when creating a line item.

extended_type.description: How the line item amount is derived. `calculated` means amount = quantity × unit_cost; `manual` means the amount is entered directly.

quantity.description: Quantity of the described item. Multiplied by unit_cost when extended_type is `calculated`.

line_item_type_id.description: ID of the line item type (cost category) to assign. Required when creating a line item if wbs_code_id and cost_code_id are not provided.

origin_data.description: Opaque third-party payload stored with the line item for external-system integrations. Not interpreted by Procore.

origin_id.description: Identifier of this line item in the originating external system; used to correlate synced records.

unit_cost.description: Cost per unit of the described item.

uom.description: Unit of measure for the described item. Must be a value from the company's Units of Measure list.

funding_rule_id.description: ID of the funding rule associated with this line item. Funding Sources must be enabled at the project level. The rule must be ACTIVE and its currency must match the direct cost currency. Pass null to disassociate an existing funding rule.

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

headers = {
    'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN",
    'content-type': "application/json"
    }

conn.request("PATCH", "/rest/v1.0/projects/%7Bproject_id%7D/direct_costs/line_items/sync", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

get.description:
Returns the Document Collections for a Project, including the "All Documents" collection tagged `PDM:collection.all_documents`.

Supported filters: `id`, `ids`, `updated_at`.

Pass `view=ids_only` to receive an array of Document Collection ids instead of full objects.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Optional response view. Omit or pass `default` for full Document Collection objects. `ids_only` returns an array of ids and raises the `per_page` ceiling from 100 to 5000. The published `per_page` maximum reflects the default view.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Language for the response to be translated into

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
Filter which Document Collections are returned. `id` and `ids` match collection ids and are combined when both are sent. `updated_at` is an inclusive ISO-8601 range `start...end`.
Valid filterable fields are:
id,
ids,
updated_at

200.description: Returns Project Document Collections. The default view returns Document Collection objects; `view=ids_only` returns an array of Document Collection ids instead.

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next and last link

post.description:
Find or Create Document Markup Downloadable PDF. Starts processing to create a downloadable PDF with markup. When completed, the same request will include a download URL for the PDF.
item_id, item_type, and attachment_id paramters are the same parameters included in the URL when viewing the attachment in procore.
Example: app.procore.com/161072/project/submittal_logs/document_viewer?attachment_id=43&item_id=42&item_type=SubmittalLog&project_id=161072

parameters.name: version_datetime
parameters.description: Optional ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC) used to retrieve the state of the document and its markup as of that point in time. Omit to retrieve the current version.

project_id.description: ID of the project that owns the item and its attachment.

item_id.description: The ID of the parent item this document belongs to

item_type.description: The type of the parent item this document belongs to (eg SubmittalLog)

attachment_id.description: ID of the ProstoreFile (attachment) being marked up. Matches the `attachment_id` shown in the document viewer URL.

200.description: Document Markup Downloadable PDF completed and download URL is included in the response.

id.description: ID of the Document Markup Downloadable PDF record.

error_message.description: Message describing a processing failure. Null for a completed PDF.

status.description: Processing state of the Downloadable PDF; always `completed` for this response.

url.description: Temporary download URL for the completed marked-up PDF. Fetch this URL to download the file.

pusher_message_name.description: Name of the Pusher message broadcast when this PDF's status changes. Subscribe to it to receive real-time processing updates.

id.description: ID of the Document Markup Downloadable PDF record.

error_message.description: Message describing a processing failure. Null while processing.

By default the response is a 302 redirect to a presigned ZIP URL in the Location header. Pass `no_redirect=true` to receive 200 `{ data: { download_url, url_expires_at } }` instead.

Document revisions without a file are silently omitted from the ZIP, so the archive may contain fewer files than IDs requested. `download_all_document_revisions` is currently disabled — an empty `document_revision_ids` list returns 400. At most 300 unique document revision IDs may be requested.

workflow.description: Workflow integration information for this document revision. Inspect `workflow.status` to determine whether the workflow is currently active or has a request in flight against the external workflow service. The blocking set used by the server for recycle is `created`, `creation_requested`, and `termination_requested`; see `WorkflowIntegrationInfoDtoV1_0.status` for full semantics.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the workflow integration on this document revision. The server blocks recycle (and other writes that would orphan an in-flight external workflow instance) when status is `created`, `creation_requested`, or `termination_requested`. Recycle is permitted when status is absent, `not_created`, `failed`, `ended`, `terminated`, or `termination_failed`. Note that `created` alone is the only status that indicates a workflow is _currently active_ — `creation_requested` and `termination_requested` are transitional states where a request is in flight against the external workflow service, and clients must treat them as blocking even though the workflow is not yet active.

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.description:
Return immediate accessible children for a specific company folder as a single mixed collection of folders and files. Descendants beyond one level are not included, and any `filters[...]` parameters apply to those immediate children.
With `include_descendants=true` and at least one `filters[...]` parameter, the endpoint searches this folder's entire subtree instead. It never widens beyond the addressed folder, so matches elsewhere in the company are not returned; use the company root-children endpoint for that. Recycle bin content is excluded unless `filters[is_in_recycle_bin]` is provided.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Response projection. Supports legacy `web_normal` requests for compatibility with v1 folder-show flows. `normal` and `web_normal` include `has_private_ancestor`; `sync_compact` omits it. `web_extended` returns everything `web_normal` returns plus a `file` object on file rows with `file_type`, `current_version` (`id`, `number`, `size`, `created_at`, `notes`), `checked_out_by` and `checked_out_until`; folder rows return `file: null`.

parameters.name: show_latest_file_version_only
parameters.description: Return only the latest file version per file.

parameters.name: exclude_folders
parameters.description: Exclude child folders from the response.

parameters.name: exclude_files
parameters.description: Exclude child files from the response.

parameters.name: include_descendants
parameters.description:
Search the addressed folder's entire subtree instead of only its immediate children. On a root-children endpoint the addressed folder is the root, so this spans the whole Documents tool; on a nested folder endpoint it spans only that folder's subtree.
Only takes effect alongside at least one `filters[...]` parameter; supplied on its own, the response remains the immediate children. Filters supplied without this parameter continue to apply to the immediate children only, so the default behavior of the endpoint is unchanged.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort immediate folder children by one or more comma-separated terms in left-to-right priority order. Supported fields are `updated_at`, `name`, `document_type`, `created_at`, and `created_by`. Prefix a term with `-` for descending order; no prefix means ascending. For example, `document_type,-created_at,name`. Leading or interior blank terms and malformed direction prefixes return 400. Native parsing ignores trailing commas; for duplicate fields, the first occurrence keeps its priority and the last occurrence sets direction. When omitted or blank, folders are returned first in natural-name order.

parameters.name: filters[created_by_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) created by the specified User IDs

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.description:
Returns the immediate accessible children of the company root folder as a single mixed collection of folders and files (descendants beyond one level are not included). Any `filters[...]` parameters apply to those immediate children.
With `include_descendants=true` and at least one `filters[...]` parameter, the endpoint instead searches the entire company Documents tool and returns every accessible folder and file matching all provided filters, regardless of depth in the folder tree. `sort`, `exclude_folders`, `exclude_files`, and pagination apply in both modes. When searching descendants, recycle bin content is excluded unless `filters[is_in_recycle_bin]` is provided, and `filters[private]` matches only items explicitly marked private (items inheriting privacy from a parent folder are not matched).
Results are permission-filtered for every user: an item is returned only when it and all of its ancestors are accessible. Schedules content requires the "Can See Schedule" permission and recycle bin content requires the "See Recycle Bin" permission; without them, those folders and everything beneath them are omitted. The `Total` header is exact and pagination is uncapped in both modes.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Response projection. Supports legacy `web_normal` requests for compatibility with v1 folder-index flows. `normal` and `web_normal` include `has_private_ancestor`; `sync_compact` omits it. `web_extended` returns everything `web_normal` returns plus a `file` object on file rows with `file_type`, `current_version` (`id`, `number`, `size`, `created_at`, `notes`), `checked_out_by` and `checked_out_until`; folder rows return `file: null`.

parameters.description: Exclude child folders from the response.

parameters.name: exclude_files

parameters.name: include_descendants
parameters.description:
Search the addressed folder's entire subtree instead of only its immediate children. On a root-children endpoint the addressed folder is the root, so this spans the whole Documents tool; on a nested folder endpoint it spans only that folder's subtree.
Only takes effect alongside at least one `filters[...]` parameter; supplied on its own, the response remains the immediate children. Filters supplied without this parameter continue to apply to the immediate children only, so the default behavior of the endpoint is unchanged.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort immediate folder children by one or more comma-separated terms in left-to-right priority order. Supported fields are `updated_at`, `name`, `document_type`, `created_at`, and `created_by`. Prefix a term with `-` for descending order; no prefix means ascending. For example, `document_type,-created_at,name`. Leading or interior blank terms and malformed direction prefixes return 400. Native parsing ignores trailing commas; for duplicate fields, the first occurrence keeps its priority and the last occurrence sets direction. When omitted or blank, folders are returned first in natural-name order.

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.description:
Returns the immediate accessible children of the project root folder as a single mixed collection of folders and files, scoped under a company (descendants beyond one level are not included). Any `filters[...]` parameters apply to those immediate children.
With `include_descendants=true` and at least one `filters[...]` parameter, the endpoint instead searches the entire project Documents tool and returns every accessible folder and file matching all provided filters, regardless of depth in the folder tree. `sort`, `exclude_folders`, `exclude_files`, and pagination apply in both modes. When searching descendants, recycle bin content is excluded unless `filters[is_in_recycle_bin]` is provided, and `filters[private]` matches only items explicitly marked private (items inheriting privacy from a parent folder are not matched).
Results are permission-filtered for every user: an item is returned only when it and all of its ancestors are accessible. Schedules content requires the "Can See Schedule" permission and recycle bin content requires the "See Recycle Bin" permission; without them, those folders and everything beneath them are omitted. The `Total` header is exact and pagination is uncapped in both modes.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Response projection. Supports legacy `web_normal` requests for compatibility with v1 folder-index flows. `normal` and `web_normal` include `has_private_ancestor`; `sync_compact` omits it. `web_extended` returns everything `web_normal` returns plus a `file` object on file rows with `file_type`, `current_version` (`id`, `number`, `size`, `created_at`, `notes`), `checked_out_by` and `checked_out_until`; folder rows return `file: null`.

parameters.name: show_latest_file_version_only
parameters.description: Return only the latest file version per file.

parameters.name: exclude_folders
parameters.description: Exclude child folders from the response.

parameters.name: exclude_files
parameters.description: Exclude child files from the response.

parameters.name: include_descendants
parameters.description:
Search the addressed folder's entire subtree instead of only its immediate children. On a root-children endpoint the addressed folder is the root, so this spans the whole Documents tool; on a nested folder endpoint it spans only that folder's subtree.
Only takes effect alongside at least one `filters[...]` parameter; supplied on its own, the response remains the immediate children. Filters supplied without this parameter continue to apply to the immediate children only, so the default behavior of the endpoint is unchanged.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort immediate folder children by one or more comma-separated terms in left-to-right priority order. Supported fields are `updated_at`, `name`, `document_type`, `created_at`, and `created_by`. Prefix a term with `-` for descending order; no prefix means ascending. For example, `document_type,-created_at,name`. Leading or interior blank terms and malformed direction prefixes return 400. Native parsing ignores trailing commas; for duplicate fields, the first occurrence keeps its priority and the last occurrence sets direction. When omitted or blank, folders are returned first in natural-name order.

Unknown or unsupported sort keys (including invalid custom field keys) are ignored; the endpoint falls back to the default sort order and returns HTTP 200. `number` and `revision` are accepted as legacy aliases of `drawing_number` and `revision_number`.

x-changelog.summary: Added viewer_experience to the web index drawing revisions response and filter
x-changelog.description:
The list drawing revisions endpoint now includes `viewer_experience` (`legacy` or
`unified`) in the `view=web_index` response payload, and accepts
`filters[viewer_experience]` to return only revisions confirmed under that viewer
experience. The filter composes with `filters[deleted]=only` so the Recycle Bin can

or `unified` is ignored, matching the other list filters.

x-changelog.description:

(`data_type` and `value`) in the `view=web_index` response payload, instead of an
empty object. This is additive and does not change any existing fields.

x-changelog.summary: Sheet number support for drawing revisions APIs
x-changelog.description: Drawing revisions payloads now include `sheet_number` and canonical `drawing_number` alongside display-formatted `number` for sheet-aware identification. For multi-sheet records, clients should treat `(drawing_number, sheet_number)` as the stable identity tuple instead of parsing presentation `number` values. Enablement is managed internally by the Drawings development team. Please contact your Procore Account Manager or Support to request enablement. When not enabled, endpoints keep current behavior.

x-changelog.summary: Added sort parameter to list drawing revisions endpoint
x-changelog.description:

by any table column (drawing_number, title, drawing_date, received_date, status, revision_number,
drawing_set, sheet_number, obsolete) and by custom fields using the `custom_field_<id>` key format.
Prefix the sort key with `-` for descending order. Unknown sort keys return HTTP 400.

x-changelog.summary: Relaxed invalid sort handling for drawing revisions list endpoint
x-changelog.description:

standard keys and invalid custom field sort keys.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

post.summary: Create a markup on a proposal
post.description:
Returns 201 with the created markup.
An ITERATIVE markup always compounds all preceding markups; compound_all is set implicitly and
compound_with is not allowed. Only one ITERATIVE markup can exist per proposal, and it must be POST_TAX.
LEGACY_OVERHEAD and LEGACY_DISCOUNT must be PRE_TAX; creating one re-enables and updates the existing
disabled legacy markup when present. Creating a LEGACY_OVERHEAD sets an existing LEGACY_DISCOUNT's
compound_with to the overhead, and vice versa. Only markups from the same stage, except
ITERATIVE, can be referenced in compound_with.

x-changelog.summary: Introduced Public API endpoints for External RFIs
x-changelog.description:
Introduced the following Public API endpoints for External RFIs:
- GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/external_rfis (List External RFIs)
- GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/external_rfis/{id} (Show External RFI)
- GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/external_rfis/{id}/revisions (List External RFI Revisions)
- PATCH /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/external_rfis/{id}/linked_local_rfis (Update Linked Local RFIs for an External RFI)
- GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/external_rfis/{id}/download_external_rfi_and_responses_attachments (Download External RFI and Responses Attachments)
- GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/external_rfis/{external_rfi_id}/advanced_exports (Show Advanced Export Options for External RFI)
- GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/external_rfis/{external_rfi_id}/external_rfi_pdf_exports/{id}/download (Download External RFI PDF Export)

x-changelog.summary: Documented recycled External RFI status values
x-changelog.description: The List External RFIs response documentation now includes the existing `_recycled` status variants returned when an upstream RFI is in the recycle bin. Generated clients should handle these variants, and integrations should tolerate unknown future status values.

x-changelog.summary: Corrected the documented External RFI list response
x-changelog.description: The List External RFIs response documentation now matches the existing runtime payload for synchronization state, origin RFI/project/company IDs, project connection IDs, linked local RFIs, cross-account origin state, and the origin RFI URL. Contact objects now list only the `id` and `name` fields returned by the API. Generated clients should handle the newly documented `private` synchronization state.

get.summary: Return a list of all External Submittals.
get.description: Return a list of all External Submittals for the specified project. External Submittals are copies of submittals from connected upstream projects, accessible via Connections Manager.

schema.description: A Connected Submittal is a read-only downstream projection of an upstream submittal shared across a connected-project boundary. The list endpoint returns an array of these objects under `data` (minimal fields); the show endpoint returns a single object under `data` with the additional extended-only fields (`has_revisions`, `connected_distributed_submittals`, `connected_submittal_connection_detail`, `linked_drawings`, `cover_sheet`, `project_connection`).

id.description: Unique identifier of the connected submittal. Use as the {id} path parameter for GET /connected_submittals/{id}, GET /connected_submittals/{id}/revisions, and PATCH /connected_submittals/{id}/linked_local_submittals.

number.description: Display number of the connected submittal. When spec-section numbering is enabled for the project, this is the spec-section-prefixed number.

title.description: Title of the connected submittal. May be null if the upstream submittal has no title.

description.description: Free-text description of the connected submittal. May be null.

status.description: Downstream projection status of the connected submittal, derived from the upstream source. This is not a submittal log status. `open` is used when the upstream submittal is not closed and has never been distributed; `reopened` is used when it is not closed and was previously distributed. `outdated` is used when the upstream submittal has been superseded by a newer revision, and when it has moved into the Draft status - a draft upstream submittal stops syncing content downstream and retains its last synced values.

translated_status.description: Localized, human-readable label for the downstream `status`, suitable for display.

revision.description: Revision label of the connected submittal. May be null.

current_revision.description: Whether this record is the current revision of the connected submittal.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the connected submittal projection was created, in ISO 8601 format.

last_updated_at.description: Timestamp when the connected submittal projection was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the connected submittal was soft-deleted, in ISO 8601 format. Null when the record is not deleted.

for_record_only.description: Whether the submittal is marked for record only (no workflow response required).

private.description: Whether the submittal is private and visible only to permitted users.

buffer_time.description: Buffer time, in days, configured for the submittal schedule. Null when not set.

lead_time.description: Lead time, in days, for the submittal. Null when not set.

prepare_time.description: Preparation time, in days, for the submittal. Null when not set.

design_team_review_time.description: Design team review time, in days. Null when not set.

internal_review_time.description: Internal review time, in days. Null when not set.

revision_source_connected_submittal_id.description: ID of the connected submittal that is the source revision for this record. Null when this record is the original revision.

connection_status.description: Whether the connected submittal's upstream project connection is currently syncing (`connected`) or not (`disconnected`).

actual_delivery_date.description: Actual delivery date, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not set.

confirmed_delivery_date.description: Confirmed delivery date, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not set.

distributed_at.description: Date the submittal was distributed, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not distributed.

due_date.description: Due date for the submittal, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not set.

issue_date.description: Issue date for the submittal, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not set.

received_date.description: Date the submittal was received, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not set.

required_on_site_date.description: Required-on-site date for the submittal, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not set.

submit_by.description: Submit-by date for the submittal, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not set.

type.description: Submittal type of the connected submittal. Null when no type is assigned.

translated_name.description: Localized, human-readable name of the submittal type.

responsible_contractor.description: Vendor responsible for the connected submittal. Null when none is assigned.

id.description: Identifier of the responsible contractor vendor.

name.description: Name of the responsible contractor vendor.

created_by.description: Contact who created the upstream submittal.

login_information_id.description: Identifier of the associated login information (user), when the contact maps to a Procore user. Null otherwise.

schema.description: A Connected Submittal is a read-only downstream projection of an upstream submittal shared across a connected-project boundary. The list endpoint returns an array of these objects under `data` (minimal fields); the show endpoint returns a single object under `data` with the additional extended-only fields (`has_revisions`, `connected_distributed_submittals`, `connected_submittal_connection_detail`, `linked_drawings`, `cover_sheet`, `project_connection`).

id.description: Unique identifier of the connected submittal. Use as the {id} path parameter for GET /connected_submittals/{id}, GET /connected_submittals/{id}/revisions, and PATCH /connected_submittals/{id}/linked_local_submittals.

number.description: Display number of the connected submittal. When spec-section numbering is enabled for the project, this is the spec-section-prefixed number.

title.description: Title of the connected submittal. May be null if the upstream submittal has no title.

description.description: Free-text description of the connected submittal. May be null.

status.description: Downstream projection status of the connected submittal, derived from the upstream source. This is not a submittal log status. `open` is used when the upstream submittal is not closed and has never been distributed; `reopened` is used when it is not closed and was previously distributed. `outdated` is used when the upstream submittal has been superseded by a newer revision, and when it has moved into the Draft status - a draft upstream submittal stops syncing content downstream and retains its last synced values.

translated_status.description: Localized, human-readable label for the downstream `status`, suitable for display.

revision.description: Revision label of the connected submittal. May be null.

current_revision.description: Whether this record is the current revision of the connected submittal.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the connected submittal projection was created, in ISO 8601 format.

last_updated_at.description: Timestamp when the connected submittal projection was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the connected submittal was soft-deleted, in ISO 8601 format. Null when the record is not deleted.

for_record_only.description: Whether the submittal is marked for record only (no workflow response required).

private.description: Whether the submittal is private and visible only to permitted users.

buffer_time.description: Buffer time, in days, configured for the submittal schedule. Null when not set.

lead_time.description: Lead time, in days, for the submittal. Null when not set.

prepare_time.description: Preparation time, in days, for the submittal. Null when not set.

design_team_review_time.description: Design team review time, in days. Null when not set.

internal_review_time.description: Internal review time, in days. Null when not set.

revision_source_connected_submittal_id.description: ID of the connected submittal that is the source revision for this record. Null when this record is the original revision.

connection_status.description: Whether the connected submittal's upstream project connection is currently syncing (`connected`) or not (`disconnected`).

actual_delivery_date.description: Actual delivery date, rendered at noon in the project time zone. Null when not set.

get.description: Retrieves a list of markups associated with the specified holder.  This endpoint supports the Contract and Potential Change Order tools.  Access requires the user to have admin permissions for the relevant tool.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: When set to `with_erp_data`, includes the `prime_line_item_id` field in the response.

schema.description: Array of Markups

applies_to_all.description: Indicates if the markup applies to all change management items within the holder.

compound.description: Details of the compound calculations for the markup.

selections.description: Specifies which existing markups to include in the calculation when 'selective' compounding is chosen.

type.description:
Type of calculation for the markup:
- **Basic Calculation (null):** Percentage is multiplied by the line items that meet the application criteria.
- **Compounds all Above (above):** Percentage is multiplied by the line items that meet the application criteria and all preceding markups in the markup table.
- **Selective Compounding (selective):** Percentage is multiplied by the line items that meet the application criteria and any individually selected markups.
- **Iterative Calculation or Margin (margin):** Percentage is multiplied by the line item total, including all markups.

compounds_markups_above.description: When true, the markup percentage is calculated on the holder's subtotal plus all markups positioned above it (by `position`); when false, it is calculated on the subtotal alone. This is the legacy boolean form of the `compound.type` "above" calculation.

holder_id.description: Unique identifier for the markup holder.

line_item_type_ids.description: Identifiers of the line item types the markup applies to. Empty when the markup is not restricted to specific line item types.

markup_conditions.description: Conditions that determine how the markup will be applied to change management items within the holder.

parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort direction. Use the value to sort ascending, or prefix with a hyphen (e.g. -name) to sort descending.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: When true, returns both active and inactive harm sources. When omitted or false, returns only active harm sources.

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

schema.description: Array of Harm Sources

id.description: Unique identifier of the harm source.

name.description: Display name of the harm source, translated to the requested locale. For the untranslated original name, see name_key.

name_key.description: Untranslated original name of the harm source. Use for programmatic matching when locale-independent identification is needed.

active.description: Whether this harm source is active and available for selection when recording incidents.

global.description: Whether this harm source is a Procore-provided default. Global harm sources cannot be renamed or deleted.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this harm source was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this harm source was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

See [Filtering on List Actions](https://developers.procore.com/documentation/filtering-on-list-actions) for information on using the filtering capabilities provided by this endpoint.

parameters.name: image_category_id
parameters.description: Optional. ID of the image category to filter the images by.

parameters.name: filters[log_date]
parameters.description: Date of Photos added to the Daily Log in the format "YYYY-MM-DD", or a range of dates in the format "YYYY-MM-DD...YYYY-MM-DD".

parameters.name: filters[private]
parameters.description: If true, returns only item(s) with a `private` status.

parameters.name: filters[starred]
parameters.description: If true, returns only item(s) with a `starred` status. This will be ignored for users without permission to star photos, returning the unfiltered list rather than an error.

parameters.name: filters[location_id]
parameters.description: Location ID. Returns item(s) with the specified Location ID or a range of Location IDs.

parameters.name: filters[trade_ids]
parameters.description: Array of Trade IDs. Returns item(s) with the specified Trade IDs.

parameters.name: filters[projection]
parameters.description: Return items with the specified projection type.

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[uploader_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) uploaded by the specified User IDs

parameters.name: filters[id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified IDs.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort by. If the field is passed with a - (EX: -created_at) it is sorted in reverse order

parameters.name: serializer_view
parameters.description:
The data set that should be returned from the serializer.
The normal view includes default fields, plus links, comments_count, trades.
The android view includes default fields, plus trades, comments.
The mobile view include default fields, plus log_date, trades, comments.
The mobile_feed view includes default fields, plus comments.
The prostore_file view includes default fields, plus images.
The ids_only view does not include default fields, response returns strictly an array of image ids.
Default view is normal.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of incidents for the specified project, ordered by descending number by default. Each incident includes summary information, associated records count, and linked resources (location, contributing factors, assignees). Supports filtering by date, location, status, root cause fields, recordable flag, visible record type, and full-text search across title, creator, witness statements, actions, and related fields. Use filters[query] for keyword search.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of items returned per page (Min: 1, Max: 1000). Defaults to 1000 when parameter is not provided.

parameters.name: filters[id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified IDs.

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[event_date]
parameters.description: Returns item(s) with an event date within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.

parameters.name: filters[location_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified Location IDs.

parameters.name: filters[status]
parameters.description: Returns item(s) matching the specified status value.

parameters.name: filters[contributing_behavior_id]
parameters.description: Contributing Behavior ID. Returns item(s) with the specified Contributing Behavior ID.

parameters.name: filters[contributing_condition_id]
parameters.description: Contributing Condition ID. Returns item(s) with the specified Contributing Condition ID.

parameters.name: filters[hazard_id]
parameters.description: Hazard ID. Returns item(s) with the specified Hazard ID.

parameters.name: filters[time_unknown]
parameters.description: If true, returns item(s) where the time of Incident occurrence is unknown.

parameters.name: filters[with_record_types]
parameters.description: Returns incidents containing at least one record of a selected type that the current user can view. Multiple values use OR semantics.

items.description: Incident record type key as stored on the server. Pass this value in the filters[with_record_types] parameter when listing incidents.

parameters.name: filters[has_root_cause_analysis]
parameters.description: If true, returns only Incidents that have a Root Cause Analysis. If false, returns only Incidents that do not have one. Omit the parameter to return both.

parameters.name: filters[custom_status_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified Custom Status IDs

parameters.name: filters[type_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with a specific Type ID or a range of Type IDs.

parameters.name: filters[assignee_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with a specific Assignee ID or a range of Assignee IDs.

parameters.name: filters[query]
parameters.description: Full-text search across incident title, creator name, witness statements, action descriptions, action types, contributing behaviors, contributing conditions, hazards, and location names. Returns incidents where any of these fields contain the query string.

post.description: Creates a new incident in the specified project. Requires at minimum a title and event_date. Optionally attach associated records (injuries, near_misses, environmentals, property_damages) in a single request. Pass run_configurable_validations=true to enforce any custom validation rules configured for the Incidents tool. The operation is idempotent via UUID-based deduplication.

parameters.name: run_configurable_validations
parameters.description:
Whether or not Configurable validations from the Incident/Injury Configurable Field Set should be run (default: false).
See (https://developers.procore.com/reference/configurable-field-sets#list-project-configurable-field-sets) for a list of Configurable validations enabled on this project.

description.example: Can of gasoline tipped over near drying cement.

event_date.description: Iso8601 datetime of Incident occurrence. If time is unknown, send in the date at 0:00 project time converted to UTC.

type_id.description: The ID of the Incident Type. Defaults to the company's General type if not provided. The type must be active.

custom_status_id.description: The ID of the Custom Status. Mutually exclusive with the status field — setting one sets the other. Not updatable if the Incident has a workflows instance.

assignee_ids.description: An array of Login Information IDs to assign to the Incident. Assignees gain visibility into the Incident and its related records. Not updatable if the Incident has a workflows instance.

distribution_member_ids.description: An Array of the IDs of the Distribution Members (Not updatable if an incident has a workflows instance)

private.description: Indicates whether an Incident is private

recordable.description: Indicates whether an Incident is recordable

status.description: Status (Not updatable if an incident has a workflows instance)

time_unknown.description: Indicates that the time of the Incident occurrence is unknown

contributing_behavior_id.description: The ID of a Contributing Behavior

contributing_condition_id.description: The ID of a Contributing Condition

location_id.description: The ID of a Location

environmental_type_id.description: The ID of the Environmental Type

description.description: Description of event in Rich Text format

estimated_cost_impact.description: Estimated cost impact of the record

quantity_unit_of_measure.description: Unit of measure for the "quantity" field

affected_company_id.description: The ID of the Affected Company

managed_equipment_id.description: The ID of the Managed Equipment

work_activity_id.description: The ID of the Work Activity

custom_field_%{custom_field_definition_i.description:
Value of the custom field. The data type of the value passed in corresponds with the data_type of the Custom Field Definition.

patch.description: Restores the specified incident from the recycle bin, making it active again. The incident and all its associated records (injuries, near_misses, attachments, etc.) are recovered. Returns 200 OK on success with the incident's ID and number. Pass renumber as true to give the restored incident the next available number instead of its original one, for example when an active incident already uses it.

renumber.description: When true, the restored incident is assigned the next available incident number for the project, even if its original number is not in use. When false or omitted, the original number is kept.

number.description: The incident's number after the restore

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of injury records for the specified project, optionally scoped to a single incident via incident_id. Each injury includes affliction details, affected person, body parts, medical treatment information, and work impact metrics. By default sorted by descending full_number (incident.number). Supports filtering by affected party, body part, affliction type, filing type, harm source, and full-text search.

NOTE: The afflictions and affected_body_part keys are deprecated. Please disregard and use the affected_body_parts and affliction_type keys as documented below.

parameters.name: incident_id
parameters.description: Optional incident ID to scope results. When provided, returns only injury records belonging to the specified incident. Omit to retrieve injuries across all incidents in the project.

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[affected_company_id]

parameters.name: filters[harm_source_id]
parameters.description: Array of Harm Source IDs. Returns item(s) with the specified Harm Source IDs.

parameters.name: filters[work_activity_id]

parameters.name: filters[affected_body_part]

Optionally specify affliction details (affliction_type_id, body_part_ids), affected person information, medical treatment details, and work impact metrics. See [Working with Daily Logs](https://developers.procore.com/documentation/daily-logs) for information on filtering the response using the log\_date, start\_date, and end\_date parameters. x-changelog.summary: Updated checklist users endpoint with signatory filters and inspection scoping
x-changelog.description:
Added `filters[potential_signatory]` and optional `filters[inspection_id]`
to the checklist users endpoint.

New response fields:
- `potential_signatory`: always returned; true when the user is eligible to sign.
- `potential_signatory_as_creator`: only returned when `filters[inspection_id]` is
  omitted, for client-side creator scoping.
- `potential_signatory_as_assignee`: only returned when `filters[inspection_id]` is
  omitted, for client-side assignee scoping.

Behavior notes:
- When `filters[inspection_id]` is provided, signatory eligibility is evaluated
  in that inspection's scope. Closed inspections return no eligible signatories.
- An unknown `filters[inspection_id]` falls back to project-wide evaluation.
- Existing behavior is preserved when neither filter is provided.

x-changelog.summary: Optional sort for workflow activity histories index
x-changelog.description:
List accepts an optional `sort` query parameter. Supported values are
`created_at` and `-created_at`. When omitted, ordering is unchanged
(ascending primary key via pagination defaults). Use `sort=-created_at`
for newest-first pages when loading history incrementally.

x-changelog.summary: Locate activity histories by workflowed object on index and show
x-changelog.description:
List and show now accept `filters[workflowed_object_type]` and
`filters[workflowed_object_id]` as an alternative to `workflow_instance_id`.
Existing callers that pass `workflow_instance_id` are unchanged; when that
parameter is present it takes precedence. Change-order object types also
require `project_id`. Create still requires `workflow_instance_id`.

post.summary: Create A Manual Forecast Line Item
post.description:
Create a manual forecast line item for a budget line item.

When `async: true` and Budget Columns 2.0 is enabled, the response is `202 Accepted` with a `receipt_id`.
When `async: false` (default) or Budget Columns 2.0 is disabled, the response is `201 Created`.

async.description: Request asynchronous processing. When `true`, Budget Columns 2.0 must be enabled or the request will return `422`. On success returns `202 Accepted` with a `receipt_id`.

budget_line_item_id.description: Identifier of the parent budget line item. NOTE - budget line item id or wbs code id is required

wbs_code_id.description: Wbs code id of the parent budget line item. NOTE - budget line item id or wbs code id is required

description.description: Free-text label for the forecast line item, typically the resource or role being forecast.

quantity.description: Number of units being forecast, expressed in the given unit of measure (uom).

uom.description: Unit of measure for the forecast quantity (for example, months or weeks).

unit_cost.description: Cost per unit. Multiplied by quantity to produce amount.

amount.description: Total forecast amount (quantity multiplied by unit_cost).

id.description: Unique identifier for this manual forecast line item. Use as the {id} path parameter to update or delete the record via /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/manual_forecast_line_items/{id}.

budget_line_item_id.description: ID of the budget line item this manual forecast line item forecasts against.

wbs_code_id.description: ID of the WBS (work breakdown structure) code associated with the parent budget line item.

patch.summary: Updates a material requirements document header.
patch.description:
Updates header fields such as title, notes, and status on the material requirements document.
Use status transitions to move the document through its workflow states.
Send `void` as true to void the document instead, which sets the quantity required on every line item to 0.
Voiding is admin only, applies to Final documents only, and applies `notes` to the document note when provided.

requestBody.description: The patch request containing the updates.

value.description:
Value rules:

- TEXT: Any string
- BOOLEAN: "true" / "false"
- DATE: "YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g. "2026-03-02"). Send null or "" to clear.
- NUMBER: Numeric string (e.g. "42", "3.14"). Stored as-is.
- LOCATION: Any string (e.g. a location name or ID)
- HIDDEN: Any string
- PERSON: A valid long user/person ID as string (e.g. "12345"). Send null, "", or "0" to clear.

properties_to_add.description: Collection of resource parameters to add to the document header.

value.description:
Value rules:

- TEXT: Any string
- BOOLEAN: "true" / "false"
- DATE: "YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g. "2026-03-02"). Send null or "" to clear.
- NUMBER: Numeric string (e.g. "42", "3.14"). Stored as-is.
- LOCATION: Any string (e.g. a location name or ID)
- HIDDEN: Any string
- PERSON: A valid long user/person ID as string (e.g. "12345"). Send null, "", or "0" to clear.

properties_to_update.description: Collection of resource parameters to update in the document header.

value.description:
Value rules:

- TEXT: Any string
- BOOLEAN: "true" / "false"
- DATE: "YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g. "2026-03-02"). Send null or "" to clear.
- NUMBER: Numeric string (e.g. "42", "3.14"). Stored as-is.
- LOCATION: Any string (e.g. a location name or ID)
- HIDDEN: Any string
- PERSON: A valid long user/person ID as string (e.g. "12345"). Send null, "", or "0" to clear.

properties_to_delete.description: Collection of resource parameters to delete from the document header.

notes.description: Notes associated with the document header.

scope_start_at.description: Start date and time for scope. Clears header field if value is an empty string or "0001-01-01T00:00:00.0000000+00:00".

scope_end_at.description: End date and time for the scope. Clears header field if value is an empty string or "0001-01-01T00:00:00.0000000+00:00".

required_on_site_date.description: Date and time by which the item is required to be on site.

void.description:
When true, voids the document by setting the quantity required on every line item to 0.
Only admin users can void, and only Final documents are eligible.
When `notes` is also supplied it is applied to the document note as part of the void.

patch.description:
Creates or updates material requirements headers identified using either ids or origin_ids.
The maximum number of entities per request is 1000. Exceeding this limit will result in a 413 response.
See https://developers.procore.com/documentation/using-sync-actions for more information.

id.description: The Procore id of the resource. This should only be set when updating existing resources.

origin_id.description: The origin id of the resource. If an entry is missing both id and origin_id, then that entry will always be interpreted as an insert.

origin_data.description: The origin data for the resource. Procore does not interpret this value.

name.description: The name of this document header.

description.description: The description of this document header.

notes.description: Additional Notes about this document header.

scope_start_at.description:
The start timestamp of the scope for this document header.
Must be earlier than or equal to scope_end_at.

scope_end_at.description:
The end timestamp of the scope for this document header.

For the given set of material GUIDs, refreshes all calculated/cached data. The refresh covers calculations related to the material itself as well as any document the material is referenced by.
This operation is asynchronous: the refreshed calculations will not be immediately available or visible to subsequent reads.

get.description:
Returns a collection of Observation Items.
See [Filtering on List Actions](https://developers.procore.com/documentation/filtering-on-list-actions) for information on using the filtering capabilities provided by this endpoint.

parameters.name: filters[assignee_company_id]
parameters.description: Array of Vendor IDs. Returns item(s) where any assignee is associated to one of the specified Vendors.

parameters.name: filters[checklist_list_id]
parameters.description: Array of Checklist List IDs. Return item(s) associated with the specified Checklist List IDs.

parameters.name: filters[created_by_id]
parameters.description: Returns item(s) created by the specified User IDs.

parameters.name: filters[id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified IDs.

parameters.name: filters[location_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified Location IDs.

parameters.name: filters[assignee_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) where any assignee is one of the specified User IDs. An Observation matches when the User appears anywhere in its `assignees` list.

parameters.name: filters[checklist_item_id]
parameters.description: Return Observations(s) originating from the specified Checklist Item(s).

parameters.name: filters[custom_fields]
parameters.description: Return Observation Items whose custom field values match the supplied JSON object. The object is keyed by custom field definition ID. Matching uses JSONB containment, so only item(s) containing all of the supplied key/value pairs are returned.

schema.description: JSON object where each key is a custom field definition ID

parameters.name: filters[priority]
parameters.description:
Return only Observation Items at the given priorities. Values are
case-sensitive and match the `priority` field on the Observation.
Comma-separate values to match several priorities, e.g.
`filters[priority]=High,Urgent`.

parameters.name: filters[search]
parameters.description: Return item(s) matching the specified Search query.

parameters.name: filters[status]
parameters.description:
Return only Observation Items in the given lifecycle states. Statuses are
supplied as their integer codes:
```
  0: Initiated
  1: Ready For Review
  2: Not Accepted
  3: Closed
  4: Draft
```
Comma-separate values to match several states, e.g. `filters[status]=0,1`.
`4` (Draft) only matches Observations governed by a workflow that has not yet
been started.

parameters.name: filters[type_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified Observation Type ID.

parameters.name: filters[trade_ids]
parameters.description: Array of Trade IDs. Returns item(s) with the specified Trade IDs.

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort item(s) by an attribute. The default sort is ascending. To sort in descending order, prepend the sort value with a hyphen character '-'. Default sort is number ascending.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Controls how much of each Observation is returned. `normal` (the default) returns the documented response body. `ids` returns a bare array of Observation IDs — by far the cheapest option when you only need to know which Observations match a filter. `compact` trims the payload to list-row essentials, `base` is smaller still, `web` and `full` add attachments, drawings, root-cause associations and distribution members, `permissions` populates the `permissions` object, and `safety_hub` returns a minimal set plus `overdue`.

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

id.description: Unique identifier for this Observation Item. Pass as the `{id}` path parameter to `GET /rest/v1.0/observations/items/{id}`, or as `filters[id]` to narrow a list request.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the Observation was created.

closed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the Observation last moved to `closed`. Null if the Observation has never been closed.

deleted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the Observation was sent to the recycle bin. Null for active Observations.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last change to the Observation. Use with `filters[updated_at]` to poll for incremental changes.

number.description: Human-facing identifier of the Observation within its Project. Sortable via `sort=number`, which is also the default sort.

name.description: Short title of the Observation, shown as the row label in the Observations list.

description.description: Plain-text rendering of the Observation description, with HTML markup stripped. Use `description_rich_text` to render formatted content.
description.example: Worker was seen not wearing their hard hat

description_rich_text.description: Sanitized HTML version of the Observation description, safe to render in a rich-text viewer.
description_rich_text.example: Worker was seen not wearing their hard hat

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the Observation. `draft` is only produced for Observations governed by a workflow that has not yet been started. Filter collections with `filters[status]`.

priority.description: Urgency assigned to the Observation. Filter collections with `filters[priority]` and sort with `sort=priority`.

date_notified.description: Date the current assignee was last notified by email. Null while the Observation is unsent — those are the Observations returned by `POST /rest/v1.0/observations/items/send_unsent`.

due_date.description: Date the assignee is expected to resolve the Observation. Defaults from the Project's Observations configuration `days_due_default`.

personal.description: Whether the Observation is private. Private Observations are visible only to their creator, assignees, distribution members, and Observations admins.

origin.title: Observation origin
origin.description: The record this Observation was created from. Null when the Observation was created directly in the Observations tool. `payload` keys vary by `type`.

type.description: Kind of record the Observation originated from.

payload.title: Origin Payload
payload.description: Identifiers for the originating record. Only the keys relevant to `type` are present.

checklist_item_id.description: ID of the source Checklist Item. Present when `type` is `inspection`.

checklist_list_id.description: ID of the source Checklist List. Present when `type` is `inspection`.

coordination_issue_id.description: ID of the source Coordination Issue. Present when `type` is `coordination_issue`.

coordination_issue_number.description: Display number of the source Coordination Issue. Present when `type` is `coordination_issue`.

incident_action_id.description: ID of the source Incident Action. Present when `type` is `incident`.

bim_model_id.description: ID of the source BIM Model. Present when `type` is `bim_model`.

assignee.title: Observation Item Assignee

location.title: Location
location.description: Location the Observation was recorded at. Null when no location is set. Filter collections with `filters[location_id]`.

post.description:
Creates an Observation Item on the specified Project. `observation[name]` and `observation[type_id]` are required; `number`, `personal` and `due_date` default from the Project's Observations configuration when omitted.

Every assignee must be a user the requesting user is permitted to assign, so check `GET /rest/v1.0/observations/assignees` first or the request is rejected with a `403`.
Distribution members must be eligible to view the selected Observation category. A `403` response lists the rejected users as `{id, name}` objects in `ineligible_assignees` and `ineligible_distribution_members`.

An Observation can be linked to an originating record by supplying exactly one of `checklist_item_id`, `coordination_issue_id`, `incident_action_id` or `bim_model_id`.

parameters.description:
Whether or not Configurable validations from the Observation Items Category Configurable Field Set should be run (default: false).
See (https://developers.procore.com/reference/observations#list-observation-category-configurable-field-sets) for a list of Observation Category configurable validations enabled on this project.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Controls which Observation Item fields are returned. `normal` (the default) returns the documented detail payload, including `distribution_members`. `flat_v0` adds `distribution_member_ids`, which always matches `distribution_members`. `safety_hub` returns a minimal payload plus `overdue`.

x-changelog.summary: Assignees and distribution members must be permitted for the Observation category on create
x-changelog.description:
When your company uses advanced Observations permissions, assignees and distribution members must be
permitted for the Observation's category. Users who are not are returned in a `403` response under
`ineligible_assignees` and `ineligible_distribution_members`, each as `{id, name}` objects.

x-changelog.summary: Added asset_ids parameter to Create Observation
x-changelog.description:
Added optional `asset_ids` parameter (array of strings) to Create Observation requests.
When provided, links the specified Assets to the newly created Observation via Related Items.
Requires the Assets field to be visible in the Observations configurable field set.

x-changelog.summary: Add Attachments by Reference
x-changelog.description: Add new attachments by image, drawing revision, file version, form, or direct upload ids.

x-changelog.summary: Accept number parameter when creating an observation item
x-changelog.description: Accept number parameter when creating an observation item

x-changelog.summary: Accept document_management_document_revision_ids parameter when creating an observation item
x-changelog.description:
Accept an array of PDM document references as a parameter when creating an observation item.
The new parameter is also returned on the response.

x-changelog.summary: Recommend upload_ids field for file uploads
x-changelog.description: The `observation.upload_ids` field (available in `application/json` requests) is the recommended approach for file uploads, providing higher performance and reliability. The `attachments` property (available in `multipart/form-data` requests) remains supported for backward compatibility but is not recommended for new implementations.

x-changelog.summary: Granularize can_create_observation permission and add can_create_observation_from_inspection permission
x-changelog.description:
The can_create_observation permission now supports granular permissions. A new can_create_observation_from_inspection
permission allows read-only users to create observations from inspection items when granted.

x-changelog.summary: Enable viewable document generation for attachments uploaded via upload_ids
x-changelog.description:
Fixed an issue where attachments uploaded via the `upload_ids` parameter could not be viewed
in the document viewer. When creating or updating observations with `upload_ids`, the backend
now automatically generates viewable documents and thumbnails for the uploaded files, ensuring
they can be properly displayed in the document viewer.

x-changelog.summary: Support multiple assignees on Create Observation Item
x-changelog.description: The create endpoint now accepts `observation[assignee_ids]` to assign several users to a new Observation Item. Assignee is changing from a single-select to a multi-select: use `assignee_ids` when Assignee is a multi-select, including when assigning one person; use `observation[assignee_id]` when Assignee is a single-select. Sending both is rejected with a `400`. Every submitted user must appear in `GET /observations/assignees` or the request is rejected with a `403`.

x-changelog.summary: Return distribution_member_ids on Observation Item responses
x-changelog.description:
Observation Item responses that use `view=flat_v0` now include
`distribution_member_ids` from the persisted association. Default
`normal` responses continue to return `distribution_members` objects only.

patch.description:
Updates an Observation Item. Only the attributes you send are changed.

Changing `status` appends a Response Log entry and notifies the distribution list; changing the assignee set notifies the users added. Assignees and distribution members must be eligible for the Observation category; a `403` response lists the rejected users as `{id, name}` objects in `ineligible_assignees` and `ineligible_distribution_members`. x-changelog.summary: Assignees and distribution members must be permitted for the Observation category on update
x-changelog.description:
When your company uses advanced Observations permissions, assignees and distribution members must be
permitted for the Observation's category. Changing `type_id` also re-checks the users already on the
Observation. Users who are not permitted are returned in a `403` response under `ineligible_assignees`
and `ineligible_distribution_members`.

x-changelog.summary: Added asset_ids parameter to Update Observation
x-changelog.description:
Added optional `asset_ids` parameter (array of strings) to Update Observation requests.
When provided, replaces the set of Assets linked to the Observation via Related Items.
Pass an empty array to unlink all Assets. Requires the Assets field to be visible in
the Observations configurable field set.

x-changelog.summary: Replace Attachments by Reference
x-changelog.description: Replace existing attachments by image, drawing revision, file version, form, or direct upload ids.

x-changelog.summary: Update Attachments by Reference
x-changelog.description:
Updated the UPDATE request so attachments by image, drawing revision, file version, form, and direct upload ids are additive.
  - Will not replace existing attachments

x-changelog.summary: Accept document_management_document_revision_ids parameter when updating an observation item
x-changelog.description:
Accept an array of PDM document references as a parameter when updating an observation item.
The new parameter is also returned on the response.

x-changelog.summary: Recommend upload_ids field for file uploads
x-changelog.description: The `observation.upload_ids` field (available in `application/json` requests) is the recommended approach for file upload, providing higher performance and reliability. The `attachments` property (available in `multipart/form-data` requests) remains supported for backward compatibility but is not recommended for new implementations.

x-changelog.summary: Enable viewable document generation for attachments uploaded via upload_ids
x-changelog.description:
Fixed an issue where attachments uploaded via the `upload_ids` parameter could not be viewed
in the document viewer. When creating or updating observations with `upload_ids`, the backend
now automatically generates viewable documents and thumbnails for the uploaded files, ensuring
they can be properly displayed in the document viewer.

x-changelog.summary: Support multiple assignees on Update Observation Item
x-changelog.description: The update endpoint now accepts `observation[assignee_ids]` to replace the full set of assignees on an Observation Item; pass an empty array to leave it unassigned. Assignee is changing from a single-select to a multi-select: use `assignee_ids` when Assignee is a multi-select, including when assigning one person. Use `observation[assignee_id]` when Assignee is a single-select: omit it to leave the assignee unchanged, send a User ID to replace the assignee returned in `assignee`, or send `null` to remove it. Sending both is rejected with a `400`.

x-changelog.summary: Return distribution_member_ids on Observation Item responses
x-changelog.description:
Observation Item responses that use `view=flat_v0` now include
`distribution_member_ids` from the persisted association. Default
`normal` responses continue to return `distribution_members` objects only.
