x-changelog.summary: previous_requisition_id is now populated for Simplified Invoicing invoices
x-changelog.description: `previous_requisition_id` was always `null` for invoices whose `contract_invoicing_method` is `simplified`, because Simplified Invoicing does not store an invoice chain. It is now resolved as the non-deleted invoice on the same commitment that immediately precedes this one (`null` for the first invoice on the commitment). The field, its type and its nullability are unchanged; only the value for Simplified Invoicing invoices changes, and the field was never functional for them. Simplified Invoicing is not generally available, so no existing integration is affected. Progressive invoices are unaffected.

patch.description: Update a specified Requisition (Subcontractor Invoice). Users without admin permissions can only update a requisition (sub invoice) if it is the most recent and has a status of 'draft' or 'revise_and_resubmit'. Users with admin permissions can update a requisition (sub invoice) regardless of its status or whether it is the most recent. Requisition items are optional.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Specifies which view (which attributes) of the resource is going to be present in the response. The `header_only` view is intended for split header / line-items rendering on the Subcontractor Invoicing UI: it returns the same shape as `action_policy` plus `tax_summary`, `accounting_method`, and `summary_text`, while skipping `items` and `item_packages`.

allOf.description: Action policy for a Requisition (Subcontractor Invoice). Each key under `controls` is the name of an action (e.g. `update`, `destroy`, `send_to_erp`); each leaf is a `{ allowed: boolean, tooltip: string|null }` pair indicating whether the calling user can perform that action and, if not, why. Action-shaped controls (like `destroy`) nest a single `requisition` key, while field-shaped controls (like `update`) list one key per editable field; field-shaped controls may also nest an `items` object to gate edits on individual line item fields. `remove_billable_change_orders` additionally nests a `change_orders` object keyed by change order id, giving a per-change-order verdict (for example, a change order that was already billed on a previous invoice cannot be removed) alongside the requisition-level verdict.

x-changelog.summary: Added header_only view
x-changelog.description: Added a new `header_only` view value to the `view` query parameter. When specified, the response includes the default header fields plus `action_policy`, `tax_summary`, `accounting_method`, and — for `progressive` contracts only — `summary_text`. The `items` and `item_packages` collections are intentionally omitted. This view is intended for split header / line-items rendering, where the SOV line items are fetched separately.

x-changelog.summary: summary_text is now gated on progressive contracts in the extended view
x-changelog.description: The `summary_text` field is now only included in the response when the contract's invoicing method is `progressive`. This applies to both the `extended` and `header_only` views. Previously, the `extended` view always included `summary_text` regardless of invoicing method. Callers that relied on `summary_text` being present for `simplified` contracts in the `extended` view should update accordingly.

x-changelog.summary: Retainage percent updates now preserve explicit user intent
x-changelog.description: The update endpoint now treats retainage amount and retainage percent as separate inputs on subcontractor invoice line items. When billed work is non-zero, changing the retainage amount derives the retainage percent from retainage amount divided by billed work; for example, billed work `100` and retainage amount `10` results in retainage percent `10%`. When billed work is changed to `0`, retainage amount recalculates to `0` and the existing retainage percent is preserved unless the request explicitly includes a new percent. When billed work is already `0`, an explicit retainage percent edit is still saved, even though the retainage amount remains `0`. This changes the prior zero-billed behavior where a retained amount of `0` could clear the existing retainage percent. Additionally, retainage percent values are now validated to be between `0` and `100` inclusive on zero-billed lines; previously accepted out-of-range values (such as `-5` or `150`) now return `422` instead of being stored silently with a `200`.

x-changelog.summary: Added contract_invoicing_method to the response.
x-changelog.description: Creation of new response field contract_invoicing_method, that will tell if the contract invoicing method is progressive or simplified.

x-changelog.summary: Notice of General Availability
x-changelog.description: This endpoint is now generally available (GA).

x-changelog.summary: previous_requisition_id is now populated for Simplified Invoicing invoices
x-changelog.description: `previous_requisition_id` was always `null` for invoices whose `contract_invoicing_method` is `simplified`, because Simplified Invoicing does not store an invoice chain. It is now resolved as the non-deleted invoice on the same commitment that immediately precedes this one (`null` for the first invoice on the commitment). The field, its type and its nullability are unchanged; only the value for Simplified Invoicing invoices changes, and the field was never functional for them. Simplified Invoicing is not generally available, so no existing integration is affected. Progressive invoices are unaffected.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
This is a **0-based index** representing the page slice of the data you want to retrieve. Each page contains up to **400 items**.
### **📌 Pageable Endpoints** People endpoints that return multiple records **support pagination**. It is recommended to use this feature to prevent network timeouts from excessively large data requests.
### **📌 Response Structure** A successful response will include the following properties:
- **`possible_pages`** *(integer)* → Total number of pages available to retrieve all data. - **`current_page`** *(integer)* → The **0-based index** of the page retrieved. - **`data`** *(array)* → List of records returned for the requested page (up to 400 items per page).
If a **page value exceeds** `possible_pages`, the `data` property will return an **empty array**.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
This is a **0-based index** representing the page slice of the data you want to retrieve. Each page contains up to **400 items**.
### **📌 Pageable Endpoints** People endpoints that return multiple records **support pagination**. It is recommended to use this feature to prevent network timeouts from excessively large data requests.
### **📌 Response Structure** A successful response will include the following properties:
- **`possible_pages`** *(integer)* → Total number of pages available to retrieve all data. - **`current_page`** *(integer)* → The **0-based index** of the page retrieved. - **`data`** *(array)* → List of records returned for the requested page (up to 400 items per page).
If a **page value exceeds** `possible_pages`, the `data` property will return an **empty array**.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
This is a **0-based index** representing the page slice of the data you want to retrieve. Each page contains up to **400 items**.
### **📌 Pageable Endpoints** People endpoints that return multiple records **support pagination**. It is recommended to use this feature to prevent network timeouts from excessively large data requests.
### **📌 Response Structure** A successful response will include the following properties:
- **`possible_pages`** *(integer)* → Total number of pages available to retrieve all data. - **`current_page`** *(integer)* → The **0-based index** of the page retrieved. - **`data`** *(array)* → List of records returned for the requested page (up to 400 items per page).
If a **page value exceeds** `possible_pages`, the `data` property will return an **empty array**.

parameters.name: serializer_view
parameters.description:
Controls the RFI list item response shape. The default response schema shown
for this endpoint documents the standard list item shape; the values below
return alternate shapes used by existing clients.

- `ids_only` - Returns an array of RFI IDs only. Filters and pagination apply
  as usual, but `search`, `q`, and `sort[attribute]` are ignored for this
  view; results are always ordered by RFI ID descending.
- `base_web_index` - Returns compact web index objects containing only the RFI
  ID, full RFI number, and subject.
- `web_index` - Returns web index objects with list display fields, full
  object associations for project stage, cost code, location, sub job,
  responsible contractor, user fields, assignees, ball-in-court users, custom
  fields, requester edit permissions, linked external RFIs, and connected RFI
  origin data.
- `flatten_v0` - Returns flattened mobile-compatible objects with related
  resource IDs instead of several full objects, question and answer data,
  assignees, ball-in-court users, distribution list users, linked external
  RFIs, deletion metadata, and connected RFI origin data.
- Default (not specified) - Returns the standard RFI list item shape shown in
  the response schema.

Unrecognized values are not rejected. Any value outside the list above returns
the default RFI list item shape, so a misspelled view returns a successful
response in the wrong shape.

x-changelog.summary: Fixed responsible_contractor_id filter parameter documentation
x-changelog.description: The `filters[responsible_contractor_id]` parameter documentation has been corrected to show it accepts an array of Responsible Contractor IDs.

x-changelog.summary: Added connect_export_origin to RFI list response
x-changelog.description: The RFI list response now includes a connect_export_origin object on each list item when the RFI was exported via cross-account collaboration. The object contains source_provider_name (the originating company or project name) and rfi_number (the originating RFI number). Returns null for RFIs without a cross-collaboration origin.

x-changelog.summary: Added `reference` field to the `flatten_v0` serializer view
x-changelog.description: The `reference` field is now included in the response when using `serializer_view=flatten_v0`. Previously, this field was only available in the default and extended views. The field is a nullable string  and its value is identical to what is returned by the standard v1.0 API.

x-changelog.summary: Documented RFI list serializer_view response variants
x-changelog.description: The RFI list API documentation now describes the supported `serializer_view` values and the response shape returned by each view, including `ids_only`, `base_web_index`, `web_index`, and `flatten_v0`.

x-changelog.summary: Documented additional RFI list filters, sort attributes, and search alias
x-changelog.description: The RFI list API documentation now describes filters that the endpoint has always accepted but did not document: `current_revision`, `sub_job_id`, `priority`, `overdue`, `linked_to_external_rfis`, `linked_to_connected_rfis`, `for_location_id_with_sublocations`, and `initiated_at`. Existing ID filters are now documented as accepting a single value or an array, `filters[status]` documents the `closed_with_revision` and `closed_draft` values, and `filters[number]` is corrected to a string because it matches the full RFI number rather than a numeric ID. `sort[attribute]` documents the `ball_in_court_id`, `priority`, and `status` values, and the `q` search alias and `as_datetimes` parameters are now listed.

x-changelog.summary: Documented linked external RFI status, sync, and connection values
x-changelog.description: The linked external RFI objects returned by the `web_index` and `flatten_v0` RFI list views now document their allowed values. `status` includes the existing `_recycled` variants returned when the upstream RFI is in the recycle bin, `sync_status` documents `in_sync` and `upstream_private`, and `connection_status` documents `connected` and `disconnected`. Integrations should tolerate unknown future values.

x-changelog.summary: Corrected documented RFI response status values
x-changelog.description: The standard and extended RFI response schemas now document the existing `closed_with_revision` and `closed_draft` status values and no longer list `recycled`, which is not returned as an RFI status. Generated clients should handle the newly documented values and tolerate unknown future status values.

x-changelog.summary: Added connect_exported_project_ids to the flatten_v0 RFI list view
x-changelog.description: RFI list responses requested with `serializer_view=flatten_v0` now include `connect_exported_project_ids`, listing the connected projects this RFI has already been exported to. The list is empty when cross-account collaboration is unavailable to the caller.

x-changelog.summary: Return the RFI creator vendor separately from the creator name
x-changelog.description: Mobile index and extended RFI responses now return the creator's company as `created_by.vendor` with `id` and `name`. The `created_by.name` field now contains only the creator's name.

Table configuration for the export that controls which columns are visible and their order in the generated PDF or CSV.

When provided, the export will respect both the column visibility settings and the column order from the frontend table configuration.

The object contains source_provider_name (the originating company or project name) and rfi_number (the originating RFI number). Returns null when the RFI has no cross-collaboration origin.

x-changelog.summary: Added origin_rfi_url to linked external/connected RFIs on the RFI detail response
x-changelog.description: Linked external (cross-collaboration) RFIs returned on a local RFI's detail payload now include an `origin_rfi_url` field. It contains a zone-aware MFE deep-link back to the original RFI in the upstream (GC) project, or `null` when the upstream connection cannot be resolved (e.g. unsupported zone).

parameters.description:
Table configuration for the export that controls which columns are visible and their order in the generated PDF or CSV.

When provided, the export will respect both the column visibility settings and the column order from the frontend table configuration.
Columns marked as `hidden: true` will be excluded from the export, and visible columns will appear in the same order 
as specified in the columnState array.

If this parameter is not provided, the export will use default column visibility and order based on configurable field sets.

hidden.description: Whether the column should be hidden in the export

get.description:
Returns the Saved Views a Project user can see: their own plus every project-level Saved View. Unusable Saved Views are never returned.

By default only Saved Views belonging to a Document Collection are returned. Passing `filters[upload_collection_ids]` or `filters[recycle_bin_collection_ids]` scopes the response to Saved Views on those collections instead. A Saved View belongs to at most one collection, so at most one of `document_collection_id`, `upload_collection_id` and `recycle_bin_collection_id` is non-null.

Recycle Bin Saved Views are only returned when the Recycle Bin is enabled for the Project; when it is not, scoping to them returns an empty page rather than an error.

Supported filters: `ids`, `updated_at`, `document_collection_ids`, `upload_collection_ids`, `recycle_bin_collection_ids`.

Pass `view=ids_only` to receive an array of Saved View ids instead of full objects.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Optional response view. Omit or pass `default` for full Saved View objects. `ids_only` returns an array of ids and raises the `per_page` ceiling from 100 to 5000. The published `per_page` maximum reflects the default view.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Language for the response to be translated into

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
Object with whitelisted Field ids as keys and their corresponding MetadataValue id, MetadataValue ids array, or primitive string value as values.
Valid filterable fields are:
ids,
updated_at,
document_collection_ids,

recycle_bin_collection_ids

get.description:
Returns metadata about this Project's Schedule, including information about the Schedule integration configuration for the current project.

#### Schedule Types

| Type                                                 | Key                           |
|------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| File-based schedule integration via web browser      | "Microsoft Project"           |
| File-based schedule integration via Procore Drive    | "Microsoft Project 2010"      |
| File-based schedule integration via Procore Documents| "Microsoft Project Documents" |
| Primavera P6 database integration via Procore Drive  | "Primavera P6"                |

Note that the schedule types listed as "Microsoft Project", "Microsoft Project 2010", and "Microsoft Project Documents" are functionally identical.
In all cases Procore can consume any supported schedule file type and extract data from it, not just Microsoft Project.
Schedule files can be uploaded either via Procore Drive, via the Procore Documents tool, or via the Procore Schedule tool,
regardless of which of these three types is selected. Where Primavera P6 database integration via Procore Drive is in use, the `p6_id`
attribute returned by this API indicates which P6 project Procore Drive is extracting data from.

schedule_activity_feed.description: Whether the schedule activity feed is available to the current user.

schedule_task_comments.description: Whether task comments are available to the current user.

schedule_task_details.description: Whether task details are available to the current user.

schedule_linked_items.description: Whether linked items are available to the current user.

put.description: Upload a schedule file to import.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Optional. Locale for the import report (e.g. en, fr-FR, ja-JP). Determines the language of validation errors and warnings in the generated report. Must be the same locale used when fetching logs via the logs endpoint.

file.description: Schedule file to import. Supported formats: .mpp, .ppx, .xer.

202.description: Import accepted; poll status_url for progress

status.description: Current status

finished_at.description: When the import job finished in UTC (ISO 8601)

errors.description: Present when status is failed (with optional detailed_log_url if logs exist), or when status is completed with warnings (warning message + detailed_log_url). Omitted on success with no logs.

detailed_log_url.description: URL to fetch detailed log. Omitted when there are no logs (e.g. failed with no logs).

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

409.description: A conflicting operation is already in progress for this schedule

422.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.

DEPRECATED:
This endpoint is a duplicate of the `PUT` endpoint. It will be removed in a future version of the API. Use the `PUT` method instead.

Upload a schedule file.

#### Supported File Formats

| Type | Source                                                        |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| MPP  | Microsoft Project                                             |
| MPX  | Microsoft Project, SureTrak                                   |
| XER  | Primavera P6, Primavera Contractor                            |
| PP   | Asta Powerproject, Asta Easyplan                              |
| XML  | Formatted for Microsoft Project, e.g. Smartsheet, OpenProject |
| XML  | Primavera PMXML                                               |
| PPX  | Phoenix Project Manager                                       |
| FTS  | FastTrack Schedule                                            |
| POD  | ProjectLibre                                                  |
| GAN  | GanttProject                                                  |
| PEP  | TurboProject                                                  |
| PRX  | Primavera P3                                                  |
| STX  | Primavera SureTrak                                            |
| CDPX | ConceptDraw PROJECT                                           |
| CDPZ | ConceptDraw PROJECT                                           |
| SP   | Synchro Scheduler                                             |
| SEDF | USACE Standard Data Exchange Format                           |
| ZIP  | Compressed file containing one of the supported file types    |

get.description:
Return information about the schedule integration configuration for the current project.

#### Schedule Types

| Type                                                 | Key                           |
|------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| File-based schedule integration via web browser      | "Microsoft Project"           |
| File-based schedule integration via Procore Drive    | "Microsoft Project 2010"      |
| File-based schedule integration via Procore Documents| "Microsoft Project Documents" |
| Primavera P6 database integration via Procore Drive  | "Primavera P6"                |

Note that the schedule types listed as "Microsoft Project", "Microsoft Project 2010", and "Microsoft Project Documents" are functionally identical.
In all cases Procore can consume any supported schedule file type and extract data from it, not just Microsoft Project.
Schedule files can be upoaded either via Procore Drive, via the Procore Documents tool, or via the Procore Schedule tool,
regardless of which of these three types is selected. Where Primavera P6 database integration via Procore Drive is in use, the `p6_id`
attribute returned by this API indicates which P6 project Procore Drive is extracting data from.

This endpoint has been deprecated. Instead, use [/rest/v1/project/{project_id}/schedule)

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

get.description: All Segments for a given company

parameters.name: include[]
parameters.description: Optional sideloads to include in each segment object. Valid values: 'tier_depth' (adds the tier_depth integer field), 'action_policy' (adds the action_policy object with permitted actions for the current user). Multiple values may be passed as include[]=tier_depth&include[]=action_policy.

parameters.name: include_action_policy
parameters.description: Convenience flag equivalent to passing include[]=action_policy. When true, each segment includes an action_policy object describing permitted actions for the current user.

items.description: A work breakdown structure segment

id.description: Unique integer identifier for this WBS Segment. Use as the {id} path parameter in GET/PATCH/DELETE /rest/v1.0/companies/{company_id}/work_breakdown_structure/segments/{id}.

type.description: The segment type. One of: 'sub_job' (sub-job dimension), 'cost_code' (cost code dimension), 'line_item_type' (line item type dimension), 'custom' (user-defined custom segment), 'attribute' (attribute dimension). Only 'custom' segments can be created via the API.

name.description: Localized display name of this WBS Segment shown in the UI (e.g. "Cost Code", "Phase"). Corresponds to the i18n label, not the internal segment_type value.

position.description: Ordinal position of this segment within the company WBS pattern. Lower values appear first. Use to determine column order in budget code displays.

segment_items_count.description: Total number of segment items belonging to this segment. Use to gauge  whether a segment has been populated before attempting to list segment items.

required.description: Whether this segment must have a value assigned when creating a WBS Code. When true, budget codes cannot be created without selecting an item from this segment.

delimiter.description: Character that separates this segment's value from the next segment's value in a formatted WBS code string (e.g. '.' produces "01.02").

project_can_modify_origin_project.description: Whether project-specific segment items can be added, edited, or removed from a project. When true, project admins may manage items in this segment independently of the company list.

project_can_delete_origin_company.description: Whether segment items inherited from the company level can be deleted from a project. When true, project admins may remove company-defined items from the project's visible list.

structure.description: Hierarchy structure of this segment. 'tiered' means items can have parent-child relationships forming a multi-level tree; 'flat' means all items are at a single level with no hierarchy.

tier_depth.description: Present only when include[]=tier_depth is requested (list endpoints only).  Flat segments (sub_job, line_item_type) return 1; tiered segments return  the number of levels. Omitted (not null) when not requested.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this segment was created. Use to sort or filter segments by creation date.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this segment was last modified. Use to detect whether cached segment data needs to be refreshed.

wbs_pattern_id.description: ID of the WBS Pattern this segment belongs to. Use to correlate this segment with its parent pattern returned by GET /rest/v1.0/companies/{company_id}/work_breakdown_structure/patterns.

reason.description: A human-readable code providing additional detail on the cause of the error.

patch.summary: Updates a line item of a shipment.
patch.description:
This method applies partial updates to a line item within a shipment. The request body should
            specify only the fields  to be updated. If the operation is successful, the updated line item details are
            returned. Set `void` to true to void a line on a Final shipment. Optional `notes` are stored on
            the line when voiding and ignored for non-void updates. After a successful void, `previous_quantity`
            contains the shipped quantity from before the line was zeroed. Voiding requires admin access and
            the materials_management_void-enabled feature flag.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the shipment containing the line item to be updated. Must not be an empty GUID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the line item to be updated. Must not be an empty GUID.

requestBody.description: The patch request containing the updated values for the line item. Must not be null.

quantity.description: The quantity to update for the shipment line. Specify null to leave the quantity unchanged.

date.description:
The date and time to update for the shipment line. Specify null to leave the date and time
            unchanged.

void.description: When true, voids the shipment line by setting its shipped quantity to zero.

notes.description: Optional notes stored on the line when voiding. Ignored for non-void updates.

put.description:
Updates a specification section revision. The request body must include `specification_section`
and `specification_section_revision` objects (see schema).

**HTTP methods:** Both `PUT` and `PATCH` are supported with the same request body.

**Success:** Returns `200 OK` with the updated revision.

**Validation errors:** Returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` when attribute validation fails
(for example duplicate number and description, invalid division or specification set, or invalid
revision). The response uses `error.code` `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`, a summary `error.message`,
and `error.details` with `reason_code` `VALIDATION_ERROR` and a `failures` object whose keys are
API field names and whose values are arrays of validation message strings.

**Not found:** Returns `404 Not Found` when the specification section revision id does not exist
for the project—not for validation failures on the payload.

x-changelog.description:
`PUT` and `PATCH` `/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/specification_section_revisions/{id}` now return
**422 Unprocessable Entity** when validation fails (for example duplicate number/description, invalid division or
specification set, or invalid revision fields). The response body uses `error.code` **UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY**, a
summary `error.message`, and a non-empty `error.details` array whose first item has `reason_code` **VALIDATION_ERROR**

`specification_section_division_id`, `specification_set_id`, `issued_date`, `received_date`, `revision`, `obsolete`).

**Breaking change:** Clients that treated **404 NOT_FOUND** with a concatenated `error.message` and empty `details`
as validation errors must instead handle **422** and read per-field messages from `details[0].failures`.
**404** is only returned when the revision id does not exist for the project.

x-changelog.summary: Add opt-in redirect support to revision download (v2.1)
x-changelog.description:
`GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/specification_section_revisions/{id}/download`
now accepts an optional boolean query param `redirect`.

When `redirect=true` (truthy) and the revision is downloadable, the endpoint responds
with a `302` redirect to the file URL instead of returning the URL in the JSON body.
When `redirect` is omitted or not truthy, the existing JSON response
(`{ data: { message, download_url } }`) is unchanged.

The download is still logged and the analytics event still fires in both modes, and the
existing error responses (`404` / `400`) are unchanged.

patch.summary: Bulk update for Specification Sets for a Project
patch.description:
Applies create, update, and delete operations for specification sets in a single request.
Include any of `creation_params`, `updation_params`, and `deletion_params` as needed.

Successful operations run in one database transaction. Valid rows are persisted even when other
rows in the same request fail validation.

When one or more rows fail validation, the response is **400 Bad Request** with
`error.details[0].reason_code` set to `VALIDATION_FAILED` and a `failures` object grouping errors
under `creation_failures`, `updation_failures`, and `deletion_failures` (see the `400` response schema).

creation_params.description: New sets to create. Use `key` to correlate validation errors in the response.

key.description: Client-supplied id for matching entries in `error.details[0].failures.creation_failures`.

position.description: Ordering position of the set within the project.

updation_params.description: Existing sets to update; failures are keyed by set `id` in the error payload.

name.description: Updated name of the specification set.

position.description: Updated ordering position of the set within the project.

schema.description: Specification Sets collection Response

deletable.description: True if set does not have any related revisions or uploads

400.description: Bad Request — one or more create/update operations failed validation. Inspect `error.details[0].failures` for per-entity field messages (`*_error` keys).

schema.title: Specification Sets Bulk Validation Error
schema.description: Returned when PATCH bulk update fails model validation. Structure matches other specifications bulk endpoints (for example specification section divisions): grouped failures by operation with `VALIDATION_FAILED` in `details[0].reason_code`.

code.description: HTTP status equivalent in screaming snake case.

message.example: One or more validation errors occurred

details.description: Contains one object describing validation failures when `reason_code` is `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

message.example: One or more validation errors occurred
message.description: Localized message for this detail entry.

creation_failures.description: Map of client `key` from `creation_params` (stringified) to field errors. If `key` is omitted, the server uses the zero-based index of the item in `creation_params` as a string key.

additionalProperties.description: Keys are attribute names with an `_error` suffix (for example `name_error`, `position_error`, `date_error`).
Localized validation message for that field.

updation_failures.description: Map of specification set id (string) to field-level validation errors.

deletion_failures.description: Reserved for deletion validation; typically an empty object.

get.description:
Return a list of all Submittals from a specified Project.
See [Filtering on List Actions](https://developers.procore.com/documentation/filtering-on-list-actions) for information on using the filtering capabilities provided by this endpoint.
See [Downloading attachments with markup](https://developers.procore.com/reference/rest/document-markup#show-or-create-document-markup-downloadable-pdf).

parameters.name: filters[id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified IDs.

parameters.name: filters[ball_in_court_id]
parameters.description: User ID. Return item(s) where the specified User ID is the Ball in Court.

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[responsible_contractor_id]
parameters.description: Array of Responsible Contractor IDs. A single Responsible Contractor ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[attachments]
parameters.description: Array of boolean values to filter submittals by "Attachments" status.

parameters.name: filters[specification_section_id]
parameters.description: Array of Specification Section IDs. A single Specification Section ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[approver_id]
parameters.description: Array of User IDs. Return item(s) where the specified User IDs are in the approver list. A single integer is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[cost_code_id]
parameters.description: Array of Cost Code IDs. A single Cost Code ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[current_revision]
parameters.description: Default false. If true, only current revisions are shown. If false, all submittals are shown, regardless of whether or not it is the current revision.

parameters.name: filters[division]
parameters.description: Array of Divisions to filter on. A Division is the first two digits from the Specification Section Number. A single Division is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[location_id]
parameters.description: Array of Location IDs. A single Location ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[submittal_manager_id]
parameters.description: Array of Submittal Manager IDs. A single Submittal Manager ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[number]
parameters.description: Array of Numbers. A single Number is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[submittal_package_id]
parameters.description: Array of Submittal Package IDs. Returns item(s) associated with the specified Submittal Package IDs. A single integer value is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[response_id]
parameters.description: Array of Response IDs. A single Response ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[required_on_site_date]
parameters.description: Array of dates (date range). Returns item(s) with their required on site date withing the specified dates. A single date is also accepted. style: form

parameters.name: filters[status_id]
parameters.description: Array of Status IDs. A single Status ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[type]
parameters.description: Array of Submittal Types. A single Submittal Type is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[task_id]
parameters.description: Array of Submittal Task IDs. Returns item(s) associated with the specified Submittal Task IDs. A single integer value is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[revision]
parameters.description: Array of Submittal Revision values. A single Submittal Revision is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[specification_area_id]
parameters.description: Array of specification area IDs to filter submittals by. A single value is also accepted. Use "NULL" to filter submittals with no specification area.

items.description: Specification area ID

parameters.name: filters[unpackaged]
parameters.description: Parseable to boolean value, filters out unpackaged Submittals.

parameters.name: filters[workflow_progress]
parameters.description: Array of strings to filter submittals by "Workflow Progress" status. Available options: on_track, off_track, overdue, paused, none

items.description: Workflow progress status value

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[anticipated_delivery_date]
parameters.description: Array of dates (date range). Returns item(s) with their anticipated delivery date within the specified dates. A single date is also accepted. style: form

x-changelog.description: The `filters[status_id]` parameter now uses different status IDs than before. Status IDs are unique per company. To get the correct status IDs for your company, use the GET /rest/v1.0/companies/{company_id}/submittal_statuses endpoint.

x-changelog.summary: Fixed responsible_contractor_id filter parameter documentation
x-changelog.description: The `filters[responsible_contractor_id]` parameter documentation has been corrected to show it accepts an array of Responsible Contractor IDs.

x-changelog.summary: Add closed_at to Submittals list response
x-changelog.description: Adds `closed_at` (timestamp when the submittal was closed) to the Submittals list response body.

parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

parameters.name: filters[id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified IDs.

parameters.name: filters[ball_in_court_id]
parameters.description: User ID. Return item(s) where the specified User ID is the Ball in Court.

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[responsible_contractor_id]
parameters.description: Array of Responsible Contractor IDs. A single Responsible Contractor ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[specification_section_id]
parameters.description: Array of Specification Section IDs. A single Specification Section ID is also accepted.

Return a list of all Submittals from a specified Project.
See [Filtering on List Actions](https://developers.procore.com/documentation/filtering-on-list-actions) for information on using the filtering capabilities provided by this endpoint.
See [Downloading attachments with markup](https://developers.procore.com/reference/rest/document-markup#show-or-create-document-markup-downloadable-pdf) for information on downloading attachments with markup as a PDF.

parameters.description: User ID. Return item(s) where the specified User ID is the Ball in Court.

parameters.name: filters[ball_in_court_company_id]
parameters.description: Company ID. Return item(s) where the specified Company ID is the Ball in Court.

parameters.name: filters[closed_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) that are due within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[created_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) created within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[responsible_contractor_id]
parameters.description: Return item(s) with the specified Responsible Contractor ID.

parameters.name: filters[specification_section_id]
parameters.description: Array of Specification Section IDs. A single Specification Section ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[approver_id]
parameters.description: Array of User IDs. Return item(s) where the specified User IDs are in the approver list. A single integer is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[current_revision]
parameters.description: Default false. If true, only current revisions are shown. If false, all submittals are shown, regardless of whether or not it is the current revision.

parameters.name: filters[division]
parameters.description: Array of Divisions to filter on. A Division is the first two digits from the Specification Section Number. A single Division is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[location_id]
parameters.description: Array of Location IDs. A single Location ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[submittal_manager_id]
parameters.description: Array of Submittal Manager IDs. A single Submittal Manager ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[submittal_package_id]
parameters.description: Array of Submittal Package IDs. Returns item(s) associated with the specified Submittal Package IDs. A single integer value is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[response_id]
parameters.description: Array of Response IDs. A single Response ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[sent_date]
parameters.description: Array of dates (date range). Returns item(s) where an approver's sent date falls within the specified dates. A single date is also accepted. Use "NULL" to filter for submittals with no sent date. style: form

parameters.name: filters[workflow_step]
parameters.description: Array of workflow step numbers. Returns submittal(s) currently on one of the given steps. A single step number is also accepted. Use "NULL" to filter for submittals with no workflow step.

parameters.name: filters[status_id]
parameters.description: Array of Status IDs. A single Status ID is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[type]
parameters.description: Array of Submittal Types. A single Submittal Type is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[updated_at]
parameters.description:
Return item(s) last updated within the specified ISO 8601 datetime range.
Formats:
`YYYY-MM-DD`...`YYYY-MM-DD` - Date
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` - DateTime with UTC Offset
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00`...`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+XX:00` - Datetime with Custom Offset

parameters.name: filters[unpackaged]
parameters.description: Parseable to boolean value, filters out unpackaged Submittals.

parameters.name: filters[number]
parameters.description: Array of Numbers. A single Number is also accepted.

parameters.name: filters[has_operation_errors]
parameters.description: Parseable to boolean value, filters Submittals based on whether they have operation errors from bulk operations.

parameters.name: filters[operation_errors_by_operation_id]
parameters.description: Filters Submittals that have operation errors associated with specific operation ID(s). Accepts single or multiple operation IDs.

parameters.name: show_attachments
parameters.description: Determine the AttachmentVisible tag value(depend on configurable field set).

parameters.name: minimal_submittal_package
parameters.description: When `true`, each submittal's `submittal_package` in the response includes only `id`, `number`, `title`, and `created_by` for smaller payloads and faster responses. Omit or set to `false` for the full package object.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Dynamic configured custom-field filters. Use a `custom_field_{definition_id}` key, for example `filters[custom_field_123]=true` or `filters[custom_field_456][]=789`. Values may be strings or arrays of strings. Use `NULL` to match submittals without a value where supported.

actual_delivery_date.description:
The Actual Delivery Date of the Submittal
*This field can only be set if the project has submittal delivery information enabled

bic_due_date.description: The Ball-in-Court Due Date of the Submittal. For DSP projects, this comes from the submittal plan. For non-DSP projects with workflows, this is calculated from current step approvers.

confirmed_delivery_date.description:
The Confirmed Delivery Date of the Submittal
*This field can only be set if the project has submittal delivery information enabled

closed_at.description: Timestamp when the submittal was closed.

The ID of the Cost Code of the Submittal
*This field can only be set by admins

current_step_approvers.description: List of approvers for the current workflow step. For completed workflows, this shows approvers from the final step. Empty for submittals without workflows.

response_required.description: Whether a response is required from this approver

user.description: The user information for the approver

current_step_returned_date.description: The latest returned date from current step approvers who have answered. For completed workflows, this shows the date from the final step.

current_step_sent_date.description: The earliest sent date to current step approvers. For completed workflows, this shows the date from the final step.

custom_textarea_1.description: *This field can only be set by admins

custom_textfield_1.description: *This field can only be set by admins

design_team_review_time.description:

*This field can only be set if the project has schedule calculations enabled

distribution_member_ids.description: The IDs of the Distribution Members of the Submittal

due_date.description:
The Due Date of the Submittal
*This field is not available to be set if sequential approvers is enabled

has_responded_approver.description: Whether the Submittal has at least one approver that has responded, i.e. at least one approver has a returned date set.

internal_review_time.description:

*This field can only be set if the project has schedule calculations enabled

issue_date.description:

*This field can only be set by admins

lead_time.description:

location_id.description: The Location of the Submittal

private.description: Whether the Submittal is Private or not

received_from_id.description: The Received From of the Submittal

required_on_site_date.description:

responsible_contractor_id.description: The Responsible Contractor of the Submittal

scheduled_task_key.description:

*This field can only be set if the project has submittal delivery information enabled and the user has permissions to view the calendar tool

specification_section_id.description: The ID of the Specification Section of the Submittal

submit_by.description:

*This field can only be set by admins

*This field can only be set by admins

submittal_package_id.description:

x-changelog.summary: Add email_sent_at to submittal approvers in the V2 submittals list
x-changelog.description: Returns email_sent_at on each submittal approver, the datetime when the notification email was dispatched to the approver, expressed in the project's timezone. Null for historical records or when no email was sent; sent_date may be present while email_sent_at is null when the approver was sent the submittal without an email notification.

x-changelog.summary: Return the stored status category on the V2 submittals list
x-changelog.description: status.status on each submittal in the list is the stored category (Open, Closed, or Draft) again. status.name remains the localized label. The company submittal log statuses endpoint still localizes its status field.

x-changelog.summary: Add updated_at to the V2 submittals list
x-changelog.description: Returns updated_at, the timestamp when the submittal was last updated, on each submittal in the list.

x-changelog.summary: Added non-final-due-date inline permissions to the List Submittals endpoint
x-changelog.description: Adds per-row `permissions.can_update_required_on_site_date`, `permissions.can_update_actual_delivery_date`, `permissions.can_update_confirmed_delivery_date`, and `permissions.can_update_lead_time`, matching the shape already used by `permissions.can_update_submit_by`. All four are false for for-record-only submittals under Dynamic Submittal Plan, since only Final Due Date exists on such a submittal.

x-changelog.summary: Derive workflow_approval_status_key rejected from the latest completed response
x-changelog.description: `workflow_approval_status_key` now returns `rejected` when the latest completed workflow response is rejected, revise and resubmit, or void, including when the reject-workflow project setting is off. Completed Void / Revise and Resubmit workflows no longer serialize as `approved`.

x-changelog.summary: Added buffer time display permission to V2 submittals list
x-changelog.description: Adds `permissions.can_view_buffer_time_and_variance` to the V2 submittals list response so clients can gate buffer time and variance from backend-owned item permissions.

x-changelog.summary: Add custom field filtering to the submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Adds support for filtering the submittals list with dynamic `filters[custom_field_{definition_id}]` parameters. Supported configured custom fields include booleans, numbers, datetimes, references, and multi-value references. Filters also support "NULL" where applicable.

x-changelog.summary: Add workflow approval status fields to the V2 submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Added `workflow_approval_status_key` (rejected, approved, pending, or not_started) and `response_considered` (the response category of the latest completed workflow response, null when no approver has responded) to the submittals list api.

x-changelog.summary: Add due_date_days and workflow_step_days_late sort options to submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Add two new sort options to the submittals list API. `due_date_days` sorts by the signed number of days between the submittal's due date and today (overdue submittals sort as negative, upcoming ones as positive), grouping non-closed submittals first, then closed, then those without a due date. `workflow_step_days_late` sorts by how many days the current workflow step is past due, placing submittals that are not late at the bottom. Prefix the sort value with a minus for descending order (e.g. sort=-due_date_days).

x-changelog.summary: Add workflow_step filter to submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Add a workflow_step filter to the submittals list API to narrow submittals to the workflow step they are currently on. Accepts an array of step numbers (a single step number is also accepted) and "NULL" to filter for submittals with no workflow step.

x-changelog.summary: Added row action permissions to List Submittals endpoint
x-changelog.description: Adds per-row `permissions.can_edit` to support backend-owned edit action visibility in list clients.

x-changelog.summary: Added inline edit permissions to List Submittals endpoint
x-changelog.description: Adds per-row `permissions` flags for inline-editable list fields.

x-changelog.summary: Introduce GET Submittals Endpoint
x-changelog.description: Return a list of all Submittals from a specified Project.

x-changelog.summary: Added workflow step information fields to Submittals listing
x-changelog.description: Added new fields to display current workflow step information: `workflow_step` (with current step, total steps, and optional days late), `current_step_approvers` (approvers for current step only), `current_step_sent_date`, `current_step_returned_date`, and unified `bic_due_date` for both DSP and non-DSP projects. Enhanced approver objects with `response_required` and `user` fields.

x-changelog.summary: Add anticipated_delivery_date date filter and sort to submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Add anticipated delivery date filter and sort to submittals list API. This filter and sort feature is currently in beta and may not function as expected in all cases.

x-changelog.summary: Submittal status IDs are changed to be unique per company
x-changelog.description: The `filters[status_id]` parameter now uses different status IDs than before. Status IDs are unique per company. To get the correct status IDs for your company, use the GET /rest/v1.0/companies/{company_id}/submittal_statuses endpoint.

x-changelog.summary: Add closed_at to Submittals v2 list response
x-changelog.description: Adds `closed_at` (timestamp when the submittal was closed) to the Submittals v2 list response body.

x-changelog.summary: V2 List Submittals no longer includes is_rejected, updated_at, open_date, attachments, and related fields
x-changelog.description:
The following attributes have been removed from the List Submittals response (GET /rest/v2.0/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/submittals) to improve performance. This is a breaking change for consumers that rely on these fields in the list response. Use the Show Submittal endpoint (GET .../submittals/{id}) for full details including these attributes.
Removed attributes: `is_rejected`, `rejected_submittal_log_approver_id`, `source_submittal_log_id`, `updated_at`, `open_date`, `attachments` (array). The `attachments_count` attribute is unchanged and remains in the list response.

x-changelog.summary: Add schedule_v2_activity_id and sent_date filters to submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Add filters to submittals list API: schedule_v2_activity_id (filter by linked Schedule V2 activities via Related Items) and sent_date (filter by approver sent date).

x-changelog.summary: Add six new sort options to submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Add sort capability for submittal_manager (by manager name), attachments_count, planned_return_date, planned_internal_review_completed_date, planned_submit_by_date, and sent_date (by approver sent date). Prefix sort value with minus for descending (e.g. sort=-submittal_manager).

x-changelog.summary: Add minimal_submittal_package query parameter to List Submittals v2
x-changelog.description: The List Submittals endpoint accepts an optional query parameter `minimal_submittal_package`. When set to `true`, each submittal's `submittal_package` in the response includes only `id`, `number`, `title`, and `created_by`, reducing payload size for list views. Omit the parameter or set it to `false` for the full `submittal_package` object.

x-changelog.summary: Add has_workflow to v2 list response; approvers opt-out via drop_approvers
x-changelog.description: Adds a `has_workflow` boolean to the v2 Submittals list response, true when the submittal has any approvers. Clients that pass `drop_approvers=true` opt in to a slimmer payload where the `approvers` array is omitted (subject to server-side enablement). Clients that do not pass the parameter continue to receive `approvers` unchanged. Full approver details remain available on the Show endpoint (GET /companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/submittals/{id}).

x-changelog.summary: Reintroduce is reject field on the V2 submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Added the is rejected field to the submittals list api

x-changelog.summary: Introduce associated attachments count on the V2 submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Added a new associated attachments count field to the submittals list api that returns both the count of  attachments on the submittal as well as any attachments added by an approver.

x-changelog.summary: Add associated attachments filter on the V2 submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Added a new associated attachments count field to the submittals list api that filters on both the count of  attachments on the submittal as well as any attachments added by an approver.

x-changelog.summary: Added estimated workflow completion date to the Submittal response
x-changelog.description: Added an estimated_workflow_completion_date field to the submittal plan data in the Submittal response — the projected date the submittal's workflow completes. It surfaces on the submittal show, list, and bulk-shared-review responses.

x-changelog.summary: Add custom field sorting to submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Bring custom fields to parity with standard fields when sorting the submittals list. Sorting by a custom field orders submittals by that field's value and consistently places submittals with no value at the bottom of the list.

x-changelog.summary: Add has_responded_approver to the V2 submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Added a new `has_responded_approver` boolean field to the submittals list api. It is true when the submittal has at least one approver with a returned date, indicating an approver has responded.

x-changelog.summary: Add null_aware_location_id_with_sublocations filter to submittals list API
x-changelog.description: Add a `null_aware_location_id_with_sublocations` filter to the submittals list API. Accepts an array of location ids and expands each to include all of its sublocations. Unlike `location_id_with_sublocations`, it also accepts "NULL" to filter for submittals with no location.

x-changelog.summary: Add Due Date Days field to the submittals List API
x-changelog.description: Added a new field that calculates the difference between the due date and the today's date , this field already existed for DSP Projects now it is rendered for the default view as well.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

Formats:

parameters.description: Returns Tasks with a row_number matching the given value. get.description:
Return a list of all Tax Codes for a given Company

When tax suport is enabled in Procore you can associate line items
with a specific Tax Code. The Tax Code (sometimes known as a Tax Group)
determines the tax rate to be applied to the line item for each Tax Type
defined in Procore (Note that presently Procore only supports a single
Tax Type per company).

You may define as many Tax Codes as required. Through the web interface, a
Procore admin user may identify one of these tax codes as the default
value to be shown when creating new line items.

x-changelog.summary: Add `is_group` and `component_unique_ids` fields to Bulk Create Tax Codes endpoint
x-changelog.description:
Add support for creating tax group codes via the bulk create endpoint.
- `is_group` — Boolean flag to designate the tax code as a group. Requires the
  financials.tax.enable_tax_groups feature flag to be active.
- `component_unique_ids` — Array of ERP origin IDs identifying the component tax codes
  that make up the group. Each ID is resolved to a Procore tax code via the external_data
  table or, for codes created in the same request, via the unique_id of a sibling item.
  Required when is_group is true; invalid on non-group items.

x-changelog.summary: Make tax group rate optional on Bulk Create Tax Codes
x-changelog.description:
For tax groups (`is_group: true`), `rate` is no longer required.
When omitted, the group rate is set to the sum of its component rates
(same-request component rates preferred over existing rates). When
provided, it must equal that sum or the item is rejected.
Non-group codes still require a rate.

patch.description: Bulk Update Tax Codes for a given company

code.description: Tax Code Name

archived.description: Tax Code Archived

rate.description:
Tax code rate. Optional for tax groups: when omitted on a composition
update or conversion, the group rate is set to the sum of its component
rates. When provided, it must equal that sum or the item is rejected.
A component rate change without the parent group in the request updates
the parent group rate to the new component sum.

invoice_tax_application.description:
Tax Code Invoice Tax Application. Must be NET or GROSS for plain codes
and NONE for group tax codes. GROSS and NONE are accepted only when the
company is on the new tax experience. When omitted on a rate write, defaults
to NET for plain codes and NONE for groups. Legacy companies must omit this
field or send NET.

effective_start_date.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime when this new rate becomes effective (e.g. '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'). Omit to apply the rate immediately. When set, the current rate stays in effect until this datetime. Requires the `financials.tax.support_rate_schedule` feature flag to be enabled. Not valid for group tax codes — future rates cannot be created directly on groups.

is_group.description:
When true on a plain code, converts it to a group. Must be accompanied by
component_tax_code_ids. Requires the tax groups feature flag to be enabled.
Omit or set to false for regular code updates.

component_tax_code_ids.description:
Procore tax code IDs of the component tax codes that make up this group.
On an existing group, providing this field updates the composition (expires
the current version and creates a new one). Rate is optional; when omitted
the group rate is derived as the sum of the new component rates.
When sent for a non-group without is_group: true, silently ignored.

x-changelog.description: Add Company Bulk Update Tax Codes endpoint to update multiple tax codes.

x-changelog.summary: Add `is_group` and `component_tax_code_ids` fields to Bulk Update Tax Codes endpoint
x-changelog.description:
Add support for tax group operations via the bulk update endpoint.
- `is_group` — When true on a plain code, converts it to a group (requires
  component_tax_code_ids and the financials.tax.enable_tax_groups feature flag).
- `component_tax_code_ids` — Array of Procore tax code IDs specifying the group's
  components. On an existing group, updates the composition (expires the current
  version and creates a new one); requires rate to be provided alongside.
  When sent for a non-group without is_group: true, silently ignored (keep-as-code).
Non-group items (component rate updates) are processed before group items in the
same request to ensure component rates are committed before composition validation.

x-changelog.summary: Add `rate.effective_start_date` field to Bulk Update Tax Codes endpoint
x-changelog.description:
Add optional `rate.effective_start_date` (ISO 8601 datetime) on the Bulk Update Tax Codes
request body to schedule a future rate. Omit the field to apply the new rate immediately.
Requires the financials.tax.support_rate_schedule feature flag to be active.
Not valid for group tax codes — future rates cannot be created directly on groups.
Timeline placement, locking, and duplicate-rate idempotency match the tax rates create path.

x-changelog.summary: Derive tax group rates and cascade component rate changes on Bulk Update Tax Codes
x-changelog.description:
For tax groups, `rate` is no longer required when converting a code to a
group or when updating `component_tax_code_ids`. When omitted, the group
rate is set to the sum of its component rates. When provided, it must
equal that sum or the item is rejected.
Updating a component's rate no longer fails the item with
`component_rate_update_invalidates_group`. The parent group's rate is
updated to the new component sum, including when the parent group is not
in the request.       Non-group items are still processed before group items
in the same request.

get.description:
Return a list of all Tax Types for a given Company

A Tax Type represents a "value added tax" or "goods and services tax"
which needs to be accounted for on a commitment or an invoice generated
by Procore. In many places there will just be a single tax to deal with,
for example in Australia it will be GST, in the UK it will be VAT.
Other countries may require that multiple taxes are displayed,
for example in Canada an invoice may be required to include both GST and PST.

Procore currently only supports the definition of one tax type per company.

Tax support can be enabled at the company level by an admin user though the
web interface. Once enabled at the company level, tax support can also be
enabled or disabled at the project level. When tax support is enabled at
the company level, it is disabled for existing projects, but by default
will be enabled for new projects. An admin user can change these settings
through the web interface.

post.description: Posts telematics diagnostics for a piece of Procore equipment. Identify the equipment with resource_id, or with oem_id and oem_name when the equipment is already linked to a telematics provider. Use the canonical keys, names, and units as per example. Diagnostics with other keys are also accepted and stored, and are returned by the telematics read endpoints. Diagnostics with an empty value are ignored. Integrations that already produce ISO 15143-3 (AEMP 2.0) payloads should use the AEMP endpoints instead.

requestBody.description: Telematics diagnostics for a single piece of equipment. The example lists every canonical diagnostic, plus one provider-specific diagnostic to show that other keys are accepted.

properties.value: 625 Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, Pontiac, MI, 48342

resource_id.description: Unique identifier assigned to the equipment in Procore. When omitted, oem_id and oem_name must match equipment that is already linked to a telematics provider.

resource_type.description: Resource type against which you want to send data (equipment/labour/material) in Procore. Default value is equipment

oem_name.description: Telematics provider or equipment OEM name. Required with oem_id when resource_id is omitted.

oem_id.description: Provider equipment identifier, such as a VIN or serial number. When resource_id is omitted, requires oem_name and equipment that is already linked to a telematics provider.

pin.description: OEM ISO Number, can be same as oem_id as per AEMP 2.0 standard.

properties.description: Additional location properties. Use the key Address for a formatted address.

value.example: 625 Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, Pontiac, MI, 48342

key.description: Canonical, case-sensitive diagnostic key returned by the telematics field-definition endpoint. Other keys are also accepted and stored.

name.description: Canonical diagnostic display name returned by the telematics field-definition endpoint.

value.description: Diagnostic value represented as a string

unit.description: Unit of measure returned for this diagnostic by the telematics field-definition endpoint. Units are not validated, so send the unit listed for the key you are posting.

value.example: 625 Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, Pontiac, MI, 48342

properties.value: 625 Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, Pontiac, MI, 48342

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

422.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.

OEMName.description: OEM or telematics provider name, used with EquipmentID or SerialNumber to match this machine to its Procore equipment record

EquipmentID.description: Provider equipment identifier. SerialNumber is used when EquipmentID is absent.

SerialNumber.description: Equipment serial number used as the provider identifier when EquipmentID is absent

201.description: Equipment records, telematics provider links, and AEMP telematics data saved

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

422.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.

Python3
x-code-samples.content:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

payload = "{\"project_id\":513526,\"timecard_entry\":{\"date\":\"2018-10-14\",\"description\":\"Description\",\"billable\":true,\"hours\":\"8.0\",\"lunch_time\":\"60\",\"time_in\":\"2018-10-14T07:00:00Z\",\"time_out\":\"2018-10-14T16:00:00Z\",\"timecard_time_type_id\":1,\"timesheet_id\":41823,\"cost_code_id\":12345,\"sub_job_id\":3483483,\"location_id\":161072,\"procore_signature_id\":1121,\"party_id\":2341,\"crew_id\":1022,\"clock_in\":4567,\"clock_out\":1267,\"approval_status\":\"approved\",\"origin_id\":23423,\"origin_data\":\"{'example':'related data'}\",\"line_item_type_id\":13}}"

headers = { 'content-type': "application/json" }

conn.request("POST", "/rest/v1.0/companies/%7Bcompany_id%7D/timecard_entries", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

x-code-samples.content:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

payload = "{\"timecard_entry\":{\"date\":\"2020-10-14\",\"description\":\"This is a description.\",\"billable\":true,\"hours\":\"8.0\",\"lunch_time\":\"60\",\"party_id\":2342,\"time_in\":\"2018-10-14T07:00:00Z\",\"time_out\":\"2018-10-14T16:00:00Z\",\"timecard_time_type_id\":1,\"timesheet_id\":41823,\"cost_code_id\":12345,\"sub_job_id\":3483483,\"location_id\":161072,\"login_information_id\":2341,\"origin_id\":23423,\"origin_data\":\"{'example':'related data'}\",\"line_item_type_id\":13,\"daily_log_segment_id\":123456}}"

headers = { 'content-type': "application/json" }

conn.request("POST", "/rest/v1.0/projects/%7Bproject_id%7D/timecard_entries?serializer_view=SOME_STRING_VALUE", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))
